#1997. Mason Mount offering Michael Carrick a midfield solution which could have legs

It is not uncommon to hear football club executives talking about the importance of the “money being on the pitch”.

In other words, managers having their best players fit and available most if not all of the time. Quality at the top level is essential but so is robustness. They go hand in hand.

Unfortunately for Manchester United, the money has not been on the pitch down the years nearly as much as the club would want or expect.

Bruno Fernandes stands out for what he does with the ball primarily, but also because he plays almost every minute of every game and, while his sheer indefatigability is extreme, United know they need more of his ilk.

This is why the forthcoming season is such a big one for Mason Mount. His quality has seldom been in doubt. The problem is he has rarely been on the pitch long or consistently enough to show it.

Indeed, the one-time England midfielder has started just 25 Premier League matches since his £60m move from Chelsea three years ago and that perennial unavailability is one of the reasons doubts were being cast about his Old Trafford future going into this summer.

Yet Michael Carrick was keen to keep Mount, United have rebuffed inquiries around him and intriguingly the 27-year-old could yet have an impact on what the club do during the remaining six weeks of the transfer window.

For the second time in the space of six days, Mount was deployed in a deeper midfield role alongside new £48m, signing Andrey Santos for Friday’s resounding 5-0 victory over Norwegian side Rosenborg in Trondheim, just as he had done against Wrexham last weekend.

Mount has spent the majority of his career playing further forward, either off the right or as a No. 10 but Carrick likes him in a fluid No. 8 role, a position Erik ten Hag had identified for the player only for persistent injuries to detonate those plans.

The logic is simple: Mount is mobile, can cover the ground, is adept under pressure, has line breaking passing, vision and a nose for goal. He is also a good presence in the dressing room and a leader in his own way. Watch him imparting advice to Shea Lacey as they walked back to the centre circle after the youngster’s goal opened the scoring against Rosenborg and you get a glimpse of that.

The question, of course, is whether he can stay fit long enough to impose those qualities that help to explain why Liverpool and Arsenal had also been so keen to sign him back in 2023 and Carrick’s predecessor Ruben Amorim was also such a fan.

With United’s summer budget only stretching so far, Carrick was always going to have to think on his feet in certain areas of the pitch.

What will be interesting to see over the coming weeks is whether the manager feels Mount is robust enough to complement Santos, fellow summer signing Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo.

MASON MOUNT SCORES FOR MAN UNITED!He takes the ball with a quality turn, and curls it into the corner of the goal 🤩📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/M9ErA2HKbo

Much of the chatter among United fans at present centres on who the third midfield signing will be after Santos and Tielemans.

Given Mount’s injury record, it would be a significant risk not to recruit again in that department in the hope he could stay fit over a full season. Four options in two positions behind the No 10 of Fernandes sounds fine in principle but what happens if Mount’s season was to follow a similar trajectory to the previous three?

If United are going to strengthen in other areas, there will need to be compromises or alternative solutions that help to free up cash along the way but gambling in midfield may not be the best way to go.

With Champions League football to factor in this season, it is still hard to believe United will not seek to strengthen again in midfield but the club seem ready to take their time on that front. And all the while an assortment of names continue to fly around.

After spending £85m on Santos and Tielemans, a massive outlay on a third midfielder at this stage would be a bit of a surprise.

Could that negate a move for Real Madrid’s Aurelien Tchouameni? Alex Scott is greatly admired by United but Bournemouth are determined to keep him and have put a prohibitive pricetag on him.

AS Roma’s Manu Kone is not thought to have universal backing internally. Tyler Adams’ name has been floated again but the Bournemouth and US midfielder’s injury record counts against him.

There has not yet been evidence of a serious appetite to go for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba, whom they considered signing last summer. Sander Berge at Fulham and Borussia Dortmund’s Felix Nmecha are among a number of other midfielders who have been linked with United.

Another midfield signing could well emerge but United are keeping their cards close to their chest. Whatever materialises, though, it will still not change the fact this is a huge season for Mount.

⚽️ Shea Lacey⚽️ Jacob Devaney⚽️ Harry Amass⚽️ Ethan Williams Four #MUAcademy prospects were on the scoresheet in Trondheim 🧬💙 pic.twitter.com/fguQ36ANTM

“It was a good day. Clean sheet, scoring goals and everyone coming through injury-free hopefully is everything you want. Keeping the players fit and improving through pre-season is amongst the most important things. You want to build through the pre-season and you have to manage to players differently. It is never going to be perfect but we scored some great goals and we are moving forward nicely.

“I thought we defended well as a team for the most part. A clean sheet is a beautiful thing. I think we are in a good place with four weeks to go until the start, gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup. As it stands right now, we are in a pretty good place.”

This is what the official start of the season will look like for Michael Carrick’s side:

August 22- Hull vs Manchester UnitedAugust 30- Manchester United vs IpswichSeptember 6- Everton vs Manchester UnitedSeptember 13- Manchester United vs Manchester CitySeptember 20- Fulham vs Manchester United

They face two of the three promoted sides on the first two weekends and there is a very early Manchester derby.

August 1- Manchester United vs Atlético Madrid August 8- PSG vs Manchester United August 12- Manchester United vs Leeds August 15- AC Milan vs Manchester United

Having played Wrexham and Rosenborg in their first two games, the level of competition will rise significantly for Manchester United in the coming weeks.

There is the final whistle and Manchester United have cruised to a 5-0 win over Rosenborg in Norway. Goals from Lacey, Zirkzee, Devaney, Amass and Williams have seen Michael Carrick’s men ease to victory. A pretty one-sided game.

The first yellow card of the game is given very late on as Devaney is booked for a high boot.

A late change for Rosenborg as Hald-Hernes replaces Borgersen.

The visitors have dominated this game and they now have their fifth goal. It is created by great work from Kamason on the right side of the box before he squares it to Williams, who has the easiest of tap-ins at the far post.

Other than a few short periods in this game, Rosenborg have looked poor. They may be midway through their league season but you can see why they are down in 10th in the Norwegian top flight with just four wins from their opening 13 league games.

You would expect that Michael Carrick will be very keen to see his side keep a clean sheet.

Manchester United have their fourth of the evening. Kamason is found making an overlapping run on the right side of the box and his cross fired towards the back post is tapped in by Amass. That was a goal assisted by one full-back and scored by the other.

Good work from Soboczynski results in Rosenborg winning a corner out on the left. They take it short before a shot is hit from the edge of the box straight down the throat of Vitek.

Rosenborg hit the post. Manchester United should probably have been given a free-kick in the build-up as Soboczynski appeared to push Devaney over but play goes on. The ball comes to E Ceide at the far post but his effort strikes the outside of the post.

Just a few minutes after making a raft of changes, Manchester United have their third goal of the evening. Rosenborg fail to clear a corner from the right and the ball falls to Devaney on the six-yard box. He takes one touch before firing into the top of the net.

Bearing in mind Rosenborg are in the middle of their league season, this has been an encouraging showing so far from United. Joshua Zirkzee has been lively. He’s still more likely to leave than stay at Old Trafford this summer but performances like this won’t hamper his value. He set up Shea Lacey for his goal with a good pass after again dropping deep into space and he’s taken that goal to give United a 2-0 lead quite brilliantly. Patrick Dorgu has been a threat and Mason Mount has dovetailed well in central midfield with new signing Andrey Santos.

Both sides are going to make a raft of changes on the hour mark, with the rest of the Manchester United starting XI being changed other than Vitek in goal.

Santos brings down Borgersen not far outside the Manchester United penalty area to give Rosenborg a decent opportunity. It is a pretty decent effort from E Ceide that goes just wide of Vitek’s right post.

The visitors have not been great since the break but they have their second and it is a great solo goal from Zirkzee. Lacey, out on the left touchline, squares it for Zirkzee, who takes the ball towards the Rosenborg penalty area. He fakes a shot, which takes numerous Rosenborg defenders out of the equation as they slide past. He then sits down the Rosenborg keeper before slotting into an empty net. A fine goal from Zirkzee.

Soboczynski has his second chance since coming on at the break after good work from E Ceide down the left but the former’s effort goes wide.

That is a really poor decision from the linesman. Duris was played in behind the Manchester United defence and thought he was through for a one-on-one chance but the offside flag goes up. However, replays prove that Duris was clearly being played onside by Amass, who has looked shaky since coming on at the break.

Zirkzee receives a pass from Dorgu on the D and takes one touch before shooting. His effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner, which Wahlstedt slightly unconvincingly punches away.

That is a very good chance for Rosenborg to equalise early in this second half. Amass and Heaven makes a mess of things deep in their own half, presenting Rosenborg with a good opportunity inside the Manchester United penalty area. Two Rosenborg substitutes combine as Soboczynski squares it for Borgersen but the latter makes a mess of it and shoots well wide from 10 yards out.

Michael Carrick has decided to make just a few changes at the break with Amass and Kamason coming on. Shaw and Maguire have gone off, which has seen Yoro move inside from right-back to centre-back.

Our first goalscorer of pre-season = Shea Lacey! 💎 pic.twitter.com/AyFOWNh5Fi

With no delays, the first half is brought to an end and Manchester United take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Lacey’s goal. Expect a raft of chnages at the break.

As this half has worn on, Manchester United’s dominance has only increased.

Mbeumo appeared to be racing through one-on-one but Mortensen just about gets back to outmuscle Mbeumo and allow the ball to go back to his keeper. There were a few appeals for a foul by Mortensen but that challenge was just about fine.

Other than those early stages, Manchester United have dominated the rest of this first half and are pressing for a second. For the second time in the half, they strike the frame of the goal. Mbeumo clips in a cross from the right into the Rosenborg penalty area and it picks out the head of Yoro. However, from eight yards out, the Frenchman’s header comes back off the bar.

Moments after they hit the frame of the goal, Michael Carrick’s side take the lead. Zirkzee picks up the ball inside his own half and, from the halfway line, feeds a pass into the on-running Lacey. Dorgu wants Lacey to play the ball across to him at the back post but the latter opts against it. Instead, just inside the Rosenborg penalty area, he cuts onto his preferred left foot and curls one into the far corner. A good finish from Lacey.

Just as I was saying that both sides were lacking a cutting edge in the final third, Manchester United are inches away from taking the lead as they strike the post. Santos feeds a delicate pass into the path of Dorgu on the left side of the box. Dorgu strikes his effort powerfully but it comes off the outside of the far post.

Both sides have lacked a cutting edge when they get into the opposition final third, hence why there has not been a plethora of good chances.

Mbeumo beats his man down Manchester United’s right and cuts it back to Mount on the edge of the Rosenborg penalty area. Mount hits it first time but his shot is blocked and spins behind for a corner. It is Manchester United’s first of the game but it is headed away.

That was nearly the moment for Rosenborg to take the lead. Pereira’s cross from the left-hand side of the box takes a deflection and nearly ends up at the feet of Chiakha at the back post but it is just out of his reach.

Rosenborg looked the sharper in the early exchanges but Manchester United are growing into the game and starting to gain more control.

Manchester United create their first opening of the game. Rosenborg poorly five the ball away deep inside their half and immediately Zirkzee plays it into the path of Mbeumo, whose shot from the right side of the box is saved by Rosenborg keeper Wahlstedt, who initially spilt the shot but gathered at the second attempt.

Mount trips Sahsah just outside the Manchester United penalty area, which will give Rosenborg a good shot to take an early lead. Rosenborg look a little sharper unsurprisingly in these early stages.

The Rosenborg captain Selnaes takes but hits it straight into the wall.

With Rosenborg in the midst of their season and Manchester United just in their second pre-season game, you would expect the hosts to have more rhythm and flow in their game.

Manchester United to appear to be lining up with a back four, with Yoro starting at right-back rather than his more customary centre-back position.

We are under way in Norway. Rosenborg are playing in white, with Manchester United in blue.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, with Harry Maguire leading Manchester United out, and we are getting closer to kick-off in Norway.

Bring on United! 🫡Watch Rosenborg v United LIVE on MUTV, with build-up starting at 16:00 BST 📲

Manchester United’s preparations for the new season continue in Norway as they take on Rosenborg in their second pre-season game. These sides did meet in a pre-season friendly two years ago in July 2024, with Rosenborg winning that encounter 1-0.

Manchester United kicked off their pre-season against Wrexham nearly a week ago, which they lost 1-0 in Helsinki. Michael Carrick opted to deploy two different XIs for each half, meaning 22 players got a run-out. Manchester United kick off their Premier League campaign at newly promoted Hull City on August 22.

They have added two midfielders to their ranks over the last few weeks, both from the Premier League. Brazilian Andrey Santos has joined from Chelsea whilst Belgium’s Youri Tielemans has arrived from Aston Villa. Santos made his first Manchester United appearance in the loss to Wrexham whilst Tielemans is yet to feature having made the knockout stages with Belgium at the World Cup. A number of players are still yet to return from World Cup duty, including the likes of Lisandro Martinez, Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo, although Rashford still faces an uncertain future.

Former Leeds goalkeeper Karl Darlow has also arrived but he is currently recovering from a minor procedure. Benjamin Sesko is still trying to shake off a shin injury whilst Matthijs de Ligt is not yet available due to a back injury which plagued for most of last season. Manuel Ugarte faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines having picked up a serious injury whilst playing for Uruguay at the World Cup. After this game, the level of competition for Manchester United for the rest of pre-season ramps up a number of notches, with the likes of Atlético Madrid and back-to-back European champions PSG to come over the next couple of weeks as Carrick’s men prepare for a season in which they return to the Champions League.

Rosenborg are in the midst of their league campaign in Norway and are experiencing a tricky campaign. They are currently 10th in the Norwegian top flight, having won just four of their 13 league games thus far, but their form has picked up of late as they have won three of their last five games. They won their last match 3-0 against Start six days ago.

#1995. Manchester United vs. Roma - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 01 Nov 2026 22:34, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 15:36

Struggling Manchester United head into Tuesday’s Champions League matchday four encounter against 15th-placed Roma at Old Trafford winless in nine consecutive matches.

The 21st-placed Red Devils’ last victory in any competition came against European debutants Sabah almost two months ago, highlighting the uphill challenge facing a beleaguered Michael Carrick ahead of what could be his final match in charge if they suffer another defeat.

For 45 minutes at Stamford Bridge, United suggested that they could end their extended scoring drought, with the Red Devils creating enough chances to have led Chelsea before the break.

Amad Diallo failed to convert two promising opportunities, and while their first-half performance offered encouragement, there was a sense that Xabi Alonso’s men would not produce another underwhelming 45 minutes.

Indeed, so it proved, as Morgan Rogers scored a solo goal, admittedly aided by United’s seemingly lax defending, before Lisandro Martinez self-destructed by collecting two yellow cards within 90 seconds, conceding a penalty with the second offence.

Cole Palmer converted from 12 yards to all but put the game beyond the Red Devils’ reach, leaving them winless in nine consecutive matches, with defeats in their last three and four of the previous five.

Carrick received the dreaded vote of confidence less than a week ago after the 3-0 hammering by Bournemouth, but United, now 17th in the Premier League table and outside the relegation zone on goal difference, cannot keep losing indefinitely; something has to give.

Gian Piero Gasperini’s men will be in no mood to do the beleaguered hosts any favours, as the in-form Italian outfit aim to extend the Manchester club’s winless run.

The Giallorossi have reason to believe that their current form can inflict further misery on the Premier League strugglers, given their five-match unbeaten streak, which includes four victories.

Particularly striking is Roma’s free-scoring form, with the Serie A club netting three or more goals in four of those five unbeaten matches, although their defensive frailties remain a concern ahead of facing United’s admittedly underwhelming attack.

Gasperini’s men enter matchday four having conceded three in a six-goal thriller against Napoli, two in a 4-2 victory over out-of-form Cagliari and another two in Saturday’s 5-2 hammering of relegation-threatened Udinese.

Roma have suffered several chastening defeats against United, including a 7-1 hammering in 2007 and a 6-2 beatdown in 2021, but the Giallorossi will back themselves to finally win at Old Trafford and increase the pressure on Carrick.

Manchester United form (all competitions):

Martinez may be suspended domestically, but the centre-back - despite doubts about his commitment - should partner Harry Maguire, with Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot on either side of the central defenders.

Bruno Fernandes’s role on Tuesday night will be intriguing, as Carrick could deploy Youri Tielemans in an advanced central position and move the Portuguese playmaker out wide, with Andrey Santos and Kobbie Mainoo potentially forming the midfield base.

That would likely leave Mason Mount as the third attacking midfielder behind Bryan Mbeumo, with Matheus Cunha limited to a role off the bench.

Missing out, though, are Patrick Dorgu, Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko, while Marcus Rashford and Amad will be assessed.

Gasperini has no fresh injury concerns following Saturday’s 5-2 win over Udinese, although Muhammed Bah, Paulo Dybala, Manu Kone, Lorenzo Pellegrini and Mile Svilar remain sidelined for the midweek clash.

Donyell Malen sits second in the Capocannoniere race with eight goals, one behind Gustavo Varela, and the forward will hope to add to his three Champions League strikes.

With Malen also registering two assists, level with Matias Soule, the Dutchman is undoubtedly the away side’s leading threat, particularly in the absence of Dybala and Pellegrini.

Manchester United possible starting lineup:

Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Mazraoui; Mainoo, Santos; Fernandes, Tielemans, Mount; Mbeumo

Gollini; N'Dicka, Mancini, Hermoso; Molina, De Roon, Pisilli, Wesley; Cristante, Soule; Malen

United’s encouraging first half against Chelsea offered little consolation after another defeat, while their nine-match winless run makes it difficult to trust Carrick’s men against free-scoring opponents.

Roma’s defensive frailties may offer the hosts a route to goal, but Malen and company have our backing to inflict further misery on the beleaguered Red Devils.

#1994. WATCH: Nico Raskin turns interviewer after Rangers teammate's Scotland joy

James Penrice was welcomed into the Scotland fold with a cheeky message from Rangers team-mate Nico Raskin after earning his first senior international call-up.

The 27-year-old left-back has been selected by Sébastien Pocognoli for this month’s Nations League double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 A first @ScotlandNT call-up for James Penrice! 💙 James joins teammates Findlay Curtis and Liam Kelly in the squad for the upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures. 🎙️ Fresh off the training pitch, @RangersTV and Nico Raskin caught up with James following the news. https://t.co/jMukr0qH2n

— Rangers Football Club (@RangersFC) November 3, 2026

Raskin was first to interview his team-mate after the news broke, joking: “Well done James, what do you want me to ask? What is the question? How do you feel to be called up, brother?”

Penrice replied: “Incredibly proud. Buzzing for my family as well.”

Raskin then joked about Belgian boss Pocognoli’s decision to select the Rangers defender. He said: “Well-deserved. I always knew Belgian managers have good eyes to see players!”

Speaking to Rangers TV afterwards, Penrice revealed he had only discovered he was in the squad minutes before heading out for training. He said: “Five minutes before I came out.

“Kev zoomed round in the cart and came right up to me and just went… and I went, ‘Oh my God, unreal!’”

Rangers youth prospect reveals personal ‘privilege’ of working with boyhood hero

Russell Martin ‘spoken highly of’ at Manchester United before Rangers stint

Pedro Caixinha back in Europe after joining 13th club of managerial career

Penrice admitted an international call-up was something he could scarcely have imagined earlier in his career. He added: “I’ve waited a wee while, but I knew coming back to Scotland, coming to Rangers, it would help my cause.

“It’s credit to the boys in there as well. They’ve helped me incredibly, and I’m just buzzing.

“It’s a weird feeling because I didn’t ever think going through the early part of the career, I would ever be called up. But it’s happened now, so I’m just delighted.

“It’s an incredibly proud moment for me and my family.”

#1992. Home struggles jeopardising unbeaten run: All the key stats ahead of Milan vs. Inter

AC Milan will be looking to extend their unbeaten run against Inter this evening, but recent home struggles could make things difficult for them.

After what was a poor display against Bologna, Milan really need to bounce back with a good performance and a win against Inter tonight. Gerry Cardinale said as much last night, stressing that he will be ‘crushed’ if they don’t make the most of this opportunity.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, while the record in the derby has been good lately with seven games unbeaten, the Rossoneri have struggled at home. They have lost four of their last eight league games at San Siro, while conceding six goals in the last two home games.

In short, while some stats and facts speak in their favour, the Rossoneri cannot be certain of a win tonight.

➤ AC Milan have won three of their last four Serie A matches against Inter (D1), as many as they had in their previous 16 meetings (D4 L9). The Rossoneri have won their last two matches and have not won three consecutive matches against the Nerazzurri since a run of four under Carlo Ancelotti between 2002 and 2004.

➤ Inter have won more matches (70) and scored more goals (260) against Milan than any other team in Serie A history. However, the Nerazzurri have also conceded 236 goals against the Rossoneri, fewer than those conceded against Roma (237) and Juventus (270); with 496 goals in total, the Milan derby could become the third match in the competition’s history to reach the 500-goal mark, after Inter-Roma (544) and Inter-Fiorentina (502).

➤ Milan have collected 18 points from their first nine games of this Serie A season, the same amount they achieved at the same point last season; in five of their previous six seasons in the top flight, the Rossoneri have collected at least 21 points after the first 10 games, with the sole exception of 2024/25 (17).

➤ AC Milan have lost four of their last eight home games in Serie A (W3 D1), as many as they had suffered in their previous 29 (W15 D10); furthermore, the Rossoneri have conceded six goals in their last two home games, one more than they had conceded in their previous five.

➤ Inter have scored in each of their last 19 Serie A matches, the longest unbroken streak among teams currently in the top flight; their last game without a goal came against AC Milan on March 8, 2026.

➤ Since the start of last season, Inter have scored at least two goals in 16 away league matches; only Bayern Munich (18) have done better in the top five European leagues, with Barcelona sharing the same figure as the Nerazzurri.

➤ Inter and Milan are the only two teams in Serie A this season to already have two players with at least four goals scored: Marcus Thuram and Lautaro Martínez for the Nerazzurri, and Adrien Rabiot and Alphadjo Cisse for the Rossoneri.

➤ Hakan Çalhanoglu played 135 Serie A matches for AC Milan between 2017 and 2021, scoring 22 goals and providing 31 assists. The Nerazzurri midfielder hasn’t been involved in a single goal in his last four matches for the Rossoneri in the tournament, after having been involved in four goals in his first five (two goals, both penalties, and two assists).

➤ After his brace on the last matchday, Alphadjo Cisse reached four goals in Serie A at 20 years and 6 days; if he were to score his fifth goal at 20 years and 9 days, he would become the seventh-youngest player in AC Milan’s history to do so, and the third in the three-point-for-a-win era, after Alexandre Pato and Stephan El Shaarawy.

➤ Francesco Pio Esposito, at 21 years and 125 days, could become Inter’s youngest Italian goalscorer in a Serie A derby since the three-point-for-a-win era; among Nerazzurri players of any nationality, only Obafemi Martins and Ronaldo have scored in a league derby at an earlier age during this period.

#1989. Guimaraes will not force Newcastle exit like Isak, says Howe

Eddie Howe is confident Bruno Guimarães will not demand to leave Newcastle United for Arsenal and echo Alexander Isak’s acrimonious departure to Liverpool last summer.

Howe admitted he could not guarantee that Guimarães will still be at the club in September but gave a strong defence of his captain’s character and insisted the Brazil international will return for pre-season training next week as planned.

Given the huge gap between Newcastle’s valuation of Guimarães and what Arsenal have indicated they would be willing to pay for the 28-year-old, there is a belief on Tyneside that the only way the captain would join the London club is if he behaved as badly as Isak did 12 months ago.

Newcastle value Guimarães at £100m, while Arsenal, through intermediaries, have only indicated they would be willing to pay about £60m including bonuses.

Isak did not travel on the club’s pre-season tour to Asia and then went on strike, refusing to train or play, until Newcastle agreed to sell him to Liverpool for a British record £128m on deadline day.

Asked if he feared a repeat of that with Guimarães this time around, Howe replied: “I’ve spoken to him as I would do with Bruno normally. He is a fantastic person and we have had some really good conversations both before, during and after the World Cup. What we speak about obviously has to remain private but he is a great player and a great person.

“Look, I don’t know what is going to happen with Bruno. That is up to other people to speculate about but also other people to have conversations about which I’m not a part of. I don’t think it is fair to compare situations and what happened previously. You’ve got to look at this in its own right.

“Bruno is captain of our football club. He has been an unbelievable player and person all the time we have worked together. I speak on behalf of everyone at the football club when I say we absolutely love him and of course everyone wants him to stay.

“The plan is for him to come back on July 31, he gets an extended break because of the World Cup and is currently enjoying a holiday with his family... There is nothing to say that Bruno won’t be back training with us.”

"We've had some really good conversations" 🗣️Eddie Howe speaks on Newcastle's transfer window so far and speculation around Bruno Guimarães ⚫️⚪️ pic.twitter.com/zB1W31Fne0

Arsenal’s interest in Guimarães is well known but there has been little progress since they began their pursuit more than a month ago.

Whether Arsenal can come up with an offer that tempts Newcastle into negotiations remains to be seen but it is thought the Premier League champions will try to harden up their interest before Guimarães returns for pre-season training.

Newcastle United were held to a 1-1 draw by Gateshead in their second pre-season friendly of the summer. A 79th-minute own-goal saved the Premier League club’s blushes but what did we learn from the match?

Steur did not grab many headlines when he arrived from Ajax for £20m earlier this month because of Sandro Tonali’s move to Tottenham Hotspur. But those familiar with Dutch football would have been excited that Newcastle had signed him.

The 18-year-old has impressed with his performances in training and gave a glimpse of his significant potential in his first public display. He is young and sources have told Telegraph Sport that he must develop physically before he is ready to play every week in the Premier League – but you can already see he has a very high ceiling.

As you would expect from a player described as Ajax’s best midfield prospect for a generation, he is assured on the ball. He is also a progressive passer, always looking to break the lines to get his team moving forward. Eddie Howe will love him.

Whisper it, but there were shades of Bruno Guimarães in his style of play, in the way he took the ball under pressure, in tight spaces, and played on the turn. Patience will be needed but the signs are really encouraging.

Guimarães’s future is all supporters have wanted to speak about for weeks. I was at a wedding on Friday and it felt like everyone asked me about it at some point – including the bride and groom immediately after completing their first dance.

It has already become a summer-long transfer saga that has not progressed since Arsenal’s interest was revealed last month. Telegraph Sport has repeatedly checked whether there have been any fresh developments over the past week and the answer from senior Newcastle sources has remained consistent: there are no talks ongoing and nothing has accelerated, despite claims Arsenal were preparing an official £70m bid.

However, Newcastle need clarity from their captain. He is due back for pre-season next week and is expected to fly to Spain for their training camp on July 31. He has intimated he would like to move to Arsenal but unless Newcastle receive a bid that matches their asking price, he and his representatives have been told he will not be allowed to leave.

Schär has been a brilliant player for Newcastle, but at the age of 34 and coming off the back of a serious ankle injury, he looked understandably rusty against Gateshead.

This will be the former Switzerland international’s ninth season at St James’ Park and he was at fault for giving away a soft free-kick that led to Gateshead scoring first.

Schar accepted a contract extension earlier this summer on reduced terms and although Howe values his quality and experience, he is going to be a back-up centre-back this season.

Neave, 19, started the game as Newcastle’s centre-forward as Will Osula was missing and Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa were given additional time off after playing in the World Cup for Germany and DR Congo respectively.

But those players will return to training next week and, although Neave forced a good save in the first half, he is not ready to start in the Premier League. There is little point keeping him around as a fourth-choice striker when he needs to be playing regularly at this stage of his career.

A loan move is on the cards and he could be a really smart signing for a Championship club or a team competing at the top of League One. The most important thing is that he gets regular senior games rather than hangs around at Newcastle on the fringes of the first-team squad.

Eddie Howe has said "he does not know" what will happen with Bruno but pretty strong defence of his character and denied similarities with Isak. Said they have spoken regularly throughout the summer and he will be back for pre season training on July 31st #nufc

Eddie Howe’s side will head down to Ashton Gate before jetting off to La Manga for a training camp on July 31, which will feature many of those who played in the World Cup, including Bruno Guimarães who has been linked with a move to Arsenal.

In Spain, Newcastle will face Valencia at the Mestalla, before returning to the UK to play Everton at Murrayfield. They will then host Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg at St James’ Park for their final tune-up matches before the Premier League season starts.

This is their pre-season schedule in full:

The referee brings this contest to a close and it finishes a goal apiece at Gateshead International Stadium. Not the result Howe was hoping for, but he can at least find some comfort in a positive showing from new signing Steur in the heart of midfield.

Newcastle ended up with 76 per cent of the ball and created three ‘big chances’ but lacked the cutting edge in the final third to make that dominance tell. Credit must go to Gateshead who defended resolutely and took their best chance of the match.

Important pre-season minutes 👊 pic.twitter.com/FpzYVdbc0C

The hosts have near enough seven bodies in their back line and Newcastle are struggling to find a way through.

Bone picks Pivas’ pocket on the edge of the box but the Serbian defender does well to recover and Jaouen gets a rare touch on the ball as he clears his lines.

Newcastle have five minutes, plus added time, to grab a go-ahead goal. Plenty of industry on show from the youngsters who have come on, but the play has largely been restricted to a midfield slug-fest in the last minutes.

Triple substitution from Howe. Hall, Ramsey and Willock make way for Salia, Munda and Charlton.

Gateshead 1 Newcastle 1 (OG) Hall’s cross from the left in turned by Williams. Newcastle had been turning the screw as Gateshead dropped deeper and deeper.

The stadium announcer tells us that there are 7,195 people at this afternoon’s match.

Sanusi and Park replace Murphy and Barnes.

There is the first yellow card of the match. Home lands an overzealous challenge on Willock in the centre of the pitch and receives a booking for his troubles.

Ferreira is then played into the left channel and unleashes a shot which is turned behind for a corner by Desbois, who has been awesome this afternoon.

Jaouen, Miley and Ferreira replace Pope, Shahar and Neave.

Gateshead are sitting deeper meaning that their penalty area is often getting quite congested.

There are opportunities for the hosts to counter, though, and Boatswain has the chance to play in Telford but severely overhits the through-ball.

A note on Steur... He’s completed 65 of his 68 attempted passes so far. That’s 96 per cent. Impressive stuff.

Hall falls on to the ball under pressure on the byline. The referee awards a free-kick to Gateshead and Hall protests his case. Just not happening for the left-back, who has been given the licence to get forward.

Schar makes way for Pivas at the hour mark. Gateshead respond with a double change.

Hall is brought down in the Gateshead box by Ferguson as he tears towards the byline. He wants a penalty but the referee awards a corner – there is a momentary confrontation between the two players but they settle their differences quickly.

Murphy switches wings to create an overload with Barnes down the left and flashes a cross into the box which is dealt with by Gateshead. Newcastle need more invention like that if they are to break down this stubborn Gateshead side.

Chance for Newcastle! Steur releases Barnes into the left channel and he plays the ball across goal but just in front of Neave who had the freedom of Tyneside at the back post. Desbois is called into action moments later, punching the ball clear after some pinball in the box.

Steur shifts the ball on to his left foot and has a go from 25 yards out, firing the ball high and wide. Good intent, though.

Ramsey is dropping in to receive the ball to feet. His average position in the first half was significantly more withdrawn than Willock’s, and Howe will surely look to get him further up the pitch to affect play in the final third in the second period.

An immediate chance for the hosts’ front man Boatswain at the start of the second half. The ball just gets away from him.

Newcastle have work to do and, unlike last weekend against Darlington, Howe sticks with the same XI at the start of the second period. Gateshead also unchanged.

A moment of silence impeccably observed in memory of King Kev 🖤🤍 pic.twitter.com/TmeQ5A64jN

Newcastle go into the break a goal down. There have been chances for the visitors, who dominated the ball in that first period. Expect changes at the interval.

How has Barnes missed that?! A lovely ball in from the right comes through a thicket of limbs and lands at the winger’s feet only a couple of yards out from goal. He can’t make a meaningful contact on the ball and the chance passes him by.

Gateshead’s goal came against the run of play and was there first shot on target. It’s not great from Fabian Schar, who conceded the free kick competing for a long ball down the middle and Nick Pope was a little slow off his line to smother the shot too.

Gateshead 1 Newcastle 0 (Supyk) Gateshead win a free-kick 25 yards out, just to the right of the D. Chadwick’s initial effort ricochets through the wall and new signing Supyk is first on to the scene to prod the ball beyond Pope. A calamity at the back for Howe’s side!

Our Kiwi just can't stop scoring! 🇳🇿😄 https://t.co/Z0cjcEadvG pic.twitter.com/6Kca67vFom

Neave comes close to opening the scoring, firing an effort across the face of goal that goes behind for a corner.

Hall then gets a shot away from the edge of the box, but cannot keep his half-volley down and the ball sails over the bar.

Newcastle look most dangerous when Schar steps up and punches in those line-breaking passes. Gateshead defending resolutely, though, keeping things compact across the backline.

Murphy earns his side a free-kick down the right. He delivers the ball himself, with the box loaded with Schar and Murphy, and the former steals in to the near post but cannot quite stoop down low enough to get a meaningful contact on the ball. Desbois gathers without fuss.

Newcastle have won a glut of corners down their left, all of which have been taken short. The latest is played out to Steur who rains in a cross which is claimed by the goalkeeper.

Sean Steur looks like a player... some really nice touches from the young Dutchman. He is always looking to make a progressive pass and has been a real bright spark. Newcastle have dominated the game. As you would expect against opposition four divisions below them

Another tidy involvement from Steur, who disguises a pass to Ramsey on the edge of the box. The ball is worked into the path of Murphy and deflects out for a corner. The former Ajax midfielder is growing in confidence.

Hall puts in another ball from the left, this time to the back post, where the ball is headed away by Ferguson.

New signing Steur is starting to creep forward, carrying the ball nicely and picking it back up in the right channel. He stands a cross up to the near post but Murphy’s header is dealt with by Desbois.

Hall works a yard of space in a dangerous area down the left moments later, but the ball ricochets back off him and out for goal-kick.

Hall punches in a lovely ball down the line for Barnes to run on to, but the move is snuffed out by Robinson.

It does seem strange that this game has not sold out. There are thought to be about 7,000 fans inside the stadium, which once had a capacity of more than 11,000 when it was one of the country’s premier athletics venues. They even used to have Diamond League events here not so long ago.

But the capacity has been steadily reduced for safety reasons and it is rarely used for anything other than local athletic events and Gateshead FC games.

There were officially only 50 tickets left for sale a few minutes before kick-off, but there are lots of empty seats.

Chadwick lofts a tidy cross in from the left, but Boatswain’s header drifts wide of the mark. The chance came off a decent spell of possession from Cattermole’s side, the most fluent they have been in this match so far.

Ramsey regains possession high up the pitch and releases Barnes who plays in Murphy, but the Newcastle forward mistimes his run and the linesman’s flag goes up. A promising counter.

Ramsey is brought down on the edge of the box as he tries to break free and the referee awards a free-kick. There are a few contenders to take it (Schar, Barnes, Hall) but in the end it is Barnes who gets a shot away, but his curled effort flies just wide of the mark.

Another weighted ball over the top from Schar puts Anifowose under pressure in the left channel but his ball across the face of goal is cleared to safety by a team-mate.

Newcastle circulating the ball in front of Gateshead’s first line of pressure. The hosts regain possession but struggle to find a way through Newcastle’s midfield.

Schar getting a few early touches as he makes his return from injury. He plays a long, raking diagonal out to Barnes who cannot quite get past his man.

Neave tests Desbois with a well-struck effort off the next phase of play.

The officials and both sets of players line up behind a banner with the message ‘Rest in peace, Kevin Keegan’. Newcastle are in their new navy-blue away shirt, with Gateshead in their home white-and-black kit. A minute’s silence is then observed immaculately.

The tributes left in honour of Kevin Keegan outside St James’ Park is a sight to behold, with flowers, shirts and scarves covering the ground and steps in the south-west corner. It is a very moving thing to behold as people come to pay their respects to the Newcastle legend.

There will also be a minute’s silence before today’s game against Gateshead.

Some time tidy centre-forward play from Levi Amantchi in last week’s 3-3 draw. The target man has since been loaned to Kidderminster Harriers...

A post shared by Gateshead FC (@gfc_official)

Incomings Bazoumana Touré ⇠ Hoffenheim, £43mAladji Bamba ⇠ Monaco, £30mSean Steur ⇠ Ajax, £20mEwen Jaouen ⇠ Stade Reims, £18m

OutgoingsSandro Tonali ⇢ Tottenham Hotspur, £92.5mAnthony Gordon ⇢ Barcelona, £68mKieran Trippier ⇢ Wolverhampton Wanderers, FreeMatt Targett ⇢ Hull City, FreeEmil Krafth, FreeJohn Ruddy, Free

It has been a difficult and, at times, acrimonious 12 months for Eddie Howe, who must have wondered whether the job was still worth the hassle given the criticism and online vitriol he received at times last season.

Few would have blamed him if he had quit, but Howe has always been fully committed and always knew there would be a period like this to come through.

He has been in the job almost five years and last season was the first time he had been vilified by a section of the fanbase. It left its mark. The boos that followed defeats at St James’ Park hurt and he worried the unity that had powered the team’s success had fractured irreparably.

The apparent collective shrug that greeted another run to the Carabao Cup semi-final, while guiding the team into the knockout rounds of the Champions League for the first time was a source of bewilderment and frustration.

Howe has not complained or moaned. Although he wobbled towards the end of last season and there were some calling for him to be sacked, he was supported and encouraged by those above him. That loyalty mattered.

The problem is, negativity lingers in the fanbase. Even a picture of Howe at pre-season training, posted on social media by the club, led to abusive comments questioning his ability and character. Some of it was toxic. It was rightly called out by other supporters.

Goals from Elliot Anderson (wonder what happened to him?!), Allan Saint-Maximin and Jay Turner-Cooke helped Newcastle overturn a 2-0 half-time deficit when they last visited Gateshead International Stadium in 2023.

Speaking through Gateshead’s club media, Cattermole said of facing Newcastle: “It’s obviously a different test. We have to respect the opposition, they’re a high-quality team and it might not be what we’re getting in our league but we’ll still try to implement what we believe we want to be in and out of possession. It’ll be a great physical challenge for us.

He added: “They [my players] have all shown up great. What a game for them. What a game for them to go and test yourself against some big names and fantastic coaching staff, for us all it’s a great challenge for us. We hope we give them a good test, we hope we give them the challenge they want as well. I played in many of these games as a player as well. We expect it to be competitive.”

💬 "What a game for [the players] to go & play."Lee Cattermole talks tomorrow's game against @NUFC at the GIS ⤵️📺👉 https://t.co/DGuJRosJ2K pic.twitter.com/rccs5FzhG6

A classic first-game-of-pre-season vibe to Newcastle’s team sheet as established stars rub shoulders with youngsters from the academy.

Only one of their four summer signings, former Ajax midfielder Sean Steur, starts the game and there will be a lot of interest in the 18-year-old. The youngster has impressed in training over the last couple of weeks but it is thought he has a lot of work to do physically to be ready for the Premier League.

Full-back Leo Shahar was in and around the first team last season as was striker Sean Neave. Alex Murphy, who started one game in the Champions League last season is expected to go out on loan before the window shuts, but starts alongside Fabian Schar in the centre of defence.

Worryingly there is no sign of Sven Botman and Will Osula who both played in the behind-closed-doors friendly against Darlington last weekend.

Joelinton, Tino Livramento and Lewis Miley are still being eased back into things after injuries at the end of last season.

Another new signing, goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen, is on the bench and will play the second half against their National League neighbours.

Gateshead lost manager Rob Elliot to Carlisle at the end of last season and are now managed by former Sunderland and Middlesbrough midfielder Lee Cattermole.

Arrivals in Gateshead 👋 pic.twitter.com/9hTtruxGEo

Jul 18: Newcastle 3 Darlington 0 Jul 25: Gateshead vs NewcastleJul 29: Bristol City vs NewcastleAug 8: Valencia vs NewcastleAug 12: Everton vs NewcastleAug 15: Newcastle vs Bayer LeverkusenAug 16: Newcastle vs Strasbourg

Ready for our return to the GIS! 🤍🔢 pic.twitter.com/lg1TfjyD6q

Fabian Schär returns from an ankle injury that has sidelined him since January, but only one of Newcastle’s four summer signings (Sean Steur) starts.

Welcome to live coverage of Newcastle United’s pre-season friendly against North-East neighbours Gateshead. Eddie Howe’s side make the three-mile journey south of the River Tyne having beaten Darlington 3-0 in their first outing of the summer last weekend. The Magpies’ National League opponents this afternoon, helmed by former Sunderland captain Lee Cattermole, have already played three times in pre-season, thrashing Blyth 6-0 and drawing against Heaton Stannington and Hebburn Town. The Heed threatened a shock win in their last meeting with Newcastle three summers’ ago, leading 2-0 at the interval before conceding three second-half goals.

This contest at Gateshead International Stadium will be Newcastle’s first match since the death of Kevin Keegan and the club have confirmed that a minute of silence will be observed before kick-off. Newcastle’s men’s, women’s and academy teams will wear black armbands for all pre-season matches this summer.

Newcastle United's men's, women's and Under-21s teams will wear black armbands across all pre-season matches this summer as the club honours the life of Kevin Keegan.Full details ⤵️

Newcastle will welcome Liverpool, with whom Keegan enjoyed success in the 1970s, to St James’ Park for their Premier League opener, and the two sides are in talks over a suitable pre-match tribute. Flowers, messages and mementos have been laid outside Newcastle’s ground since Keegan’s death on Monday, including a heartfelt message penned by fellow club legend Alan Shearer, which read: “I hope you realised how much you meant, to me, to this club, to everyone. Thank you does not seem enough. Rest In Peace Boss. Alan Shearer.”

With regards to the football, there is an acceptance among Newcastle supporters that, having finished 12th in the Premier League last season and lost Anthony Gordon, Kieran Trippier and Sandro Tonali, this is a summer of transition. The uncertainty surrounding the future of £100m-rated club captain Bruno Guimarães, who is on the radar of Arsenal, will be a concern; Newcastle will be keen to avoid a repeat of the furore that circled Alexander Isak’s departure last summer. Guimarães will join the team next week following his World Cup exploits with Brazil and is expected to take part in Newcastle’s La Manga training camp, which starts on July 31.

Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. Bazoumana Touré – the £50m winger acquired from Hoffenheim – is expected to feature today having returned from his post-World Cup holiday. Yesterday Newcastle announced the arrival of midfielder Aladji Bamba, the France youth international, from Monaco and he was immediately integrated into team training. There is every possibility that he will feature this afternoon. Gateshead this week announced two signings of their own, as Luke Supyk, the New Zealand Under-20 forward, agreed a two-year deal having scored three goals in pre-season as a trialist. Defender Jack Robinson also joined the club.

#1987. Liverpool learn why Arsenal's "forceful" Noni Madueke avoided red card after controversial Alexis Mac Allister head clash

By Lewis Nolan | 01 Nov 2026 23:04

The Premier League have revealed that Arsenal winger Noni Madueke was not sent off against Liverpool after clashing with Alexis Mac Allister as his action was not considered aggressive or violent.

Mikel Arteta helped his side earn an invaluable three points on Sunday, overseeing a 1-0 win at Anfield in the Premier League thanks to Kai Havertz's early winner.

Liverpool pushed for an equaliser in the second half, and there were calls from the home side for Arsenal to be reduced to 10 men in the 79th minute when Madueke clashed heads with Mac Allister.

The Premier League's match centre have now confirmed that the supposed headbutt did not reach the threshold for a red card, with the VAR saying: "All of the situations have been checked and cleared. There is some contact as Madueke and Mac Allister square-up. In my opinion, it's not forceful, not violent, not brutal".

Madueke did lean his head into Mac Allister, who promptly fell to the ground, though the midfielder was himself booked for his role in a scuffle.

#LIVARS – 79’ The referee’s call of no violent conduct by Madueke on Mac Allister was checked and confirmed by VAR. VAR: “All of the situations have been checked and cleared. There is some contact as Madueke and Mac Allister square-up. In my opinion, it's not forceful, not violent, not brutal”.

Sunday was not the first time that Arsenal have been involved in a contentious decision in relation to an alleged headbutt, with defender Gabriel Magalhaes infamously involved in a clash with Erling Haaland last season.

The Manchester City striker did not react to Gabriel's head movement, and he ultimately stayed on the pitch and avoided a three-game ban despite the wide consensus that he was fortunate to escape punishment.

Madueke's movement was not as aggressive as his teammate's, and Jamie Carragher was critical of Mac Allister's reaction.

While the Liverpool midfielder's response was exaggerated, Reds striker Alexander Isak was criticised for not reacting to a clear pull by Jurrien Timber in the box that arguably prevented him from scoring.

If Haaland had reacted to Gabriel, the defender would have almost certainly been sent off, so perhaps it would be wrong to criticise players for their reactions when game-changing fouls have often been missed at key moments in crucial matches.

Arsenal have not received a single red card in any of their last 49 Premier League games, with their last red in the top flight coming against Liverpool in May 2025.

However, to suggest that Arteta's achievements at the Emirates have been aided by lenient refereeing would diminish the work he has achieved during his time at the club.

The Spaniard has managed to take the Gunners from mediocrity to the pinnacle of English football, and they should be strong favourites to retain their title.

#1985. Manchester United vs. Roma: Head-to-head record and past meetings before Champions League battle

By Seye Omidiora | 01 Nov 2026 23:39

A beleaguered Manchester United side desperately fighting to arrest an alarming domestic slide welcome an in-form Roma to Old Trafford on Tuesday for matchday four of the Champions League.

The Red Devils sit 17th in the Premier League table and are winless in nine consecutive matches across all competitions, having succumbed to a demoralising 2-0 defeat at Chelsea after Lisandro Martinez's quickfire dismissal.

In stark contrast, Gian Piero Gasperini's rampant Giallorossi travel to the North West brimming with confidence after a five-match unbeaten run, having netted three or more goals in four of those outings, including Saturday's 5-2 demolition of Udinese.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides.

Manchester United and Roma have crossed paths eight times in major European competition, with every single encounter taking place in the 21st century across both the Champions League and the Europa League.

The Red Devils have historically dominated this fixture, coming out on top in five of those clashes, while suffering two defeats and sharing the spoils on one occasion.

The rivalry's inaugural chapter unfolded during the 2006-07 Champions League quarter-finals, where Roma initially gained the upper hand with a 2-1 first-leg victory at the Stadio Olimpico thanks to goals from Rodrigo Taddei and Mirko Vucinic.

However, Sir Alex Ferguson's men responded six days later by inflicting one of the most brutal scorelines in modern knockout history, tearing the Italians apart in an unforgettable 7-1 thrashing at Old Trafford, featuring braces from Cristiano Ronaldo and Michael Carrick.

Familiarity was taken to another level the following season in 2007-08, when the two European heavyweights locked horns four times in a single continental campaign.

Drawn together in Group F, Wayne Rooney settled a tense 1-0 win for United in Manchester before Gerard Pique and Mancini traded strikes in a 1-1 draw in Rome; the sides were then paired together again in the quarter-finals, where United secured a comfortable 3-0 aggregate triumph via a 2-0 away win and a 1-0 home success en route to lifting the trophy in Moscow.

Their most recent showdowns came in the 2020-21 Europa League semi-finals, producing another goal-laden spectacle that tilted heavily toward the English giants.

Despite trailing 2-1 at the break in the first leg at Old Trafford, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's side staged a devastating second-half blitz to secure a 6-2 win led by doubles from Edinson Cavani and Bruno Fernandes, which rendered Roma's spirited 3-2 victory in the Italian capital two weeks later mere consolation as United advanced 8-5 on aggregate.

#1982. Monza 0-5 Milan Primavera: Zaramella shines in much-needed trashing

After a tough run in the league, Milan Primavera managed to build on their mid-week cup win with a strong performance against Monza this afternoon.

Excluding Wednesday’s win against Catanzaro in the Primavera Cup, Milan Primavera had lost four of their last five games heading into today’s clash. In short, a response was needed in the league as well and that is exactly what Giovanni Renna got.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There is still a long way to go, especially when you consider how much Monza have struggled so far, but it’s a crucial confidence boost to build on.

Milan Primavera opened the scoring in the 24th minute through Max Anastasio. The winger received the ball on the left flank and cut inside to shoot with his right foot. He managed to beat the goalkeeper with a nice strike, giving his side a perfect start.

It didn’t take long before the second goal arrived: four minutes later, Francesco Domnitei fired a shot on target and forced the goalkeeper to a save. However, he couldn’t control the rebound, which Mattia Zaramella pounced on for an easy goal.

Before the first half was up, Luca Nolli almost made it 3-0, hitting the post with an effort from close range. Either way, it was a great first half that put the Rossoneri in a very difficult position.

Sure enough, the second half was a lot of the same as Monza struggled to get themselves back into the game. Milan created some good chances almost immediately, but had to wait until the 65th minute for their next goal.

Zaramella picked out Riccardo Grassini in the box after winning the ball back high up the pitch, and the latter didn’t make any mistakes with the finish. Five minutes later, similarly to the first and second goals, Zaramella got his brace after picking up a good position inside the box.

It didn’t end there as Yanis Messaoudi made the most of a corner in the dying minutes, finding the back of the net with a header. 5-0, in other words, and a huge win for Milan Primavera to move to eight place at the time of writing.

#1981. Tottenham transfer news: Roberto De Zerbi ready to fight Man City for £12.5m 'favourite' of Mauricio Pochettino

By Lewis Nolan | 01 Nov 2026 23:45

Tottenham Hotspur will have to compete with Manchester City for Villarreal full-back Alexander Freeman, the latest report has claimed.

Spurs have started to improve considerably in the Premier League, collecting nine points from the last nine on offer.

Roberto De Zerbi's side most recently emerged as 2-0 winners against Crystal Palace on Saturday, but despite their strong form, there are concerns about the strength of the squad.

Pedro Porro did not start any of those three victories, and while the head coach has indicated that the defender is ready to make a return to the XI, the club must avoid aggravating his hamstring issue.

A new report from Football Insider claims that Spurs are interested in signing Villarreal right-back Freeman, though they may face competition from the likes of Manchester City for his signature.

Freeman enjoyed a strong showing with the United States of America at the 2026 World Cup under boss Mauricio Pochettino, making five appearances while scoring once and assisting once, though he is only price by Transfermarkt at £12.5m.

For Villarreal this campaign, the 22-year-old has played 14 times and started six games, and he has shown that he is not only a strong passer, but that he can also regularly win his duels.

It would be surprising if Tottenham looked to sign a starting right-back given Pedro Porro possesses immense quality.

However, the Spaniard has not started any of his side's last three games due to injury concerns, with Gray being forced to fill in.

Signing Freeman may allow Gray to be used in a more natural midfield role, while also giving Porro a suitable backup on the right.

Spurs fought against relegation in each of the last two seasons, and it is far too soon to suggest they have escaped the battle against the drop this term.

City are ordinarily in the hunt for every trophy available, but they could face severe sanctions after being found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

Demotion has not been ruled out as a punishment, and prospective targets may be wary about joining before sanctions have been revealed, something that could give Spurs an edge in a transfer tussle.

#1980. Tenerife footballer Jesus de Miguel dies after on-field collision

Tenerife player Jesus De Miguel has died after an on-field collision in a match on Monday, his club have announced.

The collision occurred as Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono raced from his goal to challenge De Miguel for the ball in stoppage time of a Spanish second-tier game at Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Canary Islands club said in a statement on Tuesday: “Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic passing, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.

“There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness.

Late on Monday night Tenerife issued a statement confirming De Miguel had been admitted to hospital and was initially described as “stable despite the severity of his condition”.

An update in the early hours of Tuesday morning said his condition had “worsened neurologically”.

Owono was immediately sent off after he charged out of his goal to challenge De Miguel in the centre circle, his knee appearing to connect with the Tenerife player’s head.

Andorra and Tenerife players beckoned on medical staff immediately and appeared visibly upset by De Miguel’s condition.

The match was suspended after the incident.

Opponents Andorra issued a statement on X which read: “With broken hearts and devastated, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, to all his teammates, friends, and to CD Tenerife. Rest in peace.”

LaLiga said in a statement: “We wish to express our deep sadness over the tragic passing of Jesús de Miguel Alameda. We share in the grief of his family, his loved ones, and @CDTOficial during these very difficult times. All our affection and support. Rest in peace.”

Meanwhile, other Spanish clubs posted messages of condolence to Tenerife and De Miguel’s family.

Barcelona said: “From FC Barcelona, we are deeply saddened by the tragic news of the passing of Jesus de Miguel, CD Tenerife player. Our thoughts and support are with his family, friends and loved ones during these difficult times.”

Real Madrid said the club “wishes to express its condolences and affection to his family, his teammates, his club and all his loved ones”.

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick faces a major defensive decision regarding Lisandro Martinez, but the centre-back is tipped to start on Tuesday night even though Matthijs de Ligt represents a strong alternative.

Indeed, Martinez is backed to feature from the off despite his recent scathing criticism of the club and a domestic suspension following his sending-off against Chelsea in the Premier League.

The Argentine should partner Harry Maguire in the heart of the rearguard, flanked by Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui on either side of the central defenders to protect goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Between the two defeats in the Europa League and the three draws in the league, it has been a so-so start to the season for Milan. In that sense, tonight’s derby against Inter could act as a catalyst for a good period, as a win would take them within four points of the Nerazzurri.

#1977. Why Sebastien Pocognoli picked James Penrice as he talks up Rangers star's quality

Scotland manager Sebastien Pocognoli insists the selection of Rangers' James Penrice was "logical."

The left-back, who has also operated in midfield, has been rewarded for his form so far since moving to Ibrox on loan from AEK Athens. He immediately impressed since joining but was left out of Pocognoli's first squad for the last camp.

Now, the 27-year-old will get the chance to win his first cap when the national team takes on North Macedonia and Switzerland this month.

The Scotland boss says the quality Penrice possesses, and his readiness for his system, made him an obvious choice.

#1976. Scotland squad: Two stars return, Rangers man gets first call-up and surprises in midfield

Scotland talisman Scott McTominay has returned to the squad ahead of the country’s Nations League matches against North Macedonia and Switzerland later this month.

Capped 73 times by Scotland with 15 goals, McTominay missed this season’s first international break due to a minor heart procedure, but the Napoli man returns having played his club’s past seven matches. He will work with Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli for the first time.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Fellow Serie A player Che Adams is also back in the squad after a muscle strain ruled him out of the matches against Slovenia twice, North Macedonia and Switzerland in September and October. He is one of four No 9s selected by Pocognoli.

In-form Rangers defender James Penrice has won his first call-up, with Sassuolo’s Josh Doig the one to miss out. Dinamo Zagreb defender Scott McKenna has been ruled out with a back strain. Celtic right-back Colby Donovan has also been omitted.

In midfield, uncapped Blackburn Rovers No 6 Kristi Montgomery keeps his place after earning a call-up last time out. There are no places for veteran Kenny McLean, nor Udinese’s 20-year-old Lennon Miller. Both were picked last time by Pocognoli.

Scotland play North Macedonia at Hampden Park on Friday, November 13 before travelling to St Gallen to face Switzerland at Sitterstadion on Monday, November 16.

They sit third in Nations League B1 on four points and require at least a win and a draw from their remaining two games to stand a chance of toppling Slovenia and finishing second in the group.

Goalkeepers: Scott Bain, Angus Gunn, Liam Kelly, Jon McCracken.

Defenders: Luis Binks, Luke Graham, Jack Hendry, Aaron Hickey, Nathan Patterson, James Penrice, Andy Robertson, Kieran Tierney, Stephen Welsh.

Midfielders: Ryan Christie, Lewis Ferguson, Billy Gilmour, John McGinn, Josh McPake, Scott McTominay, Kristi Montgomery.

Forwards: Che Adams, Kieron Bowie, Findlay Curtis, Ben Gannon-Doak, Oli McBurnie, Robbie Ure.

#1975. Bodo/Glimt vs Lille - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 01 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 14:13

Sensing an opportunity to snatch a win in the Champions League's league-phase, Bodo/Glimt will welcome Lille to Aspmyra Stadion on Tuesday.

Glimt are desperate to avoid a third defeat in four continental games, though Les Dogues are looking to build on their win last time out by collecting their first points in the competition.

Kjetil Knutsen's Bodo are currently embroiled in a tense title race at the summit of Norway's Eliteserien, and they will be hoping that their 3-2 triumph over rivals Viking FK can inspire them to victory in midweek.

Glimt raced into an early two-goal lead during Friday's top-of-the-table showdown, only for Viking to claw their way back to 2-2 with less than 40 minutes on the clock.

However, Knutsen's side got their noses back in front via Jens Hauge moments later and were able to hold out to beat the reigning champions and draw level on points in second, with both teams' managers being sent off before the interval.

Inspired by their success in that heated clash, Bodo - who currently sit 28th in the league-phase table - will be eyeing a spot in the Champions League's top 24 by the end of the matchweek.

In order to rise through the ranks, Glimt will need to bounce back from a 4-3 defeat to Napoli last time out in Europe, though they will be buoyed by facing one of the competition's strugglers on home turf.

Meanwhile, Davide Ancelotti's Lille have produced a strong campaign overall, but it would be fair to say that they have stumbled over the past month.

Prior to their 1-0 victory against Lens on Friday, Les Dogues had produced a four-game winless run across all competitions, losing twice and drawing twice.

Those defeats were both in the Champions League, with Ancelotti's men beaten 3-0 by Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on October 10, and 4-2 by Galatasaray at home two weeks ago.

To make matters worse, Lille are still waiting for their first Champions League points this term and sit 35th in the table, three shy of the top 24 and six behind the top eight.

That being said, the club's continental strife belies the fact that Les Dogues are second only to Paris Saint-Germain in Ligue 1 so far, and are not to be underestimated on Tuesday after scoring in all but one of their 13 matches this season.

Bodo will be without goalkeepers Julian Faye Lund and Isak Sjong due to respective injuries, though Nikita Haikin should be on hand to continue between the sticks.

Midfielder Hakon Evjen is also sidelined with a knee injury, while August Mikkelsen is dealing with a groin issue, so Patrick Berg and Sondre Fet could start in the centre of the park, platforming a strike partnership of Ole Didrik Blomberg and Andreas Helmersen.

As for Lille, they are missing the versatile Ethan Mbappe, who is serving the final game of his suspension following a red card against Real Betis on matchday one, while Hamza Igamane has a knee injury, and fellow striker Ayase Ueda is working his way back from a foot injury.

In their absence, 40-year-old Olivier Giroud could lead the line on Tuesday, supported by a trio of Dilane Bakwa, Hakon Haraldsson and Soriba Diaoune.

Elsewhere, right-back Tiago Santos suffered an anterior cruciate ligament tear and meniscus damage against Le Havre on October 12, so 18-year-old Maxima Goffi looks set to start in midweek.

Haikin; Sjovold, Bjortuft, Gundersen, Bjorkan; Auklend, Fet, Berg, Hauge; Blomberg, Helmersen

Ozer; Goffi, Ngoy, Alexsandro, Perraud; Andre, Bentaleb; Bakwa, Haraldsson, Diaoune; Giroud

Bodo may have lost two of their three Champions League matches so far, but they will be inspired by their victory over Viking and could deliver a strong performance in midweek.

However, Lille will be desperate to get off the mark in the competition, and may hold Glimt to a draw after ending their winless run.

#1973. Arsenal transfer news: Gunners in 'contact' with new Real Madrid star ahead of January after moving on from Vinicius Junior

By Lewis Nolan | 02 Nov 2026 00:17

Arsenal are in contact with Real Madrid attacker Endrick as a January move becomes more realistic, the newest report has revealed.

The Gunners will be revelling in their crucial 1-0 win against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, with that result taking them to first place in the Premier League.

Mikel Arteta's side had to rely on their defence for much of the game due to the pressure their hosts applied, but the game would have been more comfortable if they had better forwards on the pitch.

The January transfer window is fast approaching, and many supporters are keen for the club to make a marquee addition so that they do not have to rely too heavily on Bukayo Saka in the second half of the season.

Arteta was said to have been keen on Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior in the summer transfer window, though that move was always unlikely.

However, TEAMtalk claim that Arsenal are in contact with the representatives of Real attacker Endrick, who has grown increasingly frustrated by his playing time in Spain and would be open to a January move.

Endrick was reportedly of interest to many teams in the Premier League over the summer, and he may regret staying in Spain given he has played just 108 minutes for Real Madrid in all competitions.

The 20-year-old move to Lyon on loan last January, playing 21 times, scoring eight goals and providing seven assists.

One of the Brazilian's best assets is his ability to cross into the penalty area, while he is also capable of dribbling past opposition defenders before unleashing a shot at goal.

Endrick is also capable of playing across the frontline, and he could be an invaluable option for Arteta, who may need to rotate his attack considerably over the coming months in order to avoid injuries occuring.

While most have acknowledged that Arsenal's attack has been subpar for some time, the prospect of the Gunners adding an elite attacker to their ranks should be frightening.

The Londoners have already won eight of their first nine Premier League games, conceding just five times, and they have been nearly flawless at the back.

Should Arteta add a new dynamic to their attack, in January or the summer, then the club could be set for a period of dominance, especially if Manchester City are relegated or expelled for breaching the league's spending rules.

Prominent Celtic groups have called for major shareholder Dermot Desmond to attend this year’s AGM after he was represented by his son Ross in 2025.

A statement from Celtic on the meeting read: “The Celtic manager and board faced ‘hard but fair’ questioning when they took part in a well-attended meeting at Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club last night (Monday).

“Members from Greenock, Port Glasgow, Gourock, Johnny Doyle, Port Glasgow Hibs and Largs clubs were among around 120 Celtic supporters who attended to seek information and voice concerns.

“Martin O’Neill joined chairman Brian Wilson, chief executive Michael Nicholson, chief financial officer Chris McKay and other club officials in a two-and-a-half-hour question and answer session.”

On the event, Wilson said: “We were grateful to the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club for hosting this event in a way that allowed everyone to make their points, many of them critical, and to ask searching questions which we did our best to answer.

“We didn’t expect an easy ride and didn’t get one, but the meeting was conducted in a constructive and mutually respectful way and the messages delivered by supporters will be taken on board and learned from.”

O’Neill said: “I asked to attend the meeting because I want to meet supporters as much as I possibly can.

“We have had a few difficult weeks in recent times and I understand our supporters’ frustrations, but my resolve and the commitment of the players is as strong as ever to continue to bring success and progress to the club as we have done before.”

Michael Nicholson said: “I thank the committee and members of the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club for inviting us to their club, and all supporters attending for the opportunity to discuss their concerns and the issues that mean so much to us all. Everyone in the room wants the best for Celtic and that was evident.

“We are grateful for supporters’ input and look forward to continuing to meet with supporters as we work on improving communication and engagement in the weeks and months ahead.”

Celtic confirmed that “issues raised by supporters included recruitment, transfer policy, communications, and the club’s ambitions and strategy”. They plan to release further details in due course on new engagement initiatives.

The event in Greenock follows similar sessions held across recent months with the Affiliation of Registered CSCs in Glasgow and the Association of Irish Celtic Supporters' Clubs in Cork. The club says it plans to hold more in the coming weeks.

Celtic have two matches ahead of the next international break - both at home. They play Besiktas in the Europa League on Thursday before the visit of Kilmarnock in the Premiership on Sunday.
