#1947. Westlake formation trick treats Hassocks to FA Vase history on Halloween

On Halloween afternoon, Hassocks delivered a frighteningly good performance to hammer Eastbourne United 5-2 in the FA Vase and make club history.

Victory took the Robins into the third round for the first time ever and left them as one of only two Sussex clubs still standing in the competition alongside Crawley Down Gatwick.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

This all-Southern Combination clash at the Hassocks Hotel Beacon Ground guaranteed at least one Premier Division side would progress to the last 64 of the competition.

Before kick off, it looked too close to call. Hassocks and United sit third and second respectively in the league table, level on 30 points.

Not only that, but they have faced off twice already this season with nothing separating them on either occasion. A 2-2 draw in the Sussex Principal RUR Charity Cup at the Oval Arena 39 days earlier was followed by a 0-0 stalemate when meeting in the league in Mid Sussex 18 days ago.

James Westlake played a trick and sought to counter this familiarity by changing formation and the way Hassocks played. To say it worked a treat would be an understatement.

United were caught totally off guard. The Robins went ahead after just 30 seconds. They led by three inside a quarter hour and headed into half time 4-0 to the good with the tie over.

The visitors belatedly got to grips with what Hassocks had done after the break to win the second 45 minutes 2-1. But even then, the Robins produced the standout moment of the half when Lewis Finney smashed home a spectacular over-the-shoulder volley from 30 yards which will surely be the best goal any Hassocks player nets this season.

Pushing Finney further forward into the number 10 role of a 4-2-3-1 formation was one of the surprises sprung by Westlake. Finney did not take long to make an impact as he was also the scorer of that very early opener.

Brett Patton and Dan Hull got in a bit of a mess trying to keep possession at the back for United with Finney latching onto the loose ball, charging in on goal and rounding Alieu Secka before firing into the unguarded net.

Plenty of home fans missed it still making their way out of the Clubhouse. Some had barely settled into position when Jack Troak made it 2-0 on the five minute mark.

Big Alex Fair crossed from the right and when Secka could only parry as far as the penalty spot, Troak was on hand to take a touch and pick out the bottom corner.

Hassocks were rampant and United could do nothing to break out of their own half. Troak put a good chance from a Finney pass just wide and a Devon Fender corner then led to an almighty scramble in the box.

Finney saw a shot blocked in the chaos by Hull, tall striker Jamie Wilkes put the follow up against the post and Patton made a flying tackle to keep out the third bite of the cherry from Troak.

The Robins' third arrived on 13 minutes and was credited to Big Alex Fair even though he said afterwards it was an own goal. Fair glided his way around three United players and crossed with the head of the hapless Hull helping divert it past Secka at the near post.

There was no doubt that Fair scored the fourth with 23 minutes played. Dan Turner launched over a long throw which Troak met with a diving header brilliantly saved by Secka. The rebound fell straight to Fair, who reacted quickly to lash home a first-time drive with his left foot.

United's nightmare would have turned even darker without some inspired goalkeeping from Secka. He threw himself down to his right to repel a fierce Finney shot from 18 yards after a quick throw between Troak and Raging Joe Bull caught the visitors asleep.

Troak was also denied by Secka; first from a shot straight into the arms of the United number one and then a header following another wicked right wing delivery from Fair.

Finney produced his moment of magic five minutes after the restart. Fair flicked on an Ed Cooper kick which Liam Benson collected and lifted over the top of the United defence.

The dink was perfectly placed into the path of the onrushing Finney. He watched it drop from the sky like a hawk straight onto his right foot, unleashing an unstoppable effort which rocketed over the stranded Secka to move Hassocks a scarcely-believable five goals ahead.

United pulled one back just three minutes later when Rhyle Ovenden bent a low free kick around the wall from the edge of the box.

The good news for the visitors was short-lived, however, as an unsavoury incident midway through the half saw Sam Scott red carded. Scott had been substituted and was making his way around the perimeter of the pitch when he became involved in an altercation with Turner.

Whatever happened was enough to seriously anger the normally placid Turner, cause United striker Callum Barlow to run over and attempt to shepherd Scott away and for referee Hassan Rajwani to whip out a straight red once order was restored.

With Scott having already been replaced by Zach Robitaille, it made no numerical difference on the day. United though will now have to cope without one of their regulars through suspension. A potentially helpful situation for Hassocks back in the bread and butter of the Premier Division promotion race.

In a sign of how fierce encounters between the Robins and United have been, that was the third sending off in the three meetings between the sides this season.

But it did not spark any more disciplinary drama as the tie petered out through the final 20 minutes bar Freddie Jones pulling back another consolation for United with a glancing header from a left wing free kick.

"To go and win like that playing against a team we are level on points with in the league and who we know will be really competitive at the top of the table sends a message to everyone that we are full of confidence and going really well at the moment," said Westlake afterwards.

A message not just to their Premier Division promotion rivals but also those left in the FA Vase. How far might the Robins now go having finally got the monkey off their back of progressing beyond round two after more than 30 years of trying?

Hassocks: Cooper; Blake, D Turner, Hendy, Bull; Wilkes, Fender; Fair, Finney, Troak; Benson.

Subs: Croal, Budd, Bonwick-Adams, Brasier (used), Farrell (unused).

Starman: Big Alex Fair was a constant threat down the right and ended the afternoon with his first brace in 15 months... presuming the second goal goes down as his.

#1945. Arsenal make Premier League history by doing something no side has ever done to Liverpool at Anfield

By Lewis Blain | 02 Nov 2026 07:21

Arsenal strengthened their position at the top of the Premier League with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield.

Kai Havertz's first-half goal proved decisive, but Mikel Arteta's side also delivered another outstanding defensive performance.

In fact, the Gunners achieved something no visiting team had ever managed against Liverpool at Anfield in Premier League history.

According to The xG Philosophy, Arsenal conceded just 0.00 expected goals on target (xGOT) against Liverpool, a record low for a visiting team at Anfield in the Premier League era.

The statistic underlines the effectiveness of Arteta's defensive unit, particularly given the pressure Liverpool applied during the opening stages.

Arsenal took the lead in the 16th minute when Declan Rice delivered a dangerous ball across the face of goal, allowing Havertz to convert at the back post.

No team had ever done this to Liverpool at Anfield in Premier League history.

Liverpool responded with sustained pressure, with goalkeeper David Raya producing an important intervention to prevent Virgil van Dijk's flick-on from reaching Alexander Isak. Florian Wirtz also struck the crossbar with a free-kick as the hosts searched for an equaliser.

However, the Gunners' defensive organisation improved considerably after the interval, restricting Liverpool's opportunities and ensuring Raya was rarely seriously troubled.

Myles Lewis-Skelly's introduction helped the champions regain control late on, while Alisson denied Christos Tzolis a second goal with an excellent save.

The result secured Arsenal's first Premier League victory at Anfield since 2012 and moved them three points clear at the summit.

There is no doubt that Arsenal deserve enormous credit for their defensive display, but Liverpool's attacking numbers will concern Andoni Iraola.

The Reds have registered just 13.3 expected goals (xG) in the Premier League this season, ranking tenth in the division, while their 12 big chances created leave them joint-19th. They also rank eighth for touches inside the opposition box, ninth for shots on target per match and joint bottom for set-piece goals, having failed to score from one.

Alexander Isak has managed six goals in eight league appearances, but the striker has received limited service, while big-money signings Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola have yet to deliver consistent end product.

Arsenal's defensive structure undoubtedly contributed to those struggles, but Liverpool cannot rely on facing opponents who allow them to create opportunities through sustained pressure.

Iraola's attacking approach has shown promise, particularly with the pace and intensity of their high press, but the lack of quality in the final third is becoming increasingly difficult to overlook.

Against Arsenal, the Gunners' defensive excellence was the main story. However, Liverpool's inability to turn promising attacking positions into genuine chances suggests there is still plenty of work for Iraola to do.

#1944. Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

Richarlison. 90+2. pic.twitter.com/VIOS4Jh7P2

Tottenham will take on Getafe and Hoffenheim back on home soil before taking on Brentford on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

Chelsea have four more pre-season games, including fixtures against Juventus and AC Milan, before travelling to Fulham in the opening Premier League game of the Xabi Alonso era.

There is the final whistle and the 10 men of Tottenham snatch victory at the death with Richarlison scoring with seconds remaining.

In the final few seconds of the game, 10-man Tottenham win it. Donley’s shot from just outside the box hits the post and Richarlison follows up to score. It would have been a close call on offside if VAR was in use but it is not and Tottenham will take victory in Sydney.

Tottenham are being forced into a late change as Kyerematen, who come on for Robertson and nearly scored that wonder solo goal, is being forced off injured and is replaced by Tingey.

Delap is found in the centre of the Tottenham box with a cross from the right but the striker’s header from around the penalty spot goes wide and does not really trouble the target.

Initially, after Danso’s red card, Chelsea were in the ascendancy with a man advantage but Tottenham have dealt pretty well down a man.

Kyerematen nearly scores a quite sensational solo goal from inside his own half before driving forward. As he approaches the Chelsea penalty area, he tries to pick out the top corner and his effort comes off the top of the bar.

Xabi Alonso is making seven changes, yes seven, at once! That includes the likes of Delap and Tosin, who takes the captain’s armband.

The changes keep coming as Williams-Barnett replaces Tel for Tottenham.

A reminder that if the game is level after 90 minutes there will be a penalty shoot-out.

Roberto de Zerbi is making a double substitution as Tye Hall and Kyerematen replace Bergvall and Robertson.

17-year-old Satpaev, who hails from Kazakhstan, is replacing Estevao for Chelsea. Satpaev, who was at Kairat and turns 18 in 11 day’s time, scored the other day for Chelsea against Western Sydney.

Moore, who was on loan at Rangers last season, is replacing Solomon for Tottenham.

Robertson is so, so lucky. He is under no pressure as a cross comes over from the left and he should clear it with ease. However, he tries to be too clever and chests it back looking for his goalkeeper. There is not enough on it, allowing Pedro to nip in but his effort from inside the six-yard box is saved. Pedro probably should have scored and Robertson is a relieved man. Kinsky at the moment is the reason why Tottenham are not a couple of goals behind.

Tottenham have found it tough to get forward a lot since Danso’s red card but they do counter now and it ends with Tonali having a shot from just outside the box but his effort is easily saved by Sharman-Lowe.

Chelsea make a change as Anselmino comes on for Hato.

Palmer plays a ball down the right channel to pick out the run in behind of Palestra, who then returns it back to Palmer inside the Tottenham penalty area. Palmer’s first-time effort from the edge of the box is blocked.

Kinsky makes another big save to deny Chelsea. Tonali, who thought he had been fouled, loses the ball deep inside his own half, before Estevao has a great chance to put Chelsea in front from inside the Tottenham penalty area but Kinsky makes the save. It would have been a touch soft to give a free-kick to Tottenham but in the Premier League you suspect Tonali would have been awarded a free-kick there.

Tottenham are going to make a change at the back in light of Danso’s red card. Hardy is going to come on for Gallagher, who is booed by some of the Chelsea fans inside Accor Stadium. The England Under-18 international Hardy has come on at right centre-back in place of Danso.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal. Pedro cuts it back from the byline to the penalty spot. Estevao gets to it first and his shot takes a deflection off Robertson. Kinsky makes a brilliant reflex save to push it onto the bar before Colwill blazes over.

Roberto de Zerbi is slumped in his seat distinctly unimpressed, shaking his head in frustration and perhaps disgust.

Palmer takes the free-kick but his effort is always curling wide of the far post.

The Austrian defender came on at half-time but has lasted just three minutes before being given his marching orders. Danso makes an absolute mess of a pass back to him from Gray and lets the ball run past him. Pedro gets around him and looks destined to drive towards the Tottenham penalty area but is brought down. Danso is shown a red card as Davies was probably not going to get across in time and it was the denial of a goal-scoring opportunity. Why do that in a pre-season friendly? Stupid.

Tottenham are making two changes at the break as Richarlison and Danso come on for Solanke and Van Hecke. Chelsea have also made a substitution as 16-year-old Nicoll-Jazuli comes on.

It appears the more times you see the incident involving Wesley Fofana and Conor Gallagher right at the end of the first half the more it looks like a penalty. Fofana did not appear to get the ball and instead catches Gallagher so Tottenham can probably feel a little aggrieved not to be given a penalty.

What have you made of that first half? Remember you can share your thoughts and opinions in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

The first half is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break in Sydney.

Should Tottenham have been awarded a penalty? Robertson whips the ball in from the left to pick out the run of Gallagher into the box. Gallagher appeared to get to the ball ahead of Fofana, who seemingly then took Gallagher out but the referee does not point to the spot. That was a risky challenge to say the least from Fofana and on first viewing probably should have result in a penalty.

Palmer plays the ball forward to pick out the run in behind of Pedro, who has a two-on-one with Kinsky but the offside flag quickly goes up. Pedro was miles offside.

That was a decent opportunity for Tottenham. Tel finds the underlapping Davies with a pass towards the byline and the latter plays it across the six-yard box but Solanke was not there to meet it. Had Solanke read that, it would have been a simple tap-in.

Tel comes close to putting Tottenham back in front. It would have been a great solo goal as he drives inside from the left wing and moves into the Chelsea penalty area. He gets the better of Essugo on the corner of the six-yard box but is denied by a decent save from Sharman-Lowe.

Pedro has a chance to put Chelsea in front but his effort goes wide. Chelsea steal possession inside the Tottenham half after a poor pass from Robertson and the ball is then played forward to Pedro, who shoots from just inside the Tottenham box but his effort goes wide of the far post. Davies did just enough to put Pedro off.

Tottenham have two penalty appeals in quick succession turned down. First was for a potential handball by Essugo and then a push by Palestra on Tel. The handball would have been very harsh and the second incident was never a foul on Tel, who was losing his balance anyway.

Chelsea gift possession away deep inside their own half and Tel’s eyes light up. The ball rolls across to the Frenchman in a central position just outside the box and he opens up his body, trying to curl one into the top corner, but gets his first-time effort all wrong and his shot misses the target by a mile.

Like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Chelsea are back on level terms. Chelsea counter from deep inside their own half and the ball ends up with Gittens on the left. From the corner of the box, he crosses towards the far post. It takes a touch off a Tottenham defender and ends up at the back post where Estevao, one of the smallest men on the pitch, beats Robertson and heads into the opposite corner.

Tottenham take the lead in Sydney courtesy of £100m signing Tonali. Solomon lays it back to Tonali who, from just outside the box, hits it first time and his shot takes a big deflection off Colwill, taking it into the far corner and giving Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal no chance. That was probably Tottenham’s first proper foray forward in the game.

It has been a pretty stop-start game as play continues to be halted by fouls. The two managers might enjoy seeing the passion of their teams but they will also want to see their sides actually play, which is quite difficult when fouls are being committed left, right and centre.

Van Hecke has already fouled his former teammate Pedro once and he bundles into him again. Van Hecke has a wry smile as he walks away and Pedro tells the referee that is now twice he has been fouled by Van Hecke. I think it is a fairly safe assumption that Van Hecke and Pedro do not like each other that much!

We are not even 10 minutes into this friendly but there is absolutely no love lost between these two sides and the challenges are flying in. Former Chelsea man Gallagher slides in on Essugo, which infuriates the Chelsea players. The referee takes his time to make his decision as both sides come to blows before giving out the first booking of the game to Gallagher.

Pedro is caught by Van Hecke out on Chelsea left and the latter is absolutely furious with that decision, believing he got the ball. However, replays show that he did not get the ball and a free-kick was the right decision. Those two were teammates at Brighton and supposedly were involved in a training ground altercation just over a year ago!

The free-kick is whipped in towards the back post and the last touch is deemed to have come off Chelsea, much to their chagrin.

Lavia catches Tonali late and eventually the referee blows his whistle to bring play back for the free-kick. In a Premier League game, that may well have been a booking for Lavia. It might be a pre-season game but there will be no love lost between these bitter rivals.

The pitch in Sydney is on the bobbly side, which will make slick passing more challenging, dare I say it probably not really possible or realistic.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, with Tottenham led out by Archie Gray and Chelsea by Levi Colwill. There is a lights show inside Accor Stadium as the teams making their way onto the pitch.

Mudryk has not played for Chelsea since November 2024 after he tested positive for meldonium, a banned substance.

The Ukrainian has consistently insisted that he never knowingly used the substance and that he did not understand how it had entered his system.

#1940. Tottenham transfer news: Forgotten £50m outcast now given fresh hope of Spurs escape in January

By Lewis Blain | 02 Nov 2026 07:43

Richarlison could finally be handed a route out of Tottenham Hotspur after Trabzonspor renewed their interest in signing the Brazilian forward.

The 29-year-old has fallen out of favour under Roberto De Zerbi and has been left outside the club's first-team plans following a frustrating summer transfer window.

With Spurs now reportedly willing to accept a reduced fee, January could represent their final opportunity to secure a transfer before his contract expires.

According to reports in Turkey (via Sport Witness), Trabzonspor have not given up on signing Richarlison and could make another attempt during the January transfer window.

It is reported that the Turkish side are considering a renewed approach, although they must first create space in their foreign-player quota.

Ruslan Malinovskyi and Paul Onuachu are among the players who could make way, with Trabzonspor's financial position and squad planning also likely to influence their decision.

Galatasaray are understood to be interested too, with both Turkish clubs working behind the scenes to explore a potential deal.

Tottenham are reportedly prepared to accept around €10m (£8.5m) in January, significantly less than the €20m (£17m) they requested during the summer. That represents a considerable reduction for a player who cost Spurs around £50m, but his situation has become increasingly difficult.

Richarlison has failed to secure a move despite interest from England, Turkey and Brazil, and De Zerbi has subsequently left him outside his core plans, with the forgotten forward restricted to involvement with the U21s.

Spurs also reportedly missed out on signing Marseille's Amine Gouiri because they were unable to offload either Richarlison or Dominic Solanke.

Richarlison's Tottenham career has become a frustrating combination of inconsistent performances, failed transfers and a breakdown in his relationship with the club.

The Brazilian has struggled to establish himself as the first-choice striker, while public disagreements over his future have further complicated matters.

He reportedly rejected the opportunity to sign a contract extension, leaving Spurs facing the prospect of losing him for nothing when his deal expires in summer 2027.

Several potential exits collapsed during the summer, including interest from former club Everton and Brazilian side Vasco da Gama, while his exclusion from De Zerbi's plans has left him in limbo.

A January departure now appears increasingly sensible for all parties. Tottenham can recover a modest fee, Richarlison can pursue regular first-team football, and De Zerbi can move on from a difficult situation.

Trabzonspor still have obstacles to overcome, but the reduced asking price could finally make an agreement possible.

#1938. Middlesbrough FC and Sheffield United's Championship rivals West Ham axe boss Nuno Espirito Santo

Sheffield United and Middlesbrough’s Championship rivals West Ham United have axed Nuno Espirito Santo from his role as head coach.

The 52-year-old took the reins at the London Stadium in September 2025 and was at the helm as the Hammers suffered relegation from the Premier League.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He was trusted to oversee their rebuild in the second tier but with the club sat eighth after 13 games, Espirito Santo has been shown the door.

A club spokesperson said: “West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team head coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect.

“Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the board of directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the Club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.

“Assistant head coach Rui Pedro Silva and goalkeeper coach Rui Barbosa have also departed.

“West Ham United would like to thank Nuno, Rui and Rui for their hard work and commitment during their time at the Club, and wish them all the very best for the future.

“The process of recruiting a new head coach is already underway. Mark Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville will take temporary charge of squad preparations ahead of tomorrow evening’s EFL Championship fixture at Cardiff City, and the club will make no further comment until the appointment of the new head coach is confirmed.”

West Ham sit just three points above 10th-placed Sheffield United and are six points adrift of table-toppers Middlesbrough.

The decision has presented a curveball to Leeds United forward Joel Piroe, who linked up with Espirito Santo’s squad in the summer.

Since sealing a loan switch from Elland Road, the 27-year-old has started six of West Ham’s 13 league games and scored three goals.

Among his teammates is winger Manor Solomon, a member of Leeds’ Championship title-winning squad in 2025.

#1937. Man Utd sent Bruno Fernandes price tag warning as big-money club prepare fresh £45m January bid

By Lewis Blain | 02 Nov 2026 08:10, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 08:10

Manchester United could face a significant decision over Bruno Fernandes' future, with Al-Hilal reportedly preparing a fresh offer for their captain in January.

However, former Chelsea striker Tony Cascarino believes Premier League clubs would be unwilling to pay £60m for the Portuguese midfielder, raising questions over his market value.

With Fernandes' contract situation unresolved and growing doubts about his future at Old Trafford, a departure next year is increasingly plausible.

Al-Hilal have revived their interest in Fernandes and are prepared to offer €55m (£45m) as early as January.

That could provide United with an opportunity to cash in on their captain, whose contract is approaching its final months, although the club reportedly have an option to extend it by another year.

Cascarino, speaking on talkSPORT's Weekend Sports Breakfast, questioned whether any Premier League side would pay up to £60m for the 32-year-old.

He acknowledged Fernandes' importance to United over several seasons but argued that his age, wages and recent form would make such a fee difficult to justify for a domestic rival.

"You might from Saudi Arabia, but you wouldn't from another Premier League team - there is no way that would happen," Cascarino said.

Fernandes' relationship with Michael Carrick has also come under scrutiny after he questioned United's pressing approach following their 4-1 defeat to Como. He was subsequently dropped to on the bench against AFC Bournemouth before returning to the starting XI against Chelsea.

Portuguese journalist Pedro Sepulveda believes the midfielder's time at Old Trafford is coming to an end.

Speaking to talkSPORT Breakfast, he suggested that a separation could benefit both Fernandes and United, arguing that the midfielder would have a better opportunity to compete for major honours at a more established club.

The signs increasingly point towards Fernandes leaving United, particularly with uncertainty over his contract and the club's continued struggles.

Al-Hilal's reported £45m interest could offer United a financially attractive solution, especially when Premier League clubs may be reluctant to match that valuation for a 32-year-old on substantial wages.

Fernandes has been an outstanding servant, regularly producing goals and assists during difficult periods, but United may need a fresh start as they look to rebuild their squad.

There is still a possibility that his contract option is activated, but that would not necessarily guarantee he remains beyond January.

Ultimately, a Saudi move could suit all parties, while Fernandes may benefit from joining a team with a clearer direction and greater immediate ambitions.

‘He understands the club, understands the fans, and knows what’s required. You don’t see that “devil” in him. But it’s there, and I have it too. We are so incredibly alike.

‘Perhaps not many people thought I would become a football coach, certainly not the manager of Manchester United. Many probably thought the same about Michael Carrick.

‘When I spoke with United, I also spoke highly of Michael. “If you choose him, you’re getting a good man,” I said. I believe he did the same for me.

‘Neither of us was desperate to get the job. But we’d likely step up if they asked.’

Solskjaer spoke to Manchester United chiefs Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada following Ruben Amorim’s sacking at the start of the year and confirmed he ‘offered’ to return to the club.

The offer came after club legend Solskjaer’s three-year spell in charge of the Red Devils which ended in 2021.

‘I had a good chat with Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada,’ Solskjaer said. ‘We didn’t discuss contract length or anything of the sort.

‘I offered to step in if needed, and I made no demands. I shared my thoughts on what is required for the club to move forward. We had one brief conversation. There were no negotiations.’

Reflecting on his time in charge of Manchester United, Solskjaer added: ‘There were some fantastic moments, but everything has its time.

‘I do miss it, yes. I could have imagined staying there forever, but life goes on. It was a very special period. Of course it was.

‘It was special in many ways. Going back to the past isn’t always a good idea. Yes, I would have stepped in [in January], but I didn’t intend for it to last beyond the summer.

‘It was probably time for someone else to have a go. I also feel like I have some unfinished business. Naturally, it would have been fun to have the opportunity again.’

Manchester United play host to Roma sitting 20th in the Champions League, while the Italians are 15th with one win, one draw and one defeat from their opening three games.

#1933. England squad announcement: When will Thomas Tuchel confirm squad for November international break?

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 08:34, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 08:38

Thomas Tuchel’s England are back in action this month as they resume their 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign.

After finishing third at this summer’s World Cup, the Three Lions won three of their opening four League A Group C fixtures across an 11-day period during the September/October international break.

England responded to their matchday one defeat at home to world champions Spain (3-2) by smashing Croatia 7-0 in between two more victories without reply against the Czech Republic.

With two more games on the horizon, Sports Mole runs through everything you need to know about England's latest squad announcement.

Tuchel will announce his England squad ahead of the upcoming international break at 10am on Friday, November 6.

The Three Lions boss is then expected to hold a press conference on the same day to explain the decisions he has made.

A 27-man squad was initially named by Tuchel in September, though a number of high-profile names eventually pulled out.

Six days after Tuchel's squad announcement, England will welcome Croatia to Wembley Stadium for their penultimate League A Group C fixture at 7.45pm on November 12.

The Three Lions will conclude their Nations League group with a trip to Riyadh Air Metropolitano – Atletico Madrid’s home stadium – where they will face Spain at 7.45pm (GMT) on November 15.

England currently sit second in League A Group C with nine points from their opening four matches, three behind leaders Spain who boast a 100% record.

The Three Lions also sit six points clear ahead of Croatia in third and know that either a draw or victory against the Checkered Ones would guarantee a top-two finish in the group.

The top-two teams in all four groups in League A will progress to the quarter-finals; Spain have already qualified with two games to spare but could still be pipped to top spot by England.

Group winners are seeded for the quarter-final draw, meaning they will be drawn against a runner-up from another group and will also host the second leg of their two-legged tie.

Meanwhile, England captain Harry Kane is set to return to international action for the first time since winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or.

Already the nation's all-time top scorer with 91 goals, Kane will aim to surpass Peter Shilton (125) to become England's most-capped men’s player in history.

#1932. Roma boss sends warning to Manchester United after record-breaking start to season

Manchester United face a Roma team on Tuesday night that has had a blistering, record-breaking start to the Serie A season in terms of goals.

Gian Piero Gasperini’s side won 5-2 at Udinese on Saturday to continue their fine form which sees them unbeaten in 10 games at the start of the Serie A campaign.

In those 10 fixtures they have scored 28 goals, which is more than they had ever previously managed by this stage of the season.

‘Sometimes the numbers do tell you the story,’ he said after the dominant win at Udinese. ‘Besides scoring lots of goals, we’re also scoring with many different players.

‘That shows how much confidence there is in the team: lots of players believe they can make a decisive contribution, be it with an assist or a goal. We’re scoring more goals with more players and that’s a great sign.’

#1930. Arsenal, Liverpool and Man Utd phone £50m midfielder over stunning transfer

Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United have reportedly made contact with Lennart Karl to gauge whether the attacking midfielder would be interested in a move to England.

Karl, 18, broke into Bayern’s first-team squad in early 2025 and has gone on to establish himself as one of the brightest young talents in German football.

In that time, Karl has made a total of 52 appearances in all competitions for Bayern while helping the club win the Bundesliga, the German Cup and the German Super Cup.

However, in a recent interview, Bayern’s honorary president Uli Hoeness questioned Karl’s social media activity and suggested the teenager still had a long way to go before he could be considered a ‘superstar’- raising some doubts over the youngster’s future at the Allianz Arena.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

‘He’s far from being a superstar,’ Hoeness said of Karl.

‘Young players need humility. Comparisons with Michael Olise obviously don’t do him any good.

‘There’s still a world of difference between them.’

According to Bild, Hoeness’ remarks have caused a level of ‘unrest’ within Karl’s camp, and Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United have been alerted to a potential deal.

It’s claimed the three Premier League giants have all made contact with Karl over the phone to discuss the Germany international’s current situation.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The report adds that while it is not Bayern’s intention to force out Karl, an offer in the region of €60million (£50m) from a potential suitor could be enough to prise the diminutive midfielder away from Munich.

Karl’s contract with the reigning Bundesliga champions runs through to June 2029.

Michael Ballack, who represents Karl with the Lucky 13 agency, was less than impressed by Hoeness’ comments, jumping to the defence of his client’s presence on social media.

‘Lennart is only 18. Where were you at 18? Just as he is trying things out on the pitch, he is doing the same off it,’ the former Bayern and Chelsea midfielder told DAZN.

‘Social media is a major factor today, and not just for the younger generation. Everyone is free to present themselves as they wish.

‘Of course, they will not get everything right. Unfortunately, condemnation is inevitable.’

Ballack added: ‘It is legitimate for Uli Hoeness to criticise how Lennart presents himself publicly.

‘But it is also clear that, in doing so, he is making Lennart a public target.’

Karl has started just three of Bayern’s eight matches in the Bundesliga so far this season.

He was sent on in the 84th minute on Saturday as Vincent Kompany’s men were held to a 2-2 draw at home to fierce rivals Borussia Dortmund.

#1928. Erik ten Hag doubles down on Cristiano Ronaldo criticism with fresh attack

Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has come out swinging for Cristiano Ronaldo again, doubling down on recent criticism of the iconic forward.

Ronaldo returned to Old Trafford in 2021 for his second stint with Manchester United, before Ten Hag took charge as manager in the summer of 2022.

The relationship between the manager and the star striker did not blossom and in November 2022 Ronaldo’s contract was terminated after he criticised the boss and the club as a whole.

The Portuguese superstar moved to Saudi Arabia while Ten Hag would remain in charge of the Red Devils until his dismissal in October 2024.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The Dutchman had not said a great deal in the two years since then, but has now sprung into life with criticism of Ronaldo.

Speaking to The Athletic last month of their time together, Ten Hag said: ‘Many times I say, “Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score”.

‘He was not capable to do this. It’s the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he’s exhausted. But he couldn’t. He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn’t prepare himself.

‘Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team.

‘He was telling the players, “save your legs at the training”. I understand it when you are top fit; you have sessions, you can save the legs. But first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Ten Hag has gone for the 41-year-old again, leveling the same criticisms at him, but going even further.

The former Ajax boss says Ronaldo was not just off the pace at Manchester United, but his time at the top of the game was over when he left Real Madrid for Juventus in 2018.

‘He belongs among the greats of the world. But the reality is also that he hasn’t been able to deliver for the last seven or eight years. From Juventus onwards, it was simply over,’ Ten Hag told ESPN.

‘He couldn’t bring himself to torture himself anymore. To give it his all every day. To get fit. If you aren’t fit in the Premier League, you stand no chance. He can still finish chances. You can still see that. But if you can’t get into the penalty area anymore…’

He added: ‘Ultimately, the choice was up to him. Whether he wants to make that investment. If he doesn’t want to, I have to make other choices in the interest of the club. We have seen that.’

#1927. Slavia Prague vs Arsenal - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Knapton | 02 Nov 2026 09:52, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 14:17

An Arsenal team yet to suffer defeat in the 2026-27 Champions League league phase take on a Slavia Prague side still searching for their first triumph of the tournament at the Fortuna Arena on Wednesday evening.

The Gunners have collected seven points from the first nine on offer in Europe, whereas their Czech hosts have just one draw and two defeats to show from their opening three fixtures.

No longer perfect points-wise or rearguard-wise in the Champions League, Arsenal ventured to Bayern Munich on matchday three as the only team in the UCL yet to concede a goal, having shut out Lille and Napoli in the opening two rounds.

However, the Premier League champions still went toe to toe with their Bavarian counterparts and came away with a hard-earned point from an enthralling 2-2 draw with Bayern, replicating an incredibly rare and eerie feat in the process.

The four-goal stalemate marked just the second time that Arsenal had scored first, fallen behind and still managed to avoid defeat in a European Cup/Champions League fixture, after an identical result against none other than Bayern in 2024.

While Arsenal's 14-game winning sequence in the league phase may now be a thing of the past, the Gunners remain in the coveted top eight spots of the league-phase table, and two goals conceded still makes them the joint-best defensive side in the competition, alongside Stuttgart and PSV Eindhoven.

The elusive quadruple remains a pipe dream after their embarrassing EFL Cup exit to Fleetwood Town, but Mikel Arteta got the seismic response he was hoping for on Sunday, overseeing a long-awaited Premier League victory at Anfield.

Arsenal's 1-0 win over Liverpool - their first in the top flight away to the Reds in 14 years - took them three points clear at the top of the Premier League table, and highlighted the gap that remains between the champions and their challengers.

Involved in their own frenetic four-goal draw on matchday three - albeit in differing circumstances - Slavia Prague put their first Champions League point on the board courtesy of coming from 2-0 down to hold Fenerbahce in Istanbul.

Jindrich Trpisovsky's men may have feared a hiding when Oguz Aydin and Mason Greenwood struck inside the opening 11 minutes, but Lukas Provod swiftly cut the deficit in half before Pavel Kacor's 90th-minute leveller ended their European losing sequence.

Slavia had fallen to Lens and Sabah in their opening two fixtures, but their gritty draw at Fenerbahce was not enough to lift them out of the automatic elimination places, as Wednesday's hosts lie 32nd in the 36-team rankings after three matchdays.

The Red and Whites have also now failed to win in a staggering 18 consecutive UEFA fixtures - coincidentally the same length as Arsenal's unbeaten UCL run, excluding penalties - but Trpisovsky's crop have found form again at an ideal time.

Indeed, Slavia Prague have now strung together a five-game unbeaten run in all tournaments and have won back-to-back fixtures, most recently demolishing Jablonec 5-0 to maintain a seven-point lead at the top of the Czech First League table.

However, the reigning national champions were swept aside 3-0 by Arsenal at home in the 2025-26 league phase and have failed to win any of their previous five head-to-heads against the Gunners, whose 7-0 thumping of Slavia in 2007 remains their joint-biggest victory in European football.

Arsenal quartet Christos Tzolis, Declan Rice, Noni Madueke and Riccardo Calafiori all battled back from injury concerns to make the trip to Anfield, but Bukayo Saka (quad) and William Saliba (back) remain absent.

Eberechi Eze is also a fresh concern after Arteta revealed that the Englishman is dealing with an unspecified fitness problem, but Max Dowman - serving a three-game domestic suspension - is available here.

Given Eze's concern, Tzolis's fast-tracked comeback and Madueke's recent ankle scare, it would not be a shock to see Dowman start on Wednesday evening, as Arteta makes a handful of alterations across the park.

Meanwhile, Slavia have a handful of fitness concerns to take into account for the visit of Arsenal, including experienced winger Ivan Schranz, who has been laid low by an illness for weeks.

Star attacker Lukas Provod also missed the thrashing of Jablonec and is a doubt, as is defender Ange N'Guessan, who came off with an unspecified injury last time out.

From injuries to suspensions, 6ft 7in striker Tomas Chory has been banished by manager Trpisovsky after showing a referee the middle finger during a recent Czech First League fixture against Hradec Kralove; he is not expected to play for the club again.

Domchak; Vlcek, Holes, Zima; Suleiman, Moses, Sadilek, Kubiak; Ayaosi, Sturm; Nowak

Raya; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Lewis-Skelly, Rice; Dowman, Odegaard, Eze; Gyokeres

After Arsenal's second-string team failed to beat a fourth-tier side in the EFL Cup, Arteta should resist the urge to make wholesale changes against a Slavia side whose momentum is growing.

Nevertheless, the Czech champions have been carved open at will in Europe - shipping seven goals thus far - so we can envisage Arsenal replicating their three-goal success from last season.

Mikel Arteta’s side trailed early pace-setters Manchester City just two weeks ago but the Etihad club have suffered two successive defeats while Arsenal’s only dropped points came at the hands of Brighton.

Liverpool had the chance to climb back into the Champions League spots and move to within just three points of Arsenal but a second league defeat of the season leaves the Reds fifth.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Speaking after the full-time whistle was blown, Neville added: ‘It was a defensive masterclass from Arsenal.

‘Andoni Iraola will be upset, he will feel like his team have given everything, but the champions have turned up in a season of uncertainty, sabotaged by the Man City saga.

‘They can only do the job they continue to do and that puts them right in the driving seat.

‘Those Arsenal fans will travel back to London tonight absolutely over the moon. What a tough place this is to play football and they’ve come and conquered it.’

Arsenal and Liverpool are both in Champions League action this week, the former visiting Slavia Prague and the latter travelling to Fenerbahce.

#1923. City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier  League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

Lavelli blasts his shot down the middle, and Inter have won the Asahi Trophy!

The teenager sizes things up, and sends Donnarumma the other way.

A stuttering run, and Provedel beats it away.

Frattesi misses! Donnarumma stretches out and flings up his left arm for a great save.

Khusanov misses, firmly striking against the post.

Donnarumma dives to the right, the shot in the opposite direction.

Rayan Ait-Nouri misses! Spooned over the bar.

We’re onto the penalty shootout. The pressure builds for the Asahi Trophy.

Echeverri is fouled in midfield, he takes it quickly, but the move breaks down and Inter get back into position again. The end nears.

Three more minutes of this have been indicated.

Gonzalez finds McAidoo, and City look for room on the right. Inter sit back and stay compact.

The game has slowed to a near-halt. It seems everyone is resigned to penalties.

Ait-Nouri finds McAidoo’s run to the back post with a fabulous low cross, but the winger’s return ball is cut out by Provedel.

If McAidoo does not stay on at City for the season ahead, you’d expect plenty of sides to be looking to bring him in on loan.

Ait-Nouri is offside as he takes the ball on the left wing, and Inter have it back briefly.

McAidoo yet again gets forward and almost forces a cross past Provedel. The ball comes back to Sangare, but his effort is blocked. City are getting closer.

Khusanov is booked for a foul in midfield, and then is on hand to block a shot on the line as Inter fail to convert.

McAidoo, yet again. A shot to the far post, yet again. A miss, yet again. He looks dangerous though.

McAidoo repeats the trick, but this time he keeps his shot low and hits the bottom of the far post. The best moment of the half so far.

However, with the scores still level, it’s only 10 minutes from a penalty shootout.

McAidoo scoots into the box from the right and curls a shot wide of the far post.

Enzo makes another change 🔄 pic.twitter.com/afvwMFYlB9

Savinho slices a shot wildly high and wide. Changes are coming.

Reis claims to meet a corner at the back post, but it comes off an Inter player. The corner switches to the right, and this one is cleared, for now. City keep the ball and Ait-Nouri picks out Gonzalez’s run, and he strains to shin it over.

Lewis has the ball in the box after quick feet from Savinho with the assist, and he prods the ball at Provedel.

Foden and Semenyo off, Sangare and Echeverri on. Lewis is City’s new captain.

Foden sends in a corner, and Reis hooks a volley against the bar as the ball drops. Gonzalez gets back up to his feet slowly after that phase of play, and then sits back down as he awaits treatment.

City are camped in Inter’s half now, which is an improvement on the last half where it was more even, territorially.

McAidoo is released down the inside left, he clears his marker and aims for Semenyo, but Bisseck clears for a corner.

Pavard goes down after he is caught late from Ait-Nouri, but he’s fine to continue.

More subs now  Topalovic replaces Stankovic. Provedel replaces Martinez in goal.

Savinho might be the most dangerous player for City today, a sentence that has rarely been true in the last couple of years. McAidoo whips in a cross, which Henrique clears under no pressure.

Reis and Alleyne are the central defenders. Ait-Nouri is on the left, and Khusanov the right.

Stankovic gets a yellow as Savinho sprints down the inside left away from Inter Milan players. McAidoo is then tripped by Augusto, who hurt himself doing so.

A decent enough corner from Foden who swings the ball close to the back post, but the goalkeeper Martinez is fouled as the ball comes in.

The full slate of City changes, as Lewis has a shot blocked when a corner is not properly cleared. Savinho stands a cross up, but it comes to nothing. Khusanov has a shot scrambled away.

Frattesi, Henrique, Mosconi, Zielinski and Bastoni are the five Inter introductions, but there are more. Mkhitrayan has gone off, with Diouf, Idrrissou, and Augusto some of the exits too.

We go again. A billion subs have been made. So far, Frattesi is on. Let’s see what we know about the rest. Ait-Nouri is on.

It’s been more or less what you expect from a pre-season friendly in the humidity.

The players are yet to shake off their summer ice creams and really get sharp again, but there are some flashes of ability here and there.

Reijnders releases Semenyo, the Dutchman plays the ball into Savinho, who dances to the byline, pulls it back, but it’s then cleared from Bisseck.

That’s it for the half, and the action restarts in 15 minutes.

Savinho wriggles into the box but just fails to find Semenyo.

Mkhitaryan concedes a foul on Lewis in midfeild, and the half appears to be drifting to a bloodless close.

Savinho, maybe in his last game for City, brings the ball high up the right but then City are forced all the way back to Donnarumma.

City are not panicked by keeping the ball, and they look for a fresh opening.

Foden commits his own foul in midfield, this time on Mkhitaryan. There are a few minutes left before half-time, at which point we may see a few changes from both sides given the early stage of pre-season.

Foden swings in a corner that Savinho briefly keeps alive before Diouf clears, and Dimarco cannot quite reach the ball before it’s played back to Donnarumma.

Barella fouls Reijnders in midfield, but it’s nothing vicious.

Semenyo clips in a dangerous-looking cross from the left wing, but it’s deflected behind for a corner on the right.

Foden is tugged down in midfield, with the City man still failing to show much of his talent in the new season.

Mkhitaryan continues to find space in pockets on the left. In general, Inter are finding it very easy to trundle to the edge of the City box.

Donnarumma flaps at a cross, and Savinho and Lewis work to clear it momentarily.

Do you think the players are coping without a hydration break?

Dimarco is fed by Diouf, with the right wing-back finding the left wing-back. He’s on the right side of the pitch too, oddly, but his left-footed shot is far from dreadful, but easily stopped by Donnarumma.

City have some pressure and Kovacic hits a group of defenders with a volley from outside the box. It’s meek stuff from Maresca’s men so far but obviously, too early to draw much from it.

City are looking to build from the back through the middle, but they are quickly crowded out. Inter come forward once more.

Diouf forces a corner on the right wing as Donnarumma clears a cross. It’s taken short, Inter switch the ball left, but Mkhitaryan overhits a pass to the byline.

Mkhitaryan receives the ball on the left, inside the box, in another dangerous position. Lewis had drifted  too far inside, but the danger passes when the forward is flagged offside.

Inter are keeping the ball calmly at the back, finding spaces between the pressing City attackers.

They break through and Donnarumma beats away a low shot from Stankovic.

Benjmain Pavard scores! Manchester City fail to clear their lines and Pavard, who started the move, is on hope to finish with the keeper stricken.

Divin Mubamba gets the opener! Semenyo beats his right-bacck and crosses to the six-yard box for Mubamba to tap in.

14. Wonderful work from Semenyo 👊He beats his man on the left to get to the byline, squares it across goal and Divin converts from close range 🎯🐝 1-0 ⚪️ https://t.co/pCDrkfriLY

Dimarco volleys wide but he too was offside, and then Martinez saves from Reijnders at the other end. It’s a free-flowing match so far.

Stankovic goes close with an early header after Inter win their first corner of the match. It’s an open game so far.

City win two early corners, but they are both cleared. A bright start for the Premier League side. Esposito then goes close at the other end, but he was offside anyway.

A recent on-pitch spat over the captain’s armband between Liverpool players demonstrated that these friendlies are not simply warm-ups.

In their little costumes ahead of kick-off.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester City and Inter Milan.

The two sides meet  at Kai Tak Sports Park, Hong  Kong as their pre-season work kicks up a gear ahead of the new campaign.

City are still getting used to life without Pep Guardiola, the coach who left after a decade of high spending and high performance.

In his place is Enzo Maresca, who is not shy with the chequebook himself.

Ayyoub Bouaddi, the outstanding 18-year-old Moroccan international, should soon arrive from Lille when a fee is agreed, but Elliot Anderson and Jeremy Monga have already been signed.

City were runners-up last season, so Maresca is under pressure not just to keep things going without Guardiola, but to get the team back to the top of English football. That looks to be a tough prospect with Arsenal likely to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle in the coming days.

Inter, meanwhile, have swooped to pick up John Stones on a free transfer after his contract ended at the Etihad Stadium, and he is joined by Manuel Akanji, another former City centre-back whose loan turned permanent in the summer.

Inter won Serie A last season under head coach Cristian Chivu, and they are still one of the best sides in Europe.

While this friendly is likely to be played at a reduced pace, and will be disrupted by rustiness and substitutes, we could still learn a lot about both sides going into the new campaign, and there may be the odd surprise thrown up by a young player looking to stake a claim ahead of his senior colleagues this year.

#1922. ‘Best in the league’ – Jamie Carragher hails Declan Rice after Arsenal beat Liverpool

Jamie Carragher hailed Declan Rice as the ‘best midfielder in the country by a long way’ after Arsenal’s hard-fought win over Liverpool.

Kai Havertz scored the only goal at Anfield, tapping in at the back-post from Rice’s brilliant pass across goal.

Both teams had chances to score after Havertz’s opener but the game finished 1-0 as Arsenal moved three points clear at the top of the Premier League and Liverpool failed to climb back into the Champions League spots.

Rice was named Player of the Match after Arsenal’s battling victory and Carragher agreed with that decision, hailing him as not only the best midfielder in the Premier League but one of the greatest in the club’s history.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

‘He’s the best midfield player in the Premier League by a long way. It’s not even a debate,’ Carragher said on Sky Sports.

‘Declan Rice is the best midfield player in this country. I’m not an Arsenal fan, but sometimes I hear people speak about him.

‘And I’m sort of flabbergasted that they don’t understand football and they’re not watching the same game as me.

‘He’s a world-class midfield player. There’s absolutely no doubt about it. One of the best midfield players Arsenal have ever had.

‘They’ve had some obviously great ones. He’s right up there with the best of them.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Discussing the match at Anfield more generally, Carragher added: ‘It was a brilliant game and both teams can take a lot from it.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Liverpool played really well. They didn’t do enough but you are playing against, defensively, the best team in this country, arguably in Europe and that is without the best centre-back in the world in William Saliba.

‘When you think about Arsenal winning titles, especially in ’89 and ’91 with Tony Adams and that famous back four, I think we’re getting close to putting this back four up against that and in that conversation.

‘To come to Anfield and be put under that much pressure and not have a shot on target from the opposition, or Liverpool not to have a big chance given the money they’ve spent on their attack is absolutely outstanding.’

"That togetherness we have is undefeated" 💪Declan Rice reacts after Arsenal's monumental win at Anfield. pic.twitter.com/4r7tm77axM

Meanwhile, Rice revealed after the win that Mikel Arteta had challenged him to contribute even more to the title holders this season.

‘The manager had a really honest conversation with me at the start of the season and still thinks that I can do more in this shirt and for this club,’ Rice said.

‘And this season so far I’ve been feeling really good. We spoke about overlaps before the game.

‘I spoke to this guy [Havertz] about attacking the box with real aggression. He was there, and he nearly could have had another one with the same action. So I’m so happy for him because he deserved that goal today.

‘It’s always tiring and tough coming here. It’s my first win here as a player, so it’s demanding.’

Arteta was full of praise for his Arsenal players after they left Anfield with all three points for the first time in 14 years, describing the performance as ‘incredible’.

‘This was especially for everyone attached to this football club,’ Arteta said. ‘Fourteen years without winning here is a long time.

‘We just said after the last few days, after the defeat against Fleetwood, that things happen for a reason and that’s going to give us another spring and hunger and belief to go and do it.

‘What the team has done here today is incredible. To come here and win in the manner that we have done, I think the players deserve so much credit.’

#1921. Barnsley FC boss Daniel Stendel outlines Daniel Johnson plan after ex-Stoke City playmaker's debut

Barnsley head coach Daniel Stendel is hoping to have Daniel Johnson ready to start games in the coming weeks.

The 34-year-old arrived at Oakwell last month, penning a deal running until the end of the season after a spell on the free agent market.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He has had to be patient, but the attacking midfielder was introduced for his debut from the bench as Barnsley drew 1-1 with Oxford United on Saturday (October 31).

The outing was his first in a competitive fixture since March, when he played his final game for Turkish outfit Fatih Karagümrük.

“I think it’s really important [to give him minutes],” Stendel told The Yorkshire Post. “I don't know when he played the last game, but about his experience, his quality, we decided we'd take him in the squad.

“We have this game, nobody knows it before, but I think you can see in some little situations that he has the calmness to keep the ball, to find the right decisions, and I'm really happy that he's back in the squad and it's his first time today on the pitch, and I hope we can build him up in the next couple of days.

“Next week, maybe, he can play some more minutes that he can build up to start maybe in two weeks.”

A product of Aston Villa’s academy, Johnson left Villa Park to enjoy a memorable eight-year spell at Preston North End. Between 2015 and 2023, he racked up 336 appearances for the Lilywhites and developed a habit of tormenting the Reds.

A season with Stoke City followed before the Jamaica international moved to Turkey.

“I think we talk about this with everyone in the club, that we decided to work with so many young players in the past,” said Stendel. “But for some situations, especially for the situation that we have at the moment, we need experienced players who know a little bit what can happen.

“It's a good chance for the younger guys to look after him and take a little bit of confidence from him to play their best game.”

#1920. Alexis Mac Allister branded a ‘joke’ by Liverpool legend for Arsenal antics

Alexis Mac Allister’s attempts to get Noni Madueke sent off during Liverpool’s defeat to Arsenal have been branded a ‘joke’ and ’embarrassing’ by Reds legend Jamie Carragher.

Kai Havertz scored the only goal of the game at Anfield as the Gunners moved to the top of the Premier League table and Liverpool stayed fifth.

Andoni Iraola’s team had more possession, xG and shots than the visitors, but did not get a single one of their efforts on target.

As the home side pushed for an equaliser late on, tempers flared thanks to Mac Allister who sparked a dust-up.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard went down after a challenge with the Argentine, with Mac Allister then shouting something at the felled Norwegian before slapping him on the back of the head.

Jurrien Timber took umbrage with that and Madueke then got involved, squaring up to the Liverpool star and as their heads briefly met, Mac Allister went down holding his forehead.

Clearly it was an attempt to get the Gunners winger sent off, but neither the referee nor VAR were buying it and Madueke avoided any punishment.

Carragher made his feelings very clear on Mac Allister’s action, calling the World Cup winner ’embarrassing’ for his ‘joke’ of a response to the coming together.

‘I’m delighted he never got sent off there. We have got to be strong on calling people out and saying that this is embarrassing. I cant stand it,’ Carragher told Sky Sports.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I think everybody in the country watching football this head-to-head stuff. If someone puts their head back and butts, or course red card, but this stuff about head-to-head and if someone touches, the other one goes down and the payer gets sent off.

‘As a game, as football, people in the Premier League, supporters, call your own people out for it.

‘I’m a Liverpool fan, that’s a joke from Mac Allister but it’s got to stop. People are trying to gain an advantage because they know they can because red cards are getting given for it.

‘Whether it’s from Howard Webb, the Premier League, the managers get together. This has got to stop. Stop getting red cards for this crap!’

A social media post from the Premier League Match Centre confirmed why there was no action taken against Madueke.

It read: ‘The referee’s call of no violent conduct by Madueke on Mac Allister was checked and confirmed by VAR.

‘VAR: “All of the situations have been checked and cleared. There is some contact as Madueke and Mac Allister square-up. In my opinion, it’s not forceful, not violent, not brutal.”‘

"You're supposed to make something of it!""That's obvious that he's pulled his shirt, why does he need to dive?"Ian Wright and Daniel Sturridge discuss Alexander Isak's penalty appeal 💬 pic.twitter.com/G0aa7tP92t

The officials did not get so much praise for failing to give a penalty to Liverpool in the first half when Timber pulled Alexander Isak’s shirt as the Swede jumped for a header.

Iraola told Sky Sports: ‘The Alex Isak one is a clear penalty. You hold the t-shirt; we can all see that he holds the t-shirt.

‘The ball just goes one centimetre in front of Alex. Alex is going to hit the ball in front of the goal.’

Asked if Isak should have made more of the incident to make it clear he was fouled, the Spaniard said: ‘The fact that you are even asking me that he should have gone to the floor, that’s the thing. If he goes to the floor, they call the penalty for me. They call the penalty 100 per cent.’

#1919. Arsenal predicted lineup vs. Slavia Prague: Max Dowman starts as Bruno Guimaraes dropped

By Ben Knapton | 02 Nov 2026 10:03

Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman could be restored to the starting XI when the Gunners take on Slavia Prague in Wednesday's Champions League league-phase fixture.

The 16-year-old is currently serving a three-game domestic suspension for his sending-off at Fleetwood Town in the EFL Cup, but he is fine to feature in Europe, and his return is especially timely from a fitness perspective.

Bukayo Saka (quad) is out for several weeks, Christos Tzolis has only just returned from a hamstring injury, Eberechi Eze is a fresh concern, and Noni Madueke was dealing with an ankle problem before Sunday's 1-0 Premier League win at Liverpool.

As a result, a refreshed Dowman is in a strong position to start at the Fortuna Arena in place of Madueke, who completed the full 90 at Anfield and should now be spared for the weekend's Premier League clash with Hull City.

Mikel Arteta admitted that it was "incredible" that Eze managed to make the squad at the weekend, but as the Englishman was fit to make the bench and Tzolis played over 80 minutes after his recent return, the former could also be restored on the left.

Skipper Martin Odegaard may be the only member of Sunday's front four to hold their position, as Viktor Gyokeres for Kai Havertz could be a straight swap with fitness levels in mind.

Arteta may be hesitant to start both Myles Lewis-Skelly and Martin Zubimendi after the horror show at Fleetwood, but the former is still in line to displace Bruno Guimaraes, whose partnership with Declan Rice is yet to blossom.

#1918. Freddie Ljungberg says Man Utd star made him ‘feel sick’ in Chelsea defeat

Arsenal legend Freddie Ljungberg has taken aim at Lisandro Martinez following Manchester United’s 2-0 loss to Chelsea, claiming the defender made him ‘feel a bit sick’ with his behaviour.

Michael Carrick’s future at United was plunged into further doubt on Saturday as his side’s miserable winless streak extended to nine matches in all competitions with defeat at Stamford Bridge.

Morgan Rogers broke the deadlock just five minutes into the second half before a quickfire pair of yellow cards for Martinez left the visitors with only ten men on the field.

Cole Palmer made no mistake with the penalty awarded after Martinez’s second foul and the Blues held firm with their man advantage to pick up their fifth win of the Premier League campaign.

The result propelled Xabi Alonso’s men up into fourth place, while the Red Devils sit above the relegation only on goal difference ahead of another tough clash at home to Aston Villa next weekend.

Prior to the match, widespread reports indicated Carrick would be given the chance to fight for his future and turn United’s fortunes around after their disastrous start to the season.

But the club’s latest setback has heaped yet more pressure on an increasingly dejected-looking Carrick and in his post-match analysis for Viaplay, Arsenal Invincible Ljungberg took the opportunity to lambast Martinez for ‘letting his manager down’ again.

‘I feel, when I look at that, I feel sorry for Michael Carrick,’ Ljungberg said.

‘Everybody is slaughtering Carrick in the media and stuff, “Is he good enough as a coach, this and that”, the players are not doing it.

‘How they behave, Martinez doing what he did, I was there and I felt a bit sick.

Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel echoed Ljungberg’s takedown of Martinez, suggesting the Argentine’s conduct both on and off the pitch was simply ‘not good enough’.

‘He has cost so many goals and that is one of the issues with Manchester United, that they’re leaking goals for fun,’ the great Dane explained.

‘If you’re a big player, you played in a World Cup final, you just can’t perform like that, come out with statements like that [after the Atletico Madrid match], and then perform like he did against Chelsea.

Martinez’s sending off against Chelsea means he will be suspended for United’s upcoming encounter with Villa.

According to ex-Liverpool midfielder Danny Murphy, there is a high chance the World Cup-winning defender will never play again under Carrick.

Asked if the term ‘liability’ was perhaps too strong a word to describe Martinez on Saturday night’s Match of the Day programme, ex-Liverpool and Tottenham midfielder Murphy replied: ‘It’s getting that way. A player of that experience and quality, he knows better.‘There’s something obviously not right at the moment in his head, he’s in a different space, because you don’t see the poor performances for a player of that quality.

‘There was the Dominic Solanke issue last week [against Tottenham] and then there was the interview, rant, whatever you want to call it and then today, his performance in the second half was just nowhere near it.

‘To go and do that after you’ve just had a yellow… I don’t know whether he’s thinking of getting away, whether he’s disgruntled at everything going on around the club, but he’s given Carrick a really big dilemma now.

‘When he’s served the suspension, I think it’s unlikely that Michael, if he’s still the manager, is going to put him back in.’

Before their next top-flight clash, United will look to stop the rot when they return to Champions League action at home to Roma.

In his post-match interview with TNT Sports on Saturday, Carrick said he expected to remain in charge for the group-stage contest.

Asked by TNT Sports if he expected to be in the dugout at the Theatre of Dreams, Carrick said: ‘Yeah.’

When pressed further on his future during his post-match press conference, the United head coach said: ‘I’m just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek now.’

#1916. Piero Hincapie aims dig at Liverpool captain after Arsenal win at Anfield

Piero Hincapie has gone very niche with a dig at Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk after the Gunners won at Anfield on Sunday.

Kai Havertz scored the only goal of an entertaining game on Merseyside as Mikel Arteta’s side climbed to the top of the Premier League table and the Reds remained fifth.

Despite there only being one goal and Liverpool not managing a shot on target, it was a great match with plenty of incident, including Alexis Mac Allister trying to get Noni Madueke sent off and being branded ’embarrassing’ by Jamie Carragher as a result.

There was clearly an edge to the match at times and that continued after the final whistle as Hincapie posted on Instagram.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

It will not have been clear to all what he meant when he posted three pictures from the match with the caption: ‘I don’t forget…’

The third and final picture was a close up of the gold Premier League badge on the sleeve of Arsenal’s kit.

The gold logo is only worn by the defending champions in a Premier League season.

It was a response to Van Dijk doing the same in January after a goalless draw between Arsenal and Liverpool at the Emirates.

The Reds were defending champions at the time and the iconic centre-back was thought to be quietly reminding the north Londoners of that.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Hincapie certainly saw it that way and has reminded the Liverpool great who are the champions right now.

It is still very early in the season but Arsenal look in a very strong position to lift the Premier League title again, moving three points clear of Manchester City thanks to an eighth win in nine league games.

The Gunners’ defence continues to be the source of their strength, with just five goals conceded in nine Premier League outings, three of which came in their one defeat to Brighton.

Liverpool were very competitive in the match, but could not produce a single shot on target, with Arteta crediting his entire team for the work they do defensively.

‘I didn’t know about that statistic but that’s incredible,’ he said of goalkeeper David Raya not having to make one save.

‘It didn’t feel like this to be fair on the pitch because there were very little margins sometimes when they had the opportunity to shoot and it’s a team that shoots a lot.

‘You have to be so good at blocking shots and preventing those spaces for them to get into there. Again, it’s a commitment of every single player in every action consistently to deliver those kind of stats and to do it against this team, it’s something remarkable I would say.’
