#1914. Gary Neville speaks out on ‘remarkable’ Lisandro Martinez performances

Gary Neville says he would be ‘curled up in a ball’ if he was playing as badly as Lisandro Martinez is and certainly not pointing fingers at other people in interviews.

The Argentina international has been in dreadful form this season, much like most of his teammates, and was at fault again in the 2-0 defeat to Chelsea on Saturday.

The 28-year-old did little to prevent Morgan Rogers’ opener at Stamford Bridge and then picked up a second yellow card for a ridiculous challenge in the penalty area, which saw Cole Palmer convert from the spot.

It was a calamitous afternoon for Martinez after Manchester United had looked quite impressive in the first half, before falling apart after the break.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Neville had a damning assessment of the defender, saying he was not surprised at all to see him let his team down.

Martinez spoke out against the Manchester United hierarchy last month, criticising the lack of investment in the squad, but Neville thinks the Argentine is in no position to make such comments.

‘That’s what I expect from him, to be honest with you, that’s what I see,’ Neville told Sky Sports of Martinez’s performance at Chelsea.

‘I said the other week – and you’ve got to respect hat he is a World Cup winner – but every time I watch him for Manchester United he is at fault for a goal and he was at fault for two yesterday. The first goal is solely on him. I know the midfield could do better, but Harry Maguire has to go and watch that run and he has to come across.

‘If I was giving away the goals that he is giving away, I wouldn’t be doing interviews. And to be fair, I wouldn’t be speaking out, because I have to say, I would be curled up in a ball, if I was playing like that for Manchester United.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘We all give goals away as defenders, but the quantity of goals he gives away is remarkable. And that defence is just nowhere near good enough and it falls apart every time it is put under big pressure and it did do in the second half.’

Martinez has been a mainstay in the heart of Michael Carrick’s defence, but will now serve a suspension and may not return to the side.

Carrick does have options, with the likes of Matthijs de Ligt and Ayden Heaven on the bench at Stamford Bridge, while Noussair Mazraoui is also an option, with Leny Yoro playing at right-back against Chelsea.

Former Liverpool and England midfielder Danny Murphy said Martinez should be out of contention after becoming a liability.

‘Lisandro Martinez has got a lot to answer to, because the first goal was mainly his fault. The sending-off is absolutely ridiculous,’ Murphy said on BBC Radio 5 Live.

‘Obviously, he is going to apologise in the dressing room, but his mindset is not right to play. You can’t rely on him. He is a liability.’

On whether he would pick the defender again, Murphy said: ‘No, I wouldn’t, only because he looks like he has already gone. His head isn’t right. He is not going to be there long term, that is evident.

‘Michael has got to make some big decisions. You can’t have a liability in your team. That petulance, that behaviour on the pitch is not acceptable.

‘He has been poor for a while and he has had injury problems. He is not the answer.’

#1912. Wrexham vs Middlesbrough - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 02 Nov 2026 10:44

Middlesbrough make the trip to Wrexham on Wednesday night looking to strengthen their hold of top spot in the Championship table.

Meanwhile, the Welsh club welcome the leaders to the Racecourse Ground sitting down in 18th place, 14 points adrift of their opponents.

Despite the legacy and loyalty that Phil Parkinson has earned during his hugely-successful stint at Wrexham, he will recognise that he is fighting to keep his job in the dugout.

Not only have Wrexham lost four of their last seven matches, they have suffered consecutive defeats without scoring a goal.

A 2-0 loss at Blackburn Rovers was followed by a 1-0 reverse at Sheffield United on Friday night, Parkinson using his post-match media duties to criticise his team.

Although sitting eight points adrift of the playoffs remains a retrievable situation, Wrexham have won just three of their 13 league contests in 2026-27.

The one positive is that Wrexham remain solid enough at the back. They have conceded just six goals more than the teams with the best defensive record (13) in the division.

They now face the challenge of playing a team in Middlesbrough that has scored 30 goals in their 13 league fixtures.

Kim Hellberg's side have not lost a Championship fixture since August 22, going down by a 2-1 scoreline at Blackburn.

That remains their solitary league defeat since losing last season's playoff final, while four wins have come from their most recent five encounters.

Despite netting 13 times in six away contests, Middlesbrough have conceded five times in their last three such matches and have posted just one clean sheet on their travels.

Middlesbrough have already defeated Wrexham this season, recording a 1-0 win in the EFL Cup first round at the Riverside Stadium.

After another individual error, Parkinson may consider replacing goalkeeper Anthony Patterson with Danny Ward.

Danny Imray and Sam Smith could return at right wing-back and forward respectively, while George Dobson or Ben Whiteman may get the nod over Ben Sheaf in the engine room.

Nathan Broadhead and Josh Windass are again expected to miss out through injury.

Despite top goalscorer Will Lankshear being withdrawn with a fitness issue against Charlton Athletic on Saturday, Hellberg has suggested that the Middlesbrough forward was suffering with cramp rather than an injury.

Barring any other fitness concerns, Hellberg could select the same team from the win over the Addicks.

Alfie Jones and Rokas Pukstas are sidelined through injury.

Ward; Doyle, Worrall, Hyam; Imray, Whiteman, James, Ekomie; O'Brien, Rathbone; Smith

Vitek; Brittain, Phillips, Malanda, Borges; Berhalter, Morris; Cozier-Duberry, McGree, Conway; Lankshear

While Wrexham have already shown this season that they can turn it on in front of their own supporters, we cannot look past the head of steam that Middlesbrough have built. Although this may be competitive, Boro should come through with the three points.

#1911. Leeds United, Hull City and Sheffield Wednesday players to stay put as 2027 Asian Cup postponed

Leeds United, Hull City and Sheffield Wednesday will not lose any players to Asian Cup duty in January as the tournament has been postponed.

The 24-team tournament was due to kick off on January 7 and run until February 5, but will now run from December 23, 2027, until January 21, 2028.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The decision to postpone the tournament has been made in light of attacks by Yemen's Houthi movement on three airports in Riyadh, the capital of host nation Saudi Arabia, last month.

Leeds midfielder Ao Tanaka was likely to feature for Japan at the tournament and may have been joined by Hull’s Hidemasa Morita. The Tigers may have also had to do without defender Lucas Herrington, who represents Australia.

Sheffield Wednesday, meanwhile, have Iraq international forward Ali Al-Hamadi on loan from Ipswich Town.

A spokesperson for the tournament said: “Following extensive discussions and close consultation with the Local Organising Committee (LOC) of the AFC Asian Cup Saudi Arabia 2027 and the Saudi Arabian Football Federation (SAFF), the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has confirmed today that the upcoming edition of Asia’s crown jewel, originally to be held from January 7 to February 5, 2027, will now take place from December 23, 2027, to January 21, 2028.

“The organising committee for AFC Asian Cup approved to reschedule the flagship national team tournament in light of the current exceptional circumstances arising from developments in the region, including substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions. The new dates of the tournament will be presented to FIFA for approval.

“Exceptional circumstances have been created for the organisation and delivery of the Competition as originally scheduled, making the postponement necessary in the interest of all participating teams, officials, spectators and other stakeholders.

“The AFC commends SAFF and the LOC for their commitment to delivering a world-class tournament for the Continent’s players and fans.

“The AFC will continue to work closely with the LOC, Participating Member Associations and its valued sponsors and broadcast and commercial partners and all stakeholders to stage a showpiece befitting the stature and operational excellence synonymous with Asia’s most prestigious men’s national team competition, while minimising the impact of the postponement. Further updates will be communicated through the AFC’s official channels.”

#1910. Arsenal star says Alexis Mac Allister was ‘clever’ in controversial moment

Noni Madueke did not join in with the chorus of criticism aimed at Alexis Mac Allister after their clash at Anfield, saying the Liverpool star was ‘obviously clever’ during the incident.

Arsenal left Anfield with a 1-0 win thanks to a first-half Kai Havertz goal as they moved three points clear at the top of the Premier League table.

It was an entertaining contest, despite Liverpool not managing a shot on target, with a decent amount of edge to the game.

There was a flash point late in the match as Mac Allister appeared furious with a felled Martin Odegaard, shouting at the Norwegian and slapping him on the back of the head.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Jurrien Timber, in turn, was fuming with that response as he rushed to confront the Argentina international.

As the pair squared up, Madueke got involved and went head-to-head with Mac Allister, who then went down, claiming to have been headbutted.

He clearly had not been and neither the referee nor VAR were buying his theatrical attempt to get the Arsenal winger dismissed.

Jamie Carragher was extremely critical of Mac Allister for how he tried to engineer a red card for his opponent, but Madueke was more charitable, acknowledging that he was being baited, but it was ‘clever’ to do so.

‘To be honest, I don’t think it’s anything. Whether it’s a yellow or red card, the referee didn’t think that. VAR didn’t think that. So we all agreed there,’ Madueke told Viaplay.

‘It’s a natural movement and he is obviously clever. He tried to bait me into getting a red card there.

‘In my head, I’ll be very honest with you guys, in my head I was thinking: “It’s possible, you know, with VAR”. It’s about whoever interprets it. I don’t know what they’re thinking. But thankfully it wasn’t.’

Liverpool legend Carragher went on a rant against players acting as Mac Allister did at Anfield, calling his reaction a ‘joke’ and calling for the sport to stamp it out.

‘I’m delighted he never got sent off there. We have got to be strong on calling people out and saying that this is embarrassing. I cant stand it,’ Carragher told Sky Sports.

‘I think everybody in the country watching football this head-to-head stuff. If someone puts their head back and butts, or course red card, but this stuff about head-to-head and if someone touches, the other one goes down and the payer gets sent off.

‘As a game, as football, people in the Premier League, supporters, call your own people out for it.

‘I’m a Liverpool fan, that’s a joke from Mac Allister but it’s got to stop. People are trying to gain an advantage because they know they can because red cards are getting given for it.

‘Whether it’s from Howard Webb, the Premier League, the managers get together. This has got to stop. Stop getting red cards for this crap!’

#1906. Dwight Yorke names the manager Manchester United must appoint to replace Michael Carrick

Manchester United hero Dwight Yorke has told the Red Devils to pay whatever is necessary to bring in Unai Emery as manager.

Michael Carrick remains in charge at Old Trafford, but after nine games without a win his grip on the job looks very flimsy.

United have two games before the next international break, hosting Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday and then Emery’s Aston Villa in the Premier League on Sunday.

If they win neither of those contests then it seems extremely difficult to imagine Carrick will still be in charge when the players return from international duty.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Yorke, who played for Villa from 1989-98 before moving to Manchester United, says Emery is the only man for the job and the Red Devils should have done whatever they could to get him before they hired Ruben Amorim in 2024 and should do the same now.

‘I have said this all along, and it baffles me when people are now jumping on the bandwagon,’ Yorke said on talkSPORT.

‘I said this two-and-a-half years ago. Unai Emery was the man to go and get way before Amorim has come into the equation.

‘And just like how, you go and spend £70million on players, I think Unai Emery, you can go and spend that money, I am not saying £70m, but pay whatever Villa has asked and get him. Give him the authority to come in.

‘I have said that way before Amorim has come in. I got a backlash from the Villa fans, and to this day, I still believe that he is the best manager in the business, certainly to get Man Utd to some type of credibility and sustainability at the same time as well.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Yorke recognises that the Manchester United players are massively under-performing, but feels that Carrick has to take some of the blame for that as he appears unable to turn the tide.

‘When things are good, which it was really good under Carrick when he first took over, football is easy,’ said the former striker.

‘The difference in management is when things are not so good. As a player when things are not so good, have you got the character to bounce back?

‘This is where we have seen Carrick is being let down. You need a reaction from your players. Whether the players are on board with you, are they going to fight for you? I’ve not seen that.

‘We’ve seen Carrick in his element when things are really good. When things have not gone so well the manager’s job is trying to motivate the players, get them back to playing, showing some character, play with conviction, play with passion.

‘Even if you lose a football match, that’s fine. But if you lose football matches the way United have been losing football matches, I’m afraid that it does not look good.

‘You look at Tottenham, for instance, they were at the bottom and the manager somehow finds a way. You’ve got to find a way from your players and I’m not seeing that with Carrick.

‘This is the time as a manager when you’ve got to earn your coin and he’s not really doing that at the moment.’

#1902. Real Madrid transfer news: Los Blancos make key decision ahead of January window

By Axel Clody | 02 Nov 2026 11:11

Two months before the opening of the winter transfer window, Real Madrid have already made an important decision about it.

Real Madrid had a very turbulent last transfer window. Following the arrival of Jose Mourinho, the Spanish giants renewed part of their squad and invested more than £190m, notably on Yan Diomande and Marc Cucurella. They also parted with squad players such as Fran Garcia and Gonzalo Garcia, recovering £50m.

The next winter transfer window should be much less intense in the Madrid offices.

According to AS, Real Madrid will not be concerned with the next transfer window. The current third-placed side in La Liga do not feel the need to strengthen their squad in the middle of the season.

The club hierarchy believe this group can end a trophy drought of a year and a half. The few injuries recorded at the start of the season and possible winter opportunities are not enough to consider signing anyone this winter.

In recent days, there have been rumours about possible returns of Jacobo Ramon and Nico Paz, who are shining at Como.

‘Real Madrid’s executives have not yet made any decision on the futures of the players on whom they hold a buy-back option, and nothing is expected to be decided before next spring,’ the Spanish outlet says.

The need for a reinforcement in midfield this winter has also been mentioned in the press, but that is not the case internally.

However, Real Madrid could open the door to departures in the next transfer window. That will only happen if a player asks to leave and Mourinho does not oppose it. AS says, however, that this ‘does not seem very likely for now’.

#1901. Man United are the worst transfer operators in EUROPE as new study reveals Red Devils have made a £334MILLION loss on signings - with fellow Premier League club joining them in bottom three

Published: 09:37 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 14:11 EDT, 29 October 2026

When it rains it pours at Old Trafford, and not just through the leaky roof.

The beleaguered club, facing a managerial nightmare, dressing room unrest and unprecedented fan fury at the board and owners - have now been named the worst transfer operators in Europe over the past five years.

Stats boffins at CIES Football Observatory have put the business of hundreds of clubs around the world under the microscope.

And the findings make for grim reading for United, who are the lowest ranked European team having lost £334m since 2022.

Only big-spending Saudi side Al-Hilal are below the Red Devils in the overall standings.

The data compiled by CIES ranks every team in world football who have spent more than £42m on transfer fees since 2021, including add-ons.

Antony (left) and Rasmus Hojlund (right) were both sold for a massive loss by Man United - who rank as the worst transfer operators in Europe

They then calculated the balance between fees paid to sign players and money received for selling (loans do not count). And the value of players still owned by the club is also taken into account.

A high ranking in the list points to a shrewd, well-run transfer strategy and teams lower down have conducted poor business.

In Man United's case, they have lost approximately £156m from player sales and the value of players in under-fire Michael Carrick's squad decreased by a further £184m.

It doesn't take long to understand how these gruesome numbers came to be. United splashed out £85m on Antony from Ajax in 2022 and he left for only £21.7m to Real Betis.

Jadon Sancho arrived to much fanfare from Borussia Dortmund, costing the club £73m. They did not recoup any fee and he remains a free agent.

Rasmus Hojlund came for £72m in 2023 and later signed for Napoli for a £34m loss.

Andre Onana (£47m), Mason Mount (£60m) and Joshua Zirkzee (£36m) remain on the books but have struggled to make an impact.

The CIES study is a damning indictment of Sir Jim Ratcliffe's INEOS, who have run football operations since buying a stake in the club

Zirkzee was the only one of those players signed by Ineos, who took over the day-to-day running of football operations in 2024, and have since tried to stem the club’s losses. Club insiders have pointed to the fact that the CIES data shows that United’s poor recruitment has improved.

As well as offloading high earners like Casemiro and Sancho, United have taken a more pragmatic approach to transfers under Sir Jim Ratcliffe. Last summer, the club abandoned any attempt to sign Elliot Anderson once it became clear that his valuation had rocketed beyond the £100m mark, and refused to get into a bidding war with Tottenham over Mateus Fernandes.

In the end, United spent a total of £163m on Carlos Baleba, Andrey, Santos, Youri Tielemans and Tynan Thompson. It followed an outlay of £239m in 2025 on Benjamin Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Senne Lammens.

The figures demonstrate the challenge clubs face in not only recouping transfer fees, but also correctly identifying the right players at the right prices in recruitment.

At the very top of the list, Bundesliga outfit Eintracht Frankfurt boast an increase in value of approximately £441m.

Real Madrid are behind them with £440m, while Champions League holders PSG sit in third on £394m.

Manchester City are among the top performers - in fifth just behind Benfica - with an increase in value of around £374m, although there is clearly the enormous caveat that they have been found guilty of breaking financial rules between 2009 and 2018, a period that provided the foundation for the five years studied by CIES.

Man United are not the only Premier League side with a dreadful recent record in the market.

Tottenham's total value went down by £157m and the value of their players has dropped by £195m. Richarlison signing from Everton in 2022 for £60m and Dominic Solanke's £65m addition are two significant outlays that have failed to deliver.

It remains to be seen how Spurs' massive summer outlay on Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Co will age but Spurs are ranked fourth last on the entire CIES list.

Brighton are among the best performing club in terms of transfer strategy

Leicester City, now languishing in League One, have seen a decrease of £73m, while relegated West Ham depreciated by £63m.

Unsurprisingly, Bournemouth, Brighton and Brentford, often heralded for being among the best-run clubs, ranked highly with gains of £292m, £271m and £253m respectively.

Liverpool, who lost Trent Alexander-Arnold and Ibrahima Konate at the end of their contracts and have broken the £100m barrier on three players in two years, barely broke even with a value change of £13m.

Chelsea, despite spending approaching £2bn, have sold well and are up £179m in value change over the time frame. Nottingham Forest are another side who have been extremely busy in the market and have a rise of the same amount as the Blues.

Of the Premier League sides on the list, Man United a the worst performing by CIES metrics by a significant margin.

The crisis club have chosen to give Carrick a stay of execution and fans' lack of faith in the running of the club will only be strengthened by the brutal transfer failings of half a decade laid out in black and white.

#1900. AC Milan 3-1 Inter: Moreira inspires commanding fourth straight derby win

AC Milan recorded a huge win in the derby against Inter, scoring three times in the first half to secure a 3-1 win.

It did not take long for Milan to go in front, with Christian Pulisic heading in a cross from Diego Moreira. Then, just a few minutes later, Adrien Rabiot was on hand to fire in a corner first time and make it a two-goal lead.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Alessandro Bastoni scored from a corner to make it a one-goal lead once again, but then Moreira’s free-kick re-established the two-goal lead and that would be enough to see the Rossoneri through to the end of the game.

It marked a fourth straight win for Milan in the derby and it reduces the gap to the city rivals back down to four points.

Ruben Amorim chose to make six changes from the team that lost to Bologna on Wednesday night, with Mario Gila, Sankhoun Diawara, Luka Modric, Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all getting the nod.

Inside four minutes, Milan took the lead and it was the derby talisman Christian Pulisic who struck once again. It was quite a simple move down the right side in the end, with Diego Moreira checking back inside onto his left foot and whipped in a simply perfect cross for Pulisic to nod in from a few yards out.

Then, just a few minutes later, Milan doubled their advantage from a set-piece after another good spell of pressure. A low delivery from Moreira found the run of Rabiot towards the near post, who somehow managed to divert it in via the far post to make it 2-0.

Midway through the first half, Inter got themselves back into the game through a dead ball of their own. A corner was flicked on at the near post towards Bastoni, who was on hand to nod in from a few yards with the Milan defenders rooted.

Inter assumed the ascendancy after the goal, and they twice threatened in quick succession shortly after their first goal. Calhanoglu had a shot tipped over from the edge of the box, then another flicked header from a corner drew a desperate reaction save from Maignan.

Milan continued to give their city rivals opportunities to try and make it a brand new game. A silly foul by Pavlovic on Spence drew a free-kick just off the right edge of the box, though the eventual shot from Diouf was grasped by Maignan.

Just over 10 minutes before the break, Inter had another chance to draw themselves level. A cross from the left was not cut out by Koni De Winter, and the ball fells to Spence who fired with his left foot, but the Frenchman makes a brilliant reaction save to deflect the shot out for a corner.

Just two minutes before the break, Milan restored their two-goal advantage thanks to a quite simply beautiful free-kick from Diego Moreira. After getting two assists to his name already on the night, he turned scorer with a fantastic attempt that was up and over the wall, dipping just enough to land inside the near right post.

Ten minutes into the second half, Inter had the first big opening and it fell to their recent danger man Carlos Augusto. A cross to the far post wasn’t tracked by anyone and the wing-back ghosted in at the far post, heading it wide from about a yard off the ground.

With 25 minutes left, a corner this time for Milan: Modric’s cross from the left finds Rabiot at the near post, who tries to head it in, but his connection was poor and the ball went straight out.

In the 75th minute, it looked like the game was going to be on once again when the referee gave a penalty for what he adjudged to be a handball on Mario Gila. The replays show that the cross struck his midriff, and therefore the penalty was overturned to be a corner.

With the game settled into a rhythm of attack versus defence, Amorim chose to make a double change with eight minutes to go. Pulisic and Diawara were the ones who came off, with Alphadjo Cisse and Davide Bartesaghi the ones to come on.

In the penultimate minute of added time, a double sub came from Amorim. Ramos and Moreira came off, Filippo Terracciano and Omari Hutchinson came on.

Alphadjo Cisse came on inside the final minutes and immediately came close to scoring. The Italian forward tried a curling shot from outside the area, but Martinez saved well to put it out for a corner, keeping it 3-1.

#1899. Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

United fought back after conceding an early goal against Atletico to secure their second win of pre-season.

They fell behind in the sixth minute when Arnau Ortiz’s cross into the box evaded everyone, including United keeper Tom Heaton before hitting the back of the net.

United got the equaliser their performance deserved when the impressive Shea Lacey showed his skill in the box and was fouled. From the resulting penalty, Bryan Mbeumo sent the goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

In the 72nd minute, Mbeumo got his second of the afternoon after he bundled the ball home after the United press forced Atletico into a mistake.

The Spanish side hit the post twice in the closing stages but United held on to win.

“We had a clear plan before the game, everyone stuck to it and made the game enjoyable,” Mbeumo said. “We work really hard during training for these games, the main goal is to be ready for the season starting. I have done great things on the right but also as a striker.

“I think I am more experienced on the wing but I enjoy playing as a striker. For an offensive player, it is always good to score for the team.”

And it is. All over in Stockholm as United come back from behind to win. A really good performance by Michael Carrick’s side.

Iker Luque shoots from distance. It looks good but flies over the bar. And that should be the final effort of the match...

Mendoza and Hjulmand both hit the post in quick succession. Heaton was beaten on both occasions. United were a bit fortunate there.

Now that they are behind, Atletico are starting to have a bit more possession and play on the front foot.

A slow second half comes alive as United take the lead. A slack pass in defence by Atletico is pounced upon by Fletcher. He runs to the byline, cuts the ball back to the unmarked Mbeumo, who taps in.

OFF: Shaw, Dorgu, Lacey, MaguireON: Armer, Amass, Zirkzee, Williams

Big save from Heaton to deny Atletico at the near post after Yoro was beaten by a lovely pass from Lemar.

The energy and intensity of the first half has largely disappeared in this half. Neither keeper has been worked.

Another player, who has been tidy for United is Santos in midfield. He’s controlled the middle of the park, been safe in possession but also willing to fire a pass into the forwards.

Seven changes coming for Atletico. Typical pre-season move.

Mbeumo takes responsibility, waits for the keeper to dive and strokes the ball into the bottom left corner.

Dancing feet from Lacey in the box and Castillo brings him down. The referee rightly points to the spot.

Heaven is booked for a late tackle after Atletico threatened a counter-attack.

Amad can be very pleased after his first minutes of pre-season. He was very lively.

J. Fletcher coming for United in place of Amad.

Atletico make three changes. I’ll get them to you shortly!

No time added on, so that is the end of the half. An intriguing 45 mins. United will feel they don’t deserve to be losing.

United fail to clear the ball and it falls to Arnau Ortiz, who forces a good save from Heaton. That would have been harsh on United.

Lookman has been very quiet for Atletico. Yoro has marked him out of the game but in truth, Atletico have given him nothing to work with.

Apart from the move that led to Atletico’s goal, they have barely been in United’s half. They are struggling to beat United’s press and keep the ball. United are losing but they are working very hard and playing well.

Great pressing by United leads to Amad winning the ball back. Yoro finds Lacey, who spins and goes down the right. He whips in a cross and Mbeumo rises to attack it but heads wide. Probably should have done better.

It is probably an easy comparison but Lacey has a bit of Phil Foden about him with his movement and touch. He looks promising.

Carlos Martín goes down after a coming together with Heaven. The United defender got his arm across and made minimal contact with Martín’s face but the referee falls for the play-acting and calls a foul.

An aggressive press from United as they look to deny time to Atletico. They are pushing for that equaliser.

Amad, Mount and Mbeumo all want it. Amad takes it and his low strike is deflected and looks certain to beat Oblak but the keeper reacts quickly to make the stop.

Santos punches a pass through the lines, Mbeumo combines with Mount and the attacker is brought to the ground on the edge of the box...

Nearly a quick reply by United. Amad sets the ball for Mount to cross into the box. The midfielder’s ball goes to the far post, where Shaw meets it with a thumping volley but Oblak stands his ground and palms the ball over the bar.

From the resulting corner, Yoro should do better with his header but his effort goes wide.

Early goal for Atletico. They take a short corner, Arnau Ortiz whips in a dangerous ball that beats everyone and drops in at the far post. Heaton never moved.

United dominating possession in the opening stages with Atletico happy to sit off and let the Premier League side have it. Even in pre-season, Diego Simeone has his side set up well to defend.

The visit to the Strawberry Arena means United are back at the stadium where they won the 2017 Europa League.

📸 Wayne Rooney, 2017 🏆#UEL | @ManUtd pic.twitter.com/HxZVn1mAEQ

Gianni Infantino is facing an ultimatum from Uefa: resign or face an emergency no-confidence vote.

It is understood all 55 of Uefa’s member nations would opt to oust Infantino in a vote of no-confidence if he refuses to step down. Uefa can trigger such a vote with just 43 member nations.

European football’s governing body announced a loss of confidence on Saturday morning and has demanded change after Infantino was forced to scrap his £15bn plan to sell a stake in the World Cup.

Uefa’s statement followed widespread opposition and a revolt within Fifa’s ranks that staff are calling “kill the monster”.

The Football Association backed Uefa’s stance, saying: “We fully support Uefa’s position. It is time for a full and robust review of Fifa’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.”

Atletico: Oblak, Domínguez, Le Normand, Hancko, Ruggeri, Koke, Obed Vargas, Castillo, Arnau Ortiz, Carlos Martín, Lookman

United: Heaton; Yoro, Maguire (c), Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Amad, Lacey, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Bayindir, Mee, Vitek, Amass, Armer, Kamason, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Thwaites, Gabriel, Williams, Zirkzee.

Good afternoon and welcome to pre-season coverage of Manchester United against Atletico Madrid.

Michael Carrick’s squad continue their preparations for the new season with a trip to the Swedish capital, Stockholm, where they face Diego Simeone’s La Liga side.

Last week, United cruised to a 5-0 victory over Rosenborg but today will be their first real test. They are slowly starting to get players back but the likes of captain Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans will not be involved.

“I think we’re in a good place. I think there’s four weeks to go to the start and we’re gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup as we progress,” Carrick said.

“But I think a little bit of patience and time and trying to keep ahead and as I said, keeping everyone fit but moving forward is a really good direction to go in. And as it stands right now, I think we’re in a pretty good place. So, the boys will get better as we go.”

One player who will be looking to impress is Mason Mount. He has had an injury-hit spell at Old Trafford but is fit and ready to go for the season. He is also growing into a leadership role at the club.

He told BBC Radio Manchester: “You have different types of leaders, you have ones that are very vocal. I always want to see myself as one that leads by example and never stops working on the pitch.

“I’ve been captain previously years ago. I love the role especially with a lot of younger players on the pitch being able to speak to them and make them feel comfortable in the game and off the pitch as well. It’s a role that I really like and loved having it [the captain’s armband] in the second half.”

#1897. Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, 30, dies after collision with goalkeeper

Jesus de Miguel has died after a collision during Tenerife’s match against Andorra on Monday evening.

The 30-year-old suffered head and chest injuries following a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who was sent off the challenge near the halfway line.

Owono had sprinted from his goal to clear a long ball when his knee collided with De Miguel’s chest.

De Miguel rolled on the floor immediately after impact but was then motionless on his back as several players urgently signalled for medical help.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The referee showed Owono a red card before the match was abandoned.

An initial statement from Tenerife on Monday night said that De Miguel was ‘stable’ in hospital.

But a second update from the Spanish club in the early hours of Tuesday morning said that De Miguel’s ‘medical condition has worsened neurologically’.

Later on Tuesday morning, Tenerife announced that De Miguel has died.

Tenerife’s statement said: ‘Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe this is true, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesús de Miguel Alameda.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can lessen this overwhelming sadness. We stand with his grieving family, with his loved ones, with all of Tenerife who mourn this cruel loss today.

Andorra also released a statement which read: ‘With broken hearts and devastated, we wish to send our deepest condolences to the family of Jesús de Miguel, all his teammates, friends, and CD Tenerife. May he rest in peace.’

In response to Tenerife’s statement confirming De Miguel’s death, former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, who is now the president of Andorra FC, wrote on X: ‘I am so sorry. Rest in peace, Jesus.’

#1896. Oxford United vs Reading - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 02 Nov 2026 11:14

Oxford United play host to Reading on Wednesday night looking to extend their prolonged unbeaten streak.

At a time when the home side sit in third position in the League One table, sixth-placed Reading trail them by just one point.

While some Oxford fans would have had a level of scepticism over the appointment of unproven Aaron Ramsey, it is currently looking like a smart decision from the club's board.

Not only does Ramsey's team sit in third spot with games in hand on the sides above them, their only league defeat of the campaign has come at leaders Huddersfield Town on September 1.

A total of 19 points have been collected from nine matches since that solitary setback, with Oxford impressively not conceding more than once in any of those encounters.

However, four draws have been recorded in seven fixtures, including a goalless draw against Barnsley on Saturday when Oxford had a player advantage for 79 minutes.

Furthermore, Oxford have only netted nine times in their six matches at the Kassam Stadium, with just four goals coming in their most recent such contests.

Despite being the underdogs for this contest, Reading have quietly gone about their business to keep themselves in promotion contention.

Ten points have come from their last five games, while Leam Richardson's outfit earned a goalless draw at fourth-placed Plymouth Argyle at the weekend.

One criticism is their failure to score more than twice in eight of their last nine League One fixtures. However, they did prevail by a 5-1 scoreline at MK Dons on the one occasion that they did.

That said, thrashing MK Dons on away territory remains their only away success in six such League One matches this season, with just three goals coming in the other five games.

After goalkeeper Jamie Cumming was sent off at Barnsley, Simon Eastwood will deputise between the sticks.

Peter Kioso, Mo Missanga and Aidomo Emakhu are all in contention for recalls in wide areas.

Jamie McDonnell is expected to remain out of contention, but Jeon Jin-woo may return to the squad after injury.

Reading forward Jack Marriott will come under consideration for a recall after a 27-minute comeback appearance at the weekend.

Jamie Reid may drop out to accommodate the 32-year-old, who netted eight goals in seven games before sitting out the past month.

Charlie Savage has made more starts for Wales than in League One this campaign, but his regular substitute outings hint that he is not far off from a first third-tier appearance of 2026-27 in the first XI.

Paddy Lane, George Earthy and Benn Ward are again expected to miss out.

Eastwood; Spencer, Long, Helik, Currie; Sibley, Andrews; Lynch, Goodrham, Dembele; Harris

Pereira; Godwin-Malife, O'Connor, Knight, Dorsett; Wing, Rinomhota; Lisbie, Stokes, Williams; Marriott

With Reading having produced a similar run of form as Oxford, we expect the visitors to push Ramsey's side all the way on Wednesday night. Nevertheless, Oxford may still do enough to get all three points on the board, potentially through a late goal.

Barcelona misfit Alejandro Balde is reportedly ‘open’ to leaving the club in January amid strong interest from Manchester United.

Balde joined Barca at the age of just eight after impressing in Espanyol’s youth ranks and would go on to break into the Catalan giants’ first-team in 2021.

The 23-year-old left-back has since made a total of 172 appearances in all competitions for Barca while helping the club win seven pieces of silverware, including three La Liga titles.

However, Balde has badly struggled for regular playing time under head coach Hansi Flick, with all four of his appearances this season coming from the substitutes bench.

Balde currently finds himself behind both Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart in the pecking order at the Camp Nou and the Spain international’s career appears to be at a crossroads.

According to Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, Barca’s coaching staff are of the belief that Balde is prone to ‘losing focus’ and is unable to read the game well when it comes to pressing.

‘Balde doesn’t have the confidence he needs in his game right now, nor the conviction,’ Flick told reporters ahead of Barca’s 6-1 victory over Alaves last weekend.

It’s claimed the situation has left Balde ‘open’ to the prospect of moving on from Barca, with the out-of-favour full-back ‘beginning to accept’ that this is likely his only route back to playing consistently.

Balde is said to have grown ‘upset’ as he expected Flick to have been direct and honest with him over his limited minutes, as the German supposedly had been with the likes of Marc Casado and Hector Fort.

He has ‘learned lessons’ from his close friend Ansu Fati, who spent a number of years waiting for opportunities at Barca without managing to nail down regular game-time.

Diogo Dalot has therefore been forced to fill in as a makeshift left-back during United’s miserable winless streak under an increasingly under-pressure Michael Carrick.

#1892. Player Ratings: AC Milan 3-1 Inter – Moreira show; De Winter responds

AC Milan clinched a massive win at San Siro to paint the city of Milan red and black. Below are the player ratings for the Rossoneri, with several high ones handed out.

After an up-and-down start to the season, Milan headed into the Derby della Madonnina knowing that a win would make all the difference. Gerry Cardinale said as much before the game and luckily, they succeeded with a 3-1 win.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

🥇 Moreira (9.5 – MOTM): He’s rough around the edges sometimes, but with one fantastic goal and two very good assists in a derby, he deserves all the praise he can get. I expressed doubts about him playing on the right but tonight was his best game in that role. Really, really encouraging ahead of what’s to come.

👎 Everyone got over a 6 tonight, so there was no flop.

👔 Amorim (7): Individual brilliance was the difference-maker, BUT, it would be rude not to acknowledge some of Amorim’s moves tonight. He got the starting eleven spot on, waited with the substitutions, and gave his players good advice at the interval to avoid another push from Inter in the second half.

Maignan (8): He made a fantastic save on Spence in the first half, using his reflexes, and it’s a save that really paved the way for the win. There were other good interventions too, like the volleyball-esque clearance on Calhanoglu’s corner, and coming out to head the ball away. CAPITANO!

Gila (7): I don’t think it’s a coincidence that Milan suddenly looked much more solid with him back in the defensive four. That said, he didn’t stand out with any major interventions, but was just very good through calm passing, good positioning and marshalling. When he’s back to 100% fit, he will be even more important.

De Winter (8): He absolutely won the battle against Thuram this game and it’s not like it was an easy one either. The two had several 50-50 duels and he always came out on top. Aside from his Thuram battle, he was very good overall and deserves a high rating here.

Pavlovic (7.5): It was a bit of a roller coaster for him, but allow me to explain. He left Bastoni on the goal and simply shouldn’t have, for many reasons, and then he also missed a good chance in attack. However, the second half was brilliant with several last-ditch clearances/tackles, including a wonderful one on Barella to stop a goal. That tackle was worth everything in my opinion.

Diawara (6.5): Considering it was his first derby, and game of this calibre, we have to give him praise. He had a cautious style and it worked tonight, as he often just needed to stop his man/block the cross rather than trying to make something extraordinary with the ball. One good cross in attack for Pavlovic, which we shouldn’t forget.

Moreira (9.5 – MOTM): He’s rough around the edges sometimes, but with one fantastic goal and two very good assists in a derby, he deserves all the praise he can get. I expressed doubts about him playing on the right but tonight was his best game in that role. Really, really encouraging ahead of what’s to come.

Musah (7): He won the free-kick that Moreira converted with some smart body work. In addition to that, he was very composed (something he often struggles with) and really helped Milan get out of several tough/tight situations. One poor giveaway at the end but overall, very solid.

Modric (7.5): The veteran stayed on for the entire 90 minutes and fought until the very end. There was one sequence in the final minutes/last ten or so when he really had to scrap to get out of a tight jam, and did so successfully. What a player.

Pulisic (8): It was a great header to open the scoring for Milan, celebrating his renewal in style. The positioning is what makes him so brilliant, not just on the goal but also how he links the midfield and attack together. Could he have been even more effective on the ball? Yes, but the importance of the movement shouldn’t be played down just because it wasn’t always fireworks.

Rabiot (7.5): I’m stunned by the awareness to opt for a finish like that on the goal, but that’s why he’s such a highly-rated footballer. He was good aside from that but perhaps could have been even more effective on the ball for a higher rating. Then again, his movement and running is key.

Ramos (6.5): It feels like I say it every game, aside from the last one when he genuinely looked tired, but the running helps Milan so much in opening up space. Now, his rating is not super high here and that’s because he can still do more on the ball/in the box, but it was good.

Since all the substitutions were made from the 82nd minute onwards, I just didn’t see enough to give either of them a rating.

Bartesaghi, Jashari, Cisse, Terracciano and Hutchinson: N/A

Amorim (7): Individual brilliance was the difference-maker, BUT, it would be rude not to acknowledge some of Amorim’s moves tonight. He got the starting eleven spot on, waited with the substitutions, and gave his players good advice at the interval to avoid another push from Inter in the second half.

#1891. Barcelona vs. Aston Villa: How to watch, date, time, live stream and TV channel for Champions League clash

By Darren Plant | 02 Nov 2026 11:57

Barcelona and Aston Villa continue their respective Champions League campaigns with a showdown in Spain on Tuesday night.

While the La Liga champions sit in eighth place in the League Phase table, their Premier League opponents are third after winning three successive matches.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Champions League match will kick off at 8pm, UK time, on Tuesday night.

The Champions League fixture between Barcelona and Aston Villa will be played at Camp Nou.

Villa are making their first trip to Barcelona's iconic home ground, which is operating at a reduced 62,652 capacity, since a UEFA Super Cup contest in January 1983.

The Champions League match will be shown live on TNT Sports 1, which is channel number 410 if watching through Sky Sports.

TNT Sports is also available as an add-on for Amazon's Prime Video app.

Goals will be posted on the FootballOnTNT X account, while highlights will also be uploaded to the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel after the match.

Having already defeated Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking FK, Unai Emery knows that Villa are already on the brink of guaranteeing a top-24 place in the table.

However, the Spaniard will want to avoid having to participate in the playoffs in February. If Villa can achieve seven or eight points from their remaining five league phase fixtures, that scenario may be avoided.

Despite Saturday's disappointing 1-1 draw versus Fulham, Villa have earned 11 points from their last five games in the Premier League.

Meanwhile, Barcelona have scored an incredible 46 goals in 12 La Liga matches, winning 11 times and only losing to Real Madrid.

Nevertheless, not only did they lose 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain on matchday three, Hansi Flick's side have not kept a clean sheet in five games across all competitions.

#1890. Tottenham and Newcastle-linked striker talks up move to ‘big club’

Villarreal striker Georges Mikautadze has been linked with a move away from the Spanish side and feels he is ‘ready to go to a big club’.

The 26-year-old has had an interesting career path so far, breaking through at French side Metz before earning a move to Ajax which did not make out and he returned to his first professional club.

The Georgia international would then move to Lyon in 2024 and switched again the following year as he joined Villarreal.

He scored 15 goals in all competitions last season and has netted five so far in this campaign, including the opener in the 4-3 defeat at Liverpool in the Champions League last month.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Both Tottenham and Newcastle have been credited with interest in Mikautadze before, while Barcelona are also thought to like the forward.

He is not shy in admitting that he fancies a step up and feels ready to do just that.

‘I think I’m ready to go to a big club,’ Mikautade told L’Equipe. ‘I have everything I need and I try to show it every time. I just maybe need a little more time.’

Specifically responding to Barcelona’s interest in him, he said: ‘Yes, it’s flattering and it motivates me even more. It also means that the work is being done well.

‘As a child, ever since the Xavi-Iniesta-Busquets era and the MSN [Messi-Suarez-Neymar] trio, I’ve been a Barca supporter. But I hadn’t really thought about it.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Mikautadze will hope to show off his talents against the best team in Europe on Tuesday night when Villarreal take on Paris Saint-Germain.

PSG sit top of the group stage table with three wins from three games, looking very good in their bid to make it three Champions League titles on the spin.

Luis Enrique, the man who has led PSG to double European glory, has been philosophical on his achievements ahead of this encounter.

‘We have all won, we have all lost,’ he said. ‘I have been through countless situations where I was considered a “fraud” by a lot of people, and that fraud has kept evolving and improving, because that is the mindset a coach must have.

‘And now, everyone thinks I’m “the chosen one” or I don’t know what. And this is all a lie, all a lie.

‘The important thing is to follow your path. And along the path, the beautiful thing is that there are potholes, curves, and climbs.

‘Then the downhills also appear, which are very rewarding, but in the end, you appreciate the bad moments more. And if this is a “bad moment” for Villarreal, quote-unquote, I am sure they will get many positive things out of it.’

#1889. Coventry fan, 14, arrested following ‘cruel’ Bradley Lowery taunt in Sunderland match

A 14-year-old male has been arrested on suspicion of a public order offence and subsequently bailed after a video emerged appearing to show a Coventry fan taunting Sunderland supporters with a photograph of the late Bradley Lowery.

Bradley was a lifelong supporter of Sunderland and his battle with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer, touched the hearts of supporters across the footballing world – and beyond – before his tragic death at the age of six in July 2017.

His legacy lives on through the Bradley Lowery Foundation which was established in August later that year and has helped support countless families in raising funds for treatment and equipment which is not readily available through the NHS.

Footage of the alleged incident came to light after Coventry’s 3-1 victory at home to Sunderland in the Premier League on Saturday afternoon.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The five-second clip in question appears to show a young spectator in the home end at the Coventry Building Society Arena grinning while pointing to a picture of Bradley on a mobile phone.

It is not the first time that Bradley’s story has seemingly been hijacked in such sickening circumstances, with Sheffield Wednesday fan Dale Houghton sacked from his job and handed a 12-month suspended prison sentence following a similar incident in 2023.

‘Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland,’ a statement from the Sky Blues read on Sunday.

Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland.The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course… pic.twitter.com/RxXnhtW3DF

‘The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.’

It’s understood the teenage boy in question voluntarily handed himself into West Midlands Police, who, in turn, confirmed that an investigation was underway.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The shocking video footage went viral on social media shortly after Coventry’s defeat of Sunderland and was widely condemned by both Black Cats fans and supporters of rival clubs.

A host of Coventry fans have also shown their support for Lowery’s family in the intervening days, with many leaving heartfelt messages alongside donations on JustGiving’s The Bradley Lowery Foundation fundraising page.

Lowery’s mother, Gemma, meanwhile, has called for her ‘beautiful boy’ to be ‘remembered with love, not hate’ in a heartbreaking statement on Instagram.

‘My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate. Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters,’ she wrote.

‘As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.

‘I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between. So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face.

‘To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.

‘We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter?

‘I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were. I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don’t. I just for him to learn from this.

‘Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day.’

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Gemma took the opportunity to thank those who had stepped up to defend Bradley since the video first began to circulate on social media.

‘Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know,’ she added.

‘What some people don’t realise is that Bradley’s story didn’t end when his life did.

‘Because of Bradley, children’s lives are being saved, hundreds of families have received vital support, and children facing unimaginable battles are being given hope.

‘Through Super Brad’s Pad, families can escape hospital life, spend precious time together and make memories that last forever.‘That is Bradley’s legacy. The difference my little boy continues to make in this world. No amount of cruelty will ever take that away.‘So rather than let this photograph be remembered for hatred, I want it remembered for what it truly represents.

‘My beautiful little boy, enjoying one of the happiest days of his life, with the biggest smile on his face. That is how I want the world to remember him. #CancerHasNoColours Forever 6. Forever loved.’

Gemma finished by sharing a link to the Bradley Lowery Foundation’s website: www.bradleyloweryfoundation.com

#1888. Morocco squad announcement: Ouahbi faces injury headache before AFCON qualifiers

By Axel Clody | 02 Nov 2026 12:04

With his squad for the Niger games approaching, Mohamed Ouahbi is seeing the treatment room fill up with several important players.

A squad is rarely built without surprises. But when bad news hits the defence, midfield and attack almost at the same time, it ends up considerably disrupting the manager’s plans. Mohamed Ouahbi is experiencing that, just days before the double-header against Niger in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

Ismael Saibari, Azzedine Ounahi, Ayoub El Kaabi and Chadi Riad are unavailable for a long period, and Soufiane Rahimi is highly doubtful.

Injured in the clash between Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund, the attacking midfielder has a ruptured syndesmotic ligament in his right ankle. Successfully operated on after his injury in the Klassiker, he should stay out for several months and will miss the games against Niger on 13 and 17 November.

His absence frustrates Ouahbi because of his versatility: the manager has used him both as a number 10 and as a centre-forward, notably during the 2026 World Cup. Saibari brought power, off-the-ball runs and an ability to get into the box.

The Panathinaikos midfielder was seriously injured against Asteras Tripolis (5-1) on 18 October. He suffered damage to the tendon of the right biceps femoris, was operated on and will be out for around two and a half to three months.

Ounahi broke lines by carrying the ball, resisted the press and created in tight spaces. His place could go to Amine Harit, in form with Marseille, while Bilal El Khannouss, Neil El Aynaoui and Ayyoub Bouaddi offer other profiles. None of them exactly reproduces his qualities.

Ayoub El Kaabi, who suffered a fractured left tibia with Olympiacos at the beginning of September, is continuing his rehabilitation after his operation. At 33, he brought his positional sense and his efficiency in the box.

Soufiane Rahimi, who was injured in the hamstring against Shabab Al-Ahli on 22 October, also sees his participation compromised.

Hamza Igamane is getting closer to a return after his serious knee injury but lacks match rhythm. Ouahbi can count on Youssef En-Nesyri or promote a youngster such as Yassir Zabiri.

In defence, the Crystal Palace player suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee against Everton on 22 August. At 23, the left-footed defender, comfortable in build-up and capable of defending in a high line, was supposed to become one of the pillars of the new defence. His absence forces Ouahbi to rely on players who are already in place.

Ilias Akhomach, Soufiane El Fawzi and Youssef Belammari are also weakened and being monitored by the medical staff.

Ouahbi has a big enough pool to field a competitive team against Niger, and this double confrontation can give playing time to less-used players. However, quantity does not replace the experience of Saibari, Ounahi, El Kaabi, Rahimi and Riad: this series of injuries is already upending his squad.

#1887. Celtic team-mates must step up to help out Kasper Hogh, says skipper Callum McGregor

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 14:09 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 14:16 EDT, 29 October 2026

Callum McGregor feels it’s incumbent on Kasper Hogh’s team-mates to protect him by providing the opportunities which can help end his goal drought.

The Dane provided an assist for Camilo Duran in Wednesday’s 2-2 draw with Dundee United yet was still hooked at half-time.

Since netting a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on August 9, the forward has now gone 13 matches without finding the net in a Celtic jersey.

The club’s record signing at £11million from Bodo/Glimt in the summer, Hogh looks a shadow of the player who scored freely in the Champions League for the Norwegians last season. But skipper McGregor insists the problem can only be solved if the entire squad takes responsibility for playing to their team-mate’s strengths.

‘We don’t get that much training time now with all the games, but he is working hard,’ McGregor said.

‘Obviously, he can score goals. He’s scored goals at a really high level as well, so we have to respect that.

Kasper Hogh is substituted off in the 2-1 win over Hibernian last weekend and has struggled

Celtic skipper Callum McGregor after the 2-2 draw at home to Dundee United has backed Hogh

‘It’s about trying to make the game more consistent for guys like him, the strikers, the wingers, that we can get them in the most effective areas. And listen, all strikers, they go through good spells and they go through bad spells. Sometimes you just need a goal to hit off them and then the floodgates open.

‘He’s come in with a big price tag, there’s obviously a lot of expectation, but it’s our job to protect him as well and make the game as easy as it can be for him so that he can get his goals.

‘We’re all in it together, we’re working hard with him and we back him to get goals.’

Duran’s goal should have paved the way for Celtic to extend their lead at the top of the table but Martin O’Neill’s side found themselves behind at the break when United struck through Zac Sapsford and Neil Farrugia.

While Liam Scales’ header ensured Celtic claimed the draw which maintained the status quo at the top of the Premiership, the manager admitted he was concerned that his team didn’t exert enough control on the match.

‘Yeah, I do agree with that,’ added McGregor. ‘That’s something we are trying hard to fix. What that does is bring you control in the game and there are less counter-attack moments.

‘When you get to certain areas of the pitch, of course you want to attack. But if it’s not on or there is no space, then you cap out and pass it to your mate. Then we try to recirculate the ball into a better area. That has always been the message.

‘When you get one or two new players, you have to really hone in on that. The temptation can be to do it on your own, but actually if you are giving yourself to the team, you will get goals and assists because we will get you to the right areas to go and affect the game properly. It’s something we are working hard on.’

O’Neill began the night with Callum Osmand and Duran – two centre forwards – playing on the flanks with Hogh playing through the middle.

McGregor feels the side’s up-and-down form is partly stemming from such inconsistency in shape.

Dundee United celebrate going 2-1 up at Parkhead but had to settle for a point in the end

‘I agree. You are seeing a lot of that,’ he said. ‘It’s not really having a nailed-on profile for each of the positions.

‘The players behave like a winger, or they behave like a striker. You can get away with it for a few games, but if it’s a striker playing as a winger, you are going to get that behaviour a lot of the time.

‘You’ve got enough quality so you can score goals and get away with it. But we have to try to get the team functioning the way it should. Then that will alleviate all the other problems that we are encountering, where it becomes a bit basketball, you lose control and spend the next 15 minutes trying to get possession back.’

McGregor feels it’s imperative that the side has a clear identity if it’s not to continue to struggle to put opponents to the sword.

‘For players, you want control in games as ultimately that cuts everything else down,’ he explained. ‘It’ll cut running and transitions down and that is the type of team we want to be — and have been.

‘When you have a template that you know works, you try to get as close to it as you can. That is what brings success and, at times, it has been good.

‘We have been free-flowing and scored goals. But it’s over a 60-game period. How sustainable is it really? That is the question.

‘We were getting closer to that in the second half against United and the Motherwell game. But there is a long way to go and a lot of games to play. The team will get better.’

#1886. Goalkeeper Jesus Owono in ‘profound distress and anguish’ after death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel

Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono ‘is experiencing profound distress and anguish’ after the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

De Miguel suffered head and chest injuries following a collision with Owono, who was sent off for his challenge near the halfway line, during the closing stages of the Spanish second-division match on Monday.

Owono had sprinted from his goal to clear a long ball when his knee collided with De Miguel’s chest.

De Miguel rolled on the floor immediately after impact but was then motionless on his back as several players urgently signalled for medical help.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

The 30-year-old’s condition was first described as ‘stable, given the seriousness of the condition’ on Monday night but Tenerife issued a second update in the early hours of Tuesday morning which said that his ‘medical condition has deteriorated neurologically.’

Later on Tuesday morning, Tenerife announced that De Miguel had died in hospital.

Owono initially went to leave the pitch after his red card but then turned back after the severity of De Miguel’s situation became clear.

The 25-year-old, who was playing for La Liga side Alaves last year and has made 47 appearances for Equatorial Guinea’s national team, deleted his Instagram account after receiving abuse.

According to Spanish radio station COPE, some supporters at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium shouted ‘murderer’ at Owono, while the goalkeeper is said to have been crying and praying in the dressing room after the match was abandoned.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Meanwhile, Venancio Tomas Ndong Micha, the president of the Equatorial Guinean Football Federation, has issued his ‘full solidarity and support’ to Owono.

‘It is with deep shock and immense sorrow that I have received the news of the tragic passing of your player, Jesus de Miguel. On behalf of the Equatorial Guinean Football Federation, and on my own behalf, I wish to express our most sincere and heartfelt condolences for this irreparable loss,’ Ndong Micha said in a statement.

‘Football is a family that, in moments like this, unites in grief. We wish to extend our deepest solidarity to his family, his teammates, the coaching staff, and all the blanquiazul (blue-and-white) fans, who are currently enduring a time of indescribable sadness.

‘Furthermore, I feel it is necessary to convey our full solidarity and support at this time to our player, Jesus Lazaro Owono.

‘We know that, as an involuntary participant in this fatal incident during the match, he is experiencing this situation with profound distress and anguish.

‘The Equatorial Guinean Football Federation offers him our full personal and professional support, fully aware of the severity of this event—something no one in our sport ever wishes to witness.

‘We share in your mourning and remain entirely at your disposal. Please accept our deepest respect and support during these most difficult times.’

On Tuesday, police in Spain opened an investigation for possible involuntary manslaughter following De Miguel’s death.

Judicial authorities in the Canary Islands said it is a routine procedure as any death deemed non-natural under Spanish law automatically triggers a judicial inquiry.

However, the chief prosecutor of Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui, has said it would be ‘very difficult’ for a criminal process to be opened as De Miguel’s collision with Owono occurred during the match.

Speaking to Spanish news agency EFE, Sanchez-Jauregui explained that long-standing Spanish Supreme Court precedent distinguishes injuries sustained during a match from deliberate assaults which are committed when play is halted.

Sanchez-Jauregui added that the referee’s report and the decision of the Sports Disciplinary Committee, which will determine whether Owono intended to cause harm with his challenge on De Miguel, will be considered before any legal action.

On Tuesday afternoon, the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) announced that all of its football competitions have been suspended until November 6.

#1885. Michael Carrick future: Latest Man Utd ‘plan’ becomes clear before Roma, Aston Villa games

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 12:11

Manchester United’s plan regarding the future of under-pressure head coach Michael Carrick has become clear, according to a report.

The 45-year-old remains under the spotlight at Old Trafford following a nine-game winless run across all competitions – the club’s longest streak without a victory since September 1984.

Carrick appeared to be facing the sack following Man United’s humbling 3-0 Premier League loss at home to Bournemouth, but he was given a surprise temporary reprieve, keeping him in charge for Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea.

Despite a positive start at Stamford Bridge, a second-half meltdown from the Red Devils saw Lisandro Martinez sent off either side of goals from Chelsea duo Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer.

Speculation over Carrick’s future remains rife as he sees his Man United side languishing in 17th place in the Premier League table and level on points with Crystal Palace inside the relegation zone.

With inconceivable fears of relegation growing, Man United already find themselves eight points behind Liverpool in fifth spot and a whopping 17 points adrift of champions Arsenal at the summit.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were both in attendance at Stamford Bridge and are understood to have drawn up a list of potential managerial candidates should they decide to replace Carrick.

Aston Villa’s Unai Emery, former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann – also wanted by Juventus – have all been linked with the Old Trafford hotseat.

However, The Athletic reports that Man United’s hierarchy have privately pledged to try to get to the November international break before making a final decision on Carrick’s position as head coach.

Red Devils bosses will take stock of the situation following the club’s next two matches at home against Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday and against Emery’s Aston Villa in the Premier League five days later.

While back-to-back defeats could ultimately spell the end for Carrick, two positive results and performances against Roma and Villa may buy him more time heading into the Christmas period.

“I’m just looking forward to getting the boys ready for midweek now,” Carrick told reporters following Man United’s loss at Chelsea.

“We’ve got to keep moving forward and winning games, simple as that. There’s no words that I’m going to explain to you now that makes it any different; it’s not going to change it. You can move up the league quite quickly if you win football matches.”

Man United are set to be without at least four injured players for their midweek trip to Italy, while Martinez is available to face Roma before serving a one-match domestic ban against Aston Villa.
