Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. Pellegrini has led Betis into European competitions for five consecutive seasons, which includes losing the 2025 Europa Conference League final to Chelsea. They have been busy in pre-season action already having played five games up to this point. They have won four of the five, including a 4-0 victory over Lyon, with just one defeat coming against Granada.

They have a number of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Antony, Giovani Lo Celso, Pablo Fornals and former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin. Real Betis have already played a number of friendlies as they build up to the start of their season, which begins on August 21 when they take on Real Sociedad.

#1849. Why isn't Manchester United vs Roma on TNT Sports tonight? Champions League TV schedule explained

Manchester United take on Roma tonight as they return to Champions League action at Old Trafford.

Though we are still in the early stages of the marathon league phase it is a potentially huge game for Michael Carrick, who is under severe pressure to save his job.

Saturday’s 2-0 loss at Chelsea means Man Utd have lost three on the bounce, four out of five and now gone winless in nine consecutive matches across all competitions - their worst such run since the 1988/89 season.

They have not won a single game since September 10, when their last home fixture in the Champions League saw them demolish Azerbaijani debutants Sabah FK 4-0.

It has been a total tale of woe since then both at home and on the continent, where United were brushed aside by Atletico Madrid and Como - both listless losses followed by explosive, headline-grabbing post-match interviews from senior players, first Lisandro Martinez and then captain Bruno Fernandes.

Carrick will be desperate to avoid a repeat on Tuesday night, with Roma’s visit and that of Aston Villa in the Premier League on Sunday preceding another review of his position from the club hierarchy that is expected to take place during the November international break.

However, it could be tough going against a Roma team who remain unbeaten in Serie A this season after 10 games, sitting third and four points off top spot after thrashing struggling Udinese 5-2 at the weekend.

Despite their extensive injury problems that have seen them bring a squad featuring only 17 outfield players to England, Gian Piero Gasperini’s Giallorossi are thriving following back-to-back victories and four in their last five - including a 4-0 trouncing of Slovan Bratislava in their last European outing.

Manchester United vs Roma will not be broadcast live in the UK on TNT Sports. That is because under the current Champions League rights agreement on these shores, Amazon Prime Video has the first pick of one Tuesday night fixture to show exclusively on their platform up until the semi-finals.

This week they have chosen United vs Roma, which kicks off at 8pm GMT at Old Trafford. Coverage on Amazon begins at 6:30pm, hosted by Gabby Logan.

Expert punditry comes from ex-United stalwarts Wayne Rooney, Nicky Butt and Ashley Young, with Alan Shearer on co-commentary duties alongside Jon Champion.

Amazon’s current arrangement will continue from 2027-2031 as per the terms of the next Champions League TV rights deal, which will see the bulk of matches head to US streaming giants Paramount in an agreement struck in 2025 worth well over £1billion.

Highlights will remain on the BBC, with Sky Sports buying the rights to show all Europa League and Conference League games in the UK from next season.

#1848. GdS: ‘Milanissimo’ – how Amorim outfoxed Chivu in resounding derby win

In last night’s Derby della Madonnina, AC Milan proved that Ruben Amorim has laid the foundations for a long-term project.

Considering how October had been for Milan, most arrived at the game torn about how it would go. If you offered most a draw, they’d take it on the spot. However, the squad didn’t enter the game without belief.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Opening the scoring within five minutes, it was clear they’d come to take the game to the title leaders, and the 3-1 scoreline proved it. A dominant performance, with Amorim once again starring.

Before the game, as this morning’s Gazzetta dello Sport recalled, the Portuguese stated that he was aiming to win the Scudetto, so winning last night’s game would be pivotal. So, that’s why this result feels like more than ‘just’ three points.

They’ve now not lost in eight derbies and won their last four – a first since 1972-73 – so that confidence is backed by historical statistics. A performance like that cannot be limited to numbers, though.

Diego Moreira, Adrien Rabiot, Mike Maignan and Strahinja Pavlovic were all excellent, proving why they are pillars of the team consistently.

The best performance, though, was from Amorim. As Gazzetta states, he was perfect in ‘tactics and psychology’, winning the game with his mind in both ways. He lifted the squad after their midweek defeat and innovated the tools at his disposal again.

Whilst Cristian Chivu considered numerous tactical approaches, the Portuguese was set in his 4-2-3-1. Fluid again, with different movements to counter Inter’s side – such as Sankhoun Diawara pressing to stop Djed Spence.

Chivu had to deal with issues, but he was not alone with that. In other words, a lack of options in his squad cannot be a reason for a performance like that. After all, they had one shot on target in 90 minutes and looked almost resigned despite being on top in moments.

A night of celebrations for the Rossoneri, whilst Inter saw witches, thanks to Amorim and a bit of ‘Milanissimo’.

#1847. Manchester United given Unai Emery approval amid new Michael Carrick sack decision

Manchester United have been told why Unai Emery is the clear “first-choice” manager target to replace Michael Carrick.

The current Man Utd head coach remains under significant pressure ahead of a crucial double-header against Roma, in the Champions League on Tuesday, and Emery’s Aston Villa, in the Premier League on Sunday.

According to widespread reports, Man Utd chiefs will assess Carrick’s ongoing employment following those two games, and Emery is being suggested as the perfect replacement.

Emery has established himself as one of the Premier League's outstanding coaches through his work at Aston Villa, despite operating with more restricted resources than some of his rivals.

Emery has transformed Villa into a consistent force and Richard Dunne feels Man Utd should make him their priority, even if persuading him to leave Villa Park proves difficult.

"Unai Emery has to be right at the top of the shortlist for Man United," Dunne told Snabbare.

"He's proven what he can do at Aston Villa with restricted funds, making his signings work brilliantly. The success he's had with Villa is as impressive as anyone's in the league.

"Man United should look at him as their number one target, even if it ends in rejection."

Dunne admits he would be surprised if Emery accepted an offer from Old Trafford, given the authority and control he enjoys at Villa.

However, he believes United's managerial uncertainty reflects wider problems at the club, with the ownership, recruitment strategy and executive leadership all requiring scrutiny.

United have appointed highly regarded managers and assembled squads containing outstanding individual talent, but have struggled to restore the consistency and success expected of them.

"You have to look above the pitch at the boardroom," Dunne added.

"Ownership is a long-term problem, and recruitment and executive leadership don't seem aligned. Man United have deeper problems than just the manager.”

#1846. Jesus de Miguel: Tenerife player dies in hospital one day after goalkeeper collision

CD Tenerife player Jesus De Miguel has died following an on-field collision during a match on Monday, the club has confirmed.

The incident occurred during stoppage time of a Spanish second-tier fixture as Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono rushed from his goal to challenge De Miguel for the ball.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Canary Islands club said: "Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic passing, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8::green-background[00] a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.

"There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness.

Late on Monday, Tenerife initially confirmed De Miguel had been hospitalised and was "stable despite the severity of his condition". However, an update early on Tuesday morning stated his condition had "worsened neurologically".

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

Owono was shown a red card after charging into the centre circle, where his knee appeared to connect with De Miguel’s head. Players from both sides immediately signalled for medical help and were visibly distressed before the match was suspended.

Andorra issued a statement on X reading: "With broken hearts and devastated, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, to all his teammates, friends, and to CD Tenerife. Rest in peace."

LaLiga said: "We wish to express our deep sadness over the tragic passing of Jesús de Miguel Alameda. We share in the grief of his family, his loved ones, and @CDTOficial during these very difficult times. All our affection and support. Rest in peace."

Every football match scheduled in Spain for Tuesday has been postponed by the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF), including Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina ties.

The governing body also cancelled the official presentation for Spain’s Under-21 match against Japan out of respect and solidarity with De Miguel’s family, team-mates and Tenerife supporters.

UEFA announced that a period of silence will be observed before all European games this week, with Spanish sides Atletico Madrid, Barcelona and Villarreal competing in the Champions League.

"We are heartbroken by the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin said. "We have searched for words and found only silence."

Other Spanish clubs also expressed their condolences. Barcelona said: "From FC Barcelona, we are deeply saddened by the tragic news of the passing of Jesus de Miguel, CD Tenerife player. Our thoughts and support are with his family, friends and loved ones during these difficult times."

Real Madrid said the club "wishes to express its condolences and affection to his family, his teammates, his club and all his loved ones".

#1845. After another error-strewn display and with Godfrey available again, is it time McInnes took flaky Fernandez out of the firing line?

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 15:11 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 17:10 EDT, 29 October 2026

AT the end of a chaotic night at Tynecastle, it was fitting that it should be Olwethu Makhanya who got Rangers out of jail.

With only a couple of minutes remaining, Makhanya rose at the back post to loop a header into the far corner and snatch a point for a Rangers team who had been deeply unimpressive over the 90 minutes.

Imperious pretty much from the moment he arrived from Philadelphia Union in the summer, the 22-year-old South African centre-back was once again Rangers’ best player on the night.

Even accounting for the concession of two goals, neither of which were remotely his fault, it was another performance which underscored the fact Rangers will bank a hefty profit on a player signed for just £3million.

Had it not been for Makhanya, and not just in terms of his late equaliser, Hearts would almost certainly have won the game.

As for the supporting cast around him, the performances of Manny Fernandez and Dujon Sterling came in for a lot of criticism.

It was another error-strewn display from Fernandez, which has largely been the story of his season so far, and the normally-dependable Sterling was also at fault for one of Hearts’ goals.

Fernandez has come under criticism from supporters for his performances this campaign

Derek McInnes was asked in his post-match media conference about Makhanya, a player who is emerging as the early front-runner for the PFA Scotland Player of the Year award along with Celtic’s Camilo Duran.

‘I thought he was outstanding,’ said the Rangers boss. ‘And he had to be — because we weren’t as assured around him at times.’

It hardly required the detective skills of Poirot to understand exactly who McInnes was talking about.

Fernandez was guilty on several occasions of dilly-dallying on the ball and inviting pressure from the Hearts press.

It was his mistake after only a few minutes that put Nico Raskin in trouble and ended up with the Belgian midfielder picking up a booking for a cynical foul on Claudio Braga.

Raskin turned round immediately and gave Fernandez a piece of his mind, a frustration that was no doubt shared among the Rangers support.

Fernandez was weak for both of Hearts’ goals and the same could be said of Sterling as Calvin Miller drilled home to put Hearts 2-1 up.

The defender watches on as Calvin Miller fires Hearts in front on Wednesday night

Curiously, McInnes seemed to have changed his tune slightly yesterday when he spoke to the media, issuing a passionate defence of Fernandez. But that was just a manager trying to defend a player whom he knows is taking a lot of heat at the moment.

Deep down, McInnes will surely recognise that he now has a decision on his hands with Fernandez.

With Ben Godfrey now fit again, the question of who partners Makhanya in central defence for the rest of the season is valid.

Fernandez had a spell last season where he looked dominant and assured on the ball. There was talk of a big-money move, with interest, apparently, from clubs in England and Europe.

But that has all gone quiet now. By and large, his form has been poor this season. He is too lackadaisical and too error-prone.

There are times when it looks like he makes team-mates around him nervous, which is never a good trait for a centre-back.

Too often, he looks like an accident waiting to happen. This is the risk that McInnes now has heading into tomorrow’s Premier Sports Cup semi-final clash with Aberdeen at Hampden.

The impressive Makhanya headed a late equaliser at Tynecastle as Rangers rescued a point

The longer he persists with Fernandez, the more it feels like a howler could be on the cards at any moment.

He can defend him all he wants. As manager, that’s his prerogative. But you can’t pull the wool over punters’ eyes.

They know what they are watching. On current form, it is difficult to make a case for Fernandez retaining his place in the team.

Viewing him as a sellable asset, Rangers are obviously keen to keep on playing him in order to continue his development and inflate his transfer value. But there comes a point when that becomes counter-productive. His value is not increasing at present because he is fundamentally not playing well enough.

Eventually, it will all boil down to a very simple question. Who does McInnes trust in the heat of a title race: Fernandez or Godfrey?

Godfrey is a one-time England international. For all he may have lost his way in recent years, he is still a player of good pedigree.

Given his history of injuries, the issue will be whether he can stay fit and be robust enough to partner Makhanya for the rest of the season.

McInnes certainly has a big call to make heading into the clash with an Aberdeen side who are woefully out of form.

McInnes couldn't hide his frustration with his current side on his return to Gorgie

Perhaps the biggest takeaway to come from Tynecastle on Wednesday night was Rangers’ inability to show that they can keep the pedal to the metal in the title race.

Beyond the fact they were able to salvage a point via a late equaliser, the reality was that they failed to capitalise on Celtic’s slip-up against Dundee United.

This was against a Hearts team ravaged by injuries, with eight first-team regulars out of action for Wouter Vrancken’s side.

It was actually quite damning that Makhanya spoke afterwards and questioned the mentality of those around him. He cited a ‘lack of character’ as Rangers toiled for long periods after taking an early lead through Kevin Kelsy.

Given some of the excuses trotted out by Rangers players in recent years, it was actually refreshing to hear a player speak with such honesty.

Asked about the issue yesterday, McInnes said: ‘Yeah, I got told about Makka’s comments. I think there was a period in the game where it looked as if we were second best.

‘The running stats will tell you we weren’t, but I do think that it’s too easy to point fingers at character, and that’s a word that gets bandied about here. We’ve got plenty of character.

‘We’ve shown that already this season, with character to bounce back and get a result when it looked as if we weren’t going to get that. Lads never give up.

‘There’s a real determination and sheer will about them, but at times in the game we have to acknowledge that we weren’t good enough, both technically and physically.

‘I thought we were getting outmuscled at times and not getting to the break of the ball quick enough, a bit slow to anticipate. We were more reacting to things. I thought Hearts were on the front foot a wee bit more, ready to play the way the game was playing.

‘Sometimes it can come across that way. We’re learning about these boys on the job, and the experiences of these games will hopefully help us.’

Given that he has been Rangers’ best player this season by quite some distance, Makhanya can operate from a position of authority on these matters.

He is right to question the mentality of those around him. The reality is that Rangers do not look convincing enough to go and grab the bull by the horns in this title race.

Aberdeen will present another test in the sense that it’s a game Rangers will be fully expected to win, given the current malaise around the Dons.

Can they handle the pressure? It’s a question that few Rangers fans would answer with any certainty for as long as Fernandez remains part of the equation.

#1844. Jesse Derry back at Chelsea tonight in Sporting loan twist

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Champions League football at Stamford Bridge awaits Jesse Derry this evening.

The Chelsea youngster is on loan at Sporting in Portugal this season, but is back to the Blues’ home ground in west London to face off against Shakhtar Donetsk, who are calling the Bridge their home in Europe's premier competition this season due to the ongoing conflict in the Donbas region.

Derry will be hoping to be given the chance to make an impact, with some Chelsea fans no doubt watching on among those who head to Stamford Bridge for an evening of Champions League entertainment.

It will be the first time Derry has appeared at Chelsea’s home ground since his Premier League debut in May, when he was taken to hospital midway through the game after a sickening clash of heads with Nottingham Forest’s Zach Abbott from which he has now recovered.

Derry has had to be patient so far for opportunities to show Sporting why they opted to take him on loan for the season but may have turned a corner last week.

After all of his first six appearances for the club came in the form of cameos as a substitute, he was finally handed his first start for the Lisbon giants when they faced Maritimo in the Portuguese League Cup. Derry chipped in with his first goal involvement for the club, assisting the opening goal as Sporting prevailed 2-1 on the night.

The chance is there for Derry to make his first Champions League start this evening if interim head coach Tiago Fernandes calls on him.

The 19-year-old will be hoping his 73 minutes in the tank last week can pave the way for further minutes this evening, especially after struggling to play as much as he’d have liked so far. He has played only 32 minutes (not including stoppage time) in the Portuguese League, spread across four substitute appearances.

#1843. “I stayed to help the team” – Modric explains renewal decision, derby win and title desire

Luka Modric was always going to be essential against Inter and the AC Milan veteran proved his quality at San Siro again.

In midweek, Modric was singled out by Raffaele Palladino, who felt that the game changed in Bologna’s favour with his entry to the pitch. It’s a statement that certainly feels a little strange with Modric’s experience, but it was true.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

After all, at 41, not every game is made for Modric and Ruben Amorim has to pick the right moments with him.

Nevertheless, a start against Inter meant that he was able to control the game from the first minute and set the tempo of the game, rather than trying to find a new one, which he very much did. Thanks to that, Milan claimed all three points.

Speaking at full-time to CBS Golazo, Modric explained how the team recovered after the defeat in midweek, the journey of the team and why he chose to stay, as MilanNews relays.

“An incredible victory, an incredible performance from the first minute. I think this was perhaps our best game of the season. Overall, we deserved the win and we’re really happy after the disappointing result against Bologna midweek.”

How did you recover after the defeat against Bologna?

“We have to stay positive. We can’t complain too much about the last match because we know the next one is coming. It’s an important match and there’s no better opportunity to test ourselves against Inter, and we did just that. Unfortunately, if we want to achieve something important, we can’t afford to lose games like the one in Bologna.”

“We’re growing as a team, and we’ve got new ideas. There will be ups and downs at times, but we have to try to minimise them if we want to win titles.”

What do you think of the atmosphere at San Siro?

“It was incredible. Since I arrived here, the atmosphere has always been fantastic, in every game, but especially in games like the derbies. Tonight, from the warm-up, they were incredible, and that kind of atmosphere helps you win even more.”

After the disappointment of failing to qualify for the Champions League last season, you decided to stay at Milan. Why?

“I’m happy at Milan; I feel loved and appreciated here. I spoke with the club and the new coach and I wanted to stay because I’m happy here; I love this game and I enjoy it. I stayed to help the team and the younger players grow.”

#1842. Rennes vs Olympiacos - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 02 Nov 2026 14:52

Two unbeaten sides in this season’s Europa League will meet on Wednesday as Rennes welcome Olympiacos to Roazhon Park on matchday four.

A 2-2 draw at Juventus has the Brittany club sitting 13th in the table, with Olympiacos fifth, four points above them after a 1-0 home win over Sparta Prague.

Home and away, we have seen two different sides to Rennes throughout the 2026-27 campaign in both Ligue 1 and Europe.

At Roazhon Park, Franck Haise’s men have been outstanding, unbeaten at home this season, and seeking a sixth successive triumph on home soil.

On Wednesday they can claim consecutive home victories in the group phase of this tournament for the first time since 2023.

As good as they have fared at home, consistency has not been their strong suit of late, with Rennes only winning consecutive competitive outings once since September.

Defensively, they have conceded 11 goals in their last four competitive fixtures combined, including a 5-2 loss to Nice in Ligue 1 this past weekend.

On the other hand, Les Rouges et Noir have a 100% record versus Greek opposition in the Europa League, conceding just one goal in each of those contests.

As tough as it was to miss out on this season’s Champions League, Olympiacos have come a long way since NEC Nijmegen came from behind to beat them 2-1 on aggregate.

This team have lost just one of their last 15 competitive fixtures, while winning nine in a row heading into Thursday.

Imanol Alguacil’s men have won their last five away matches across all competitions, with their 2-1 loss to NEC in a Champions League qualifier being their only defeat as the visitors this season.

Olympiacos are one of five teams with a 100% record in the League Phase of this tournament heading into matchday four, while they are unbeaten in their last 10 Europa League group games.

Since losing 3-1 at AC Milan in 2018, they have not lost an away match in the League Phase of this competition when netting first.

The Greeks have lost three of their four Europa League meetings against French opposition, though their last visit to France in this competition saw them blank Marseille 1-0 at Stade Velodrome on matchday two.

Ligue 1 top scorer Esteban Lepaul is unlikely to play on Wednesday as he recovers from an ankle sprain, while first-choice goalkeeper Brice Samba is questionable with a leg injury.

Musa Al-Taamari and Boulaye Dia scored first-half goals at Juventus on matchday three, the first for both players in this competition.

On the other side, Olympiacos will likely be without Kostas Fortounis because of an injury, while Yusuf Yazici, an ex-Ligue 1 player at Lille, is out with a cruciate ligament tear, as is Ayoub El Kaabi, who has a broken tibia.

Armando Gonzalez netted his team-leading second goal in the Europa League on matchday three, and Stefan Ortega needed to only one stop for his second clean sheet of the tournament.

Lemaitre; Ait Boudlal, Cresswell, Rouault; Reynolds, Cisse, Rongier, Camara, Thomasson; Al-Taamari, Mayenda

Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Pirola, Onyemaechi; Freuler, Hezze; Martins, Chinquinho, Silva; Gonzalez

At home, Rennes are much more compact and solid defensively, and we trust they will find a way through a well-structured Olympiacos side that tend to play quite passively away from home.

#1841. Arsenal pay touching tribute to Jesus de Miguel after tragic death

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal paid tribute to Jesus de Miguel after the 30-year-old died from injuries suffered in a Spanish second-division match.

The Tenerife striker had serious injuries to his head and chest after colliding with goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a game against FC Andorra on Monday.

Owono's knee collided heavily with De Miguel, who was treated on the pitch for more than five minutes before being taken by ambulance to hospital.

His condition was said to be "stable despite the severity of his condition" on Monday, however that deteriorated and De Miguel died on Tuesday morning.

Tributes have been paid to De Miguel across the game, including from Kylian Mbappe and Gerard Pique, who co-owns Andorra.

Arsenal responded to the tragic news themselves as players and staff gathered at the start of their training session on Tuesday morning.

The Gunners huddled in a circle and observed a period of silence in front of a big screen with a picture of De Miguel on.

The Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) has postponed all matches scheduled for Tuesday.

UEFA announced that a period of silence take place before every European games this week, which will include matches involving Spanish sides Atletico Madrid, Barcelona and Villarreal.

"We are heartbroken by the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin ‌said. "We have searched for words and found only silence."

In a statement announcing De Miguel's death, Tenerife said: "Racked with pain, with ‌a lump in our throats and unable to ​believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic ​passing of Jesus de ⁠Miguel Alameda.

"There are no words of comfort; there is ‌absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness."

#1840. Surprise! Mikel Arteta reunited with former Arsenal striker before Champions League clash

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Yaya Sanogo paid a surprise visit to Arsenal ahead of their Champions League fixture against Slavia Prague.

The Frenchman, who was a team-mate of Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta from 2013 to 2016, was spotted at London Colney on Tuesday morning as the squad were put through their paces during training.

It is not clear as to why Sanogo was present at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, but he was able to catch up with Arteta prior to the Spaniard going to oversee preparations for the Champions League clash.

The session in question also saw the return of Sanogo’s compatriot William Saliba as he stepped up his rehabilitation from a back injury that sidelined him since the World Cup semi-final in July.

Sanogo spent four years at Arsenal upon joining from Auxerre on a free transfer as he caught Arsene Wenger’s eye, at the time, after scoring seven goals in the same week.

“For all the problems I’d had, the phone wouldn’t ring for two years," Sanogo recalled when speaking to Masterclass media. "But after my seven goals in two games, Arsene Wenger calls me.

“I had a little Motorola, I promise you I had that phone. I was at home using my Macbook and I saw +44. I’m thinking ‘What is this number?’ So I don’t answer, but he called again.

“I say ‘Hello’. ‘Hello, it’s Arsene Wenger’. I thought it was a joke.

“I say ‘Yes?’ ‘It’s Yaya Sanogo?’ I say ‘Yes’. And I don’t speak.

“He tells me ‘Everybody is talking about you, seven goals in one week, not many players have done it’. And I told him ‘Yes, thank you, that’s nice’. But I didn’t know what to say.

“He told me ‘I see you are shy. I’m getting my plane and I want to meet you. I don’t know if you care, I know there’s a lot of clubs that want you, especially after the week you had. Would you be interested to meet me in Paris?’

“I said ‘Yes’ but I don’t realise. I think it’s amazing. He asked me when it’s OK to come to Paris and he hung up.

“I’m saying ‘Wait, wait, it was really Wenger?’ I had two years of problems. Six, seven games [later], Wenger calls me. I’ll sign right now.”

Ultimately, Sanogo was not able to forge a successful career at Arsenal as his only goal for the club came in a 2-0 Champions League group stage win over Borussia Dortmund in November 2014.

#1839. Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

Stepping up in the big moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR

Unai Emery’s men head home from the Far East to face PSG in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg next week and then have one more pre-season friendly against Borussia Monchengladbach before starting their Premier League campaign at Brighton.

Possession: Aston Villa 44%-56% Bayern MunichShots: 8-16Shots on target: 3-8Corners: 3-7

Bizot nearly has a calamitous moment coming out of his penalty area but gets away with it.

The final whistle is blown soon after and Bayern hold on to beat Villa 2-1 in Hong Kong. They had looked comfortable when Diaz put them 2-0 up but Villa kept going until the end.

Victory in the final match of the #AudiFCBTour! 💪🔥 pic.twitter.com/UFhQhme62i

The space opens up for Palhinha to shoot from range but Bizot makes a fairly comfortable save down to his right.

It was all Bayern for 80 minutes of this game but Villa have come to life in the closing stages, with Vincent Kompany’s side now holding on a bit.

When Diaz scored Bayern’s second goal, Aston Villa were out of this game but it has been all Villa since then. They look the more likely to get a goal.

Gomes’ free-kick out on the left is parried behind by Neuer for a Villa corner on the right. The corner comes to nothing.

For 80 minutes, Aston Villa barely looked like scoring but come so close to getting two goals in just a few minutes. Abraham meets a cross from the right and must think he has scored but his header is brilliantly saved by the 40-year-old Neuer.

Maybe this game is not quite done and dusted yet. A cross from the right picks out Gomes on the edge of the box. The Brazilian takes one touch before toe poking past Neuer and into the Bayern net. Gomes meant that finish and Villa have some hope.

Abraham should have done better there. He has the space to drive down Villa’s right and has a decision to make; cross the ball to his left and drive forward himself to shoot. He takes a while to make the decision before his attempted cross is intercepted by Ito.

Boey’s yellow card was his final act of the game as he is replaced by Della Rovere. Boey did seem to be struggling with some cramp.

Bayern receive their second yellow card of the game as Boey is booked for cynically pulling down Lynch.

Cash, Maatsen and Buendia have gone off for Aston Villa.

Double substitution from Bayern as Pavic and Assomo replace Tah and Brown.

A fantastic goal to put the Germans 2-0 up and it is nothing more than they deserve. Ibrahimovic finds Diaz in space on the left and the Colombian drives at Cash. As he enters the Villa box, Diaz cuts inside onto his preferred right foot and smashes a shot towards goal. It appeared to go right over Bizot, who opts not to put a hand up. The ball crashes off the underside of the bar and goes in. It has been all Bayern in this second half and that goal had been coming.

Bayern are knocking on the door and come very close to doubling their lead. Diaz’s shot from the edge of the box looks destined to hit the net with Bizot beaten but fortunately for Villa Abraham is on hand on his own goal line to make the block.

Bizot makes another great save. Bayern win a free-kick out on the right after Brown was fouled. Bischoff opts to shoot instead of crossing and nearly beats Bizot at his near post but the Aston Villa keeper gets across to his left to make the save.

Unai Emery makes a double substitution as Mings and Lynch replace Torres and Guessand. Mings takes the captain’s armband.

That is a fantastic double save from Bizot, first denying Stanisic and then Ibrahimovic. Both of those shots came through bodies so Bizot did a good job of reacting and making the saves with his legs on both occasions.

It is safe to say the Bayern fans out in Hong Kong love Diaz, who is cheered every time he touches the ball.

Vincent Kompany is going to make a triple change as Ito, Diaz and Palhinha come on. Former Liverpool man Diaz received a great ovation from the fans in Hong Kong. Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenha, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa in this window.

Should Bayern have been awarded a penalty there? A ball is played in behind the Villa defence into the penalty area and Ibrahimovic appeared to be brought down but the referee waves those appeals away. On first viewing, that appeared to be a penalty.

Just before the hour mark, it is time for some changes from Aston Villa. Abraham and Bogarde come on for Madjo and Kamara. This is Abraham’s first appearance of this pre-season.

Good play from Gomes earns Aston Villa a free-kick not far outside the Bayern penalty area out on the left, in a similar position to the free-kick that Bayern scored from in the first half. Buendia clips in a good ball to the back post, where Guessand looks likely to score but instead misses the ball on the stretch. Should Guessand have done better with that? Probably.

Brown was starting in his customary left-back position for Bayern in the first half but is now operating out on the right wing.

Gomes leaves one late on Pavlovic and, had this been a competitive fixture, I suspect that might have been a yellow card.

Tah is brought down by Gomes and Bayern will have a free-kick out on the right not a million miles outside the Villa penalty area. The delivery though is poor and easily cleared away.

Bayern have brought Stanisic on at half-time for Laimer. Aston Villa have not made a change at the break.

Possession: Aston Villa 45%-55% Bayern MunichShots: 4-7Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 1-2

The first half in Hong Kong is brought to an end and Bayern take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Kim’s goal.

There will be one added minute at the end of this first half.

Aston Villa have struggled to create much going forward and have not really had a genuine goal-scoring opportunity in this first half. Their forward line though will look quite different when they kick off the seaosn than it does today.

The German side take the lead in Hong Kong. Bischof’s left-footed delivery from a free-kick out on the left is sublime, whipping it right into the corridor of uncertainty. The quality of delivery means it is quite a simple header for Kim, who makes no mistake with his header into the far corner. Kim might have been offside but obviously there is no VAR in use today. 1-0 Bayern.

That is a waste in the end from Bayern. Boey fires a pass in-field into Laimer, who takes a fantastic first touch on the turn inside the Villa half. He drives through the Villa half and at the penalty area but his pass outside looking for Cardozo is poor and overhit, with the ball rolling out for a goal kick. Laimer will be annoyed at himself having done all the hard work and then failed to execute the easy part.

Bischof eyes one up from range and tries to pick out the top corner. Bizot is routed to his spot and is hoping the shot goes wide. Bischof’s effort is always curling wide, much to Bizot’s relief.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Bayern Munich. Guessand drives forward into the Bayern half and is brought down by a cynical foul from Cardozo. You were half expecting Cardozo to perhaps escape without a booking with it being a pre-season friendly but he does not. It was the right call to book him.

That was lovely from Pavlovic. The German midfielder shows good feet to beat Gomes before getting his shot away from a central position just outside the box. He forces Bizot into a decent save but one he should be making.

Bayern force Villa into an error and win themselves a corner as a result out on the left. It is delivered into a dangerous area at the front post but Villa do a good job of handling it and clearing their lines.

Bayern Munich have made two signings this summer; Brown from Bundesliga rivals Frankfurt and Saibari from PSV. Brown is starting at left-back for Bayern today with Saibari not involved as he closes in on a return from a knock picked up at the World Cup with Morocco. Brown feels like such a Bayern signing, nabbing a good player from a Bundesliga rival.

Aston Villa have made four signings so far this summer but just one is in their starting XI today in the form of Gomes, who joined from Midlands rivals Wolves this summer. Young Swiss midfielder Manzambi has joined from Freiburg but is currently out injured. Garnacho picked up a knock and Cisse, who has arrived from LASK, is not involved for Villa today.

The ball is played in behind the Aston Villa defence to pick out the run of Binder. On the edge of the Villa box, Binder gets the first touch but Lindelof is calm in defence and heads back to his keeper Bizot.

Moments later, Gomes is dispossessed inside his own half and Ibrahimovic has a shot from just outside the box but drags it wide of the far post.

Good work from 17-year-old Madjo down Aston Villa’s left wins them their first corner of the game. Buendia’s inswinger is headed away too easily at the near post. Aston Villa have seen their former set-piece coach Austin MacPhee nabbed this summer by Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea.

The referee is allowing the game to flow and thus not blowing for soft fouls.

The first chance of the game falls to Bayern Munich. Brown’s cross from the left is headed by Maatsen straight to Ibrahimovic on the edge of the box. Ibrahimovic, not any relation to Zlatan, takes the shot on first time but it is blocked by Maatsen, who makes up for that poor header with the block. The ball goes behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.

Interestingly, there are only eight outfield substitutions on the Aston Villa bench for this game, with the likes of Garnacho and McGinn picking up knocks the other day. It appears then that at least a couple of Villa outfield players will have to play the full 90.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, Aston Villa led out by Matty Cash and Bayern Munich by Manuel Neuer, and we are closing in on kick-off in Hong Kong. A group of delegates shake the hands of both starting XIs.

Chelsea and Juventus played in this stadium the other night and it is safe to say that the pitch does not look in the best state ahead of kick-off today. It looks like it will continue to rip up and the last thing the two managers will want is to pick up any serious injuries.

Currently, before the two sides emerge, the crowd in Hong Kong are being treated to some pre-match dancing and entertainment, which includes people dressed as pandas and sharks dancing. Would the Premier League ever take inspiration and have dancing pandas before kick-off?

Aston Villa: Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Kamara, Joao Gomes, Hemmings, Buendia, Guessand, Madjo.Substitutes: Wright, Asemota, Mings, Abraham, Nedejkovic, Bogarde, Rowe, Burrowes, Carroll, Lynch.

Bayern Munich: Neuer, Kim, Tah, Brown, Boey, Laimer, Bischof, Pavlovic, Ibrahimovic, Binder, Cardozo. Substitutes: Ulrich, Podar-Stiube, Urbig, Kimmich, Luis Díaz, Palhinha, Ito, Chávez, Pavic, Bara, Manuba, Stanisic, Della Rovere, Assomo.

The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return to training after their World Cup exploits and Aston Villa are also without captain John McGinn and new signing Alejandro Garnacho, who picked up knocks in their win over BG Pathum the other day.

Aston Villa have already sold Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers this summer, with Lucas Digne on the verge of a move to PSG, but could another starter be on the way out of Villa Park? England defender Ezri Konsa has been linked with moves to the likes of Arsenal and Liverpool but will Unai Emery be able to keep hold of the 28-year-old?

The atmosphere is building with our fans in Hong Kong! 🔴⚪️#AudiFCBTour pic.twitter.com/m4fFXAWxGb

It has been a big summer of change at Aston Villa already and there could be more changes before the end of the window. Left-back Lucas Digne is set to move to PSG and is set to be replaced by Atlético Madrid’s Matteo Ruggeri. Joao Palhinha, who is on the bench for Bayern Munich today, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa.

“Aston Villa are a top side with a very good coach. They have a large squad and will field plenty of talent. They have already played more friendlies than us, but for us it is a good challenge. It is a match in which we will learn a lot about our team’s fitness. It will be a good match for us.”

“It is difficult to improve; after all, it is not just about the trophies we have won, but also about the number of goals and matches we have won. It is possible, but difficult. Right now, I would say our aim is to win the Champions League; there is no doubt about that. And throughout the season, I will be saying that we need to focus on the next match. To achieve that; to win the Bundesliga, the cup and the Champions League, we need the whole squad to be fit and healthy. We need to make good use of them and improve the squad. We have already done that, but hopefully it will help us achieve our goals.”

Aston Villa’s preparations for the new season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

After losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East. It has been a summer of significant change at Aston Villa thus far with some key members of their squad departing and some new faces arriving. Youri Tielemans has departed after Manchester United triggered his release clause and they then sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a British transfer record £117m. Unai Emery’s side have brought in 20-year-old Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho, with the deal for Garnacho being an initial loan. Manzambi is currently on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

Unai Emery’s side were dealt a blow during the World Cup as Belgian midfielder Amadou Onana picked up a serious knee injury. They were though boosted by the return of Boubacar Kamara after seven months out as he scored in the 3-1 friendly victory over BG Parthum. As one midfielder returned from injury in that game, another picked up a fresh injury as John McGinn suffered a knock to his knee. The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return after their world Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with an away game on the south coast against Brighton on August 23 but will be involved in the Uefa Super Cup against PSG next week having lifted the Europa League last season.

Bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer. The likes of Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are not available as they are still yet to return after World Cup duty but Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Bayern’s German stars are set to return.

After today, Bayern have one more friendly against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

#1838. Musah happy with Milan rejuvenation after ‘most beautiful night’: “The fans are incredible”

In the summer, it seemed Yunus Musah was a player on the move, but Ruben Amorim opted to keep him, a decision AC Milan are overjoyed with.

Last summer, it seemed Musah was heading to a permanent exit. Atalanta pursued him all summer and there was interest from across Europe. However, that wasn’t seen as a bad thing by most.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

So, when La Dea opted against signing him permanently in the summer, most expected the same outcome: a departure. Yet, Amorim opted to keep him and that decision has paid off substantially.

The American has become a core part of the team, and has definitely rejuvenated his career. Indeed, he is beginning to look like the player the Rossoneri hoped he’d become when they signed the youngster from Spain.

Speaking at full-time to Sky Sport 24, the midfielder looked back on his recent rise and admitted that the work was not yet done, as MilanNews relays.

Is it the most beautiful night of the year?

“Yes, it’s definitely been the best night of the year so far. We know that in derbies, when you win, especially at home, the stadium is incredible, the fans are incredible. We learn from every match: we learned from Bologna and we’ll try not to make the same mistakes moving forward.

Today you walked out to a standing ovation: has everything turned upside down?

“I’m happy with the current situation, but football has a short memory and I have to continue like this until the end of the season; otherwise, I know things can change again immediately and here you have to play well every game because there’s always someone who wants your place, you’re at Milan.”

Did you test Rabiot’s goal: was the ball a cross or a shot?

“It was a corner we set up, which we knew Inter wouldn’t pursue. Adrien, no, in my opinion, wanted to put the ball there to create danger, put it there and hope someone would be there. But no, honestly no, I don’t think he meant to shoot.”

#1837. Man City XI vs RB Leipzig: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup, injury latest for Champions League

Manchester City have no fresh injury concerns ahead of their Champions League clash against RB Leipzig.

Antoine Semenyo is Man City’s one long-term absentee after suffering a knee injury in the win over Ipswich last month, keeping him out of the last four matches in all competitions as a result.

The Ghana international, along with youngsters Ryan McAidoo and Kaden Braithwaite, was not spotted on Tuesday’s training session before flying out to Germany, but Enzo Maresca still has a near fully-fit squad to choose from.

There is, however, a decision to make in goal as Gianluigi Donnarumma has looked shaky in recent weeks and the City boss has made it clear the Italian is not a guaranteed starter.

“I think it is one thing to say that in this moment it is Gigio plus 10, and another thing to say undroppable,” Maresca said before the loss to Brighton in the Premier League.

“They are two different things. There is no player that is undroppable but in this moment it is Gigio plus 10. In this moment I see it like this.”

Geronimo Rulli staked his claim for a start with an impressive display in the Carabao Cup win over Brighton but may have to settle for a place on the bench again.

Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly are pushing for returns after dropping down to the bench at the weekend, while Ayyoub Bouaddi could be rested after starting the last two games.

Phil Foden is highly likely to start as he has been chosen for pre-match press conference duties, though he might be asked to operate from the right-hand side as Rayan Cherki is recalled in the No10 role behind Erling Haaland.

Predicted Man City XI: Donnarumma; Nunes, Khusanov, Guehi, O’Reilly; Anderson, Fernandez; Foden, Cherki, Doku; Haaland

Time and date: 8pm GMT on Wednesday, November 4, 2026

#1836. Why West Ham fans should welcome - and be wary of - Scott Parker appointment

Scott Parker is the frontrunner to succeed Nuno Espirito Santo, who was sacked as West Ham head coach on Tuesday morning with the club’s promotion hopes hanging in the balance.

West Ham were widely considered favourites to bounce straight back to the Premier League this season, but after six wins from their first 13 Championship games, they are down in eighth place.

Having recorded a £104.2million loss in the last financial year, the club are acutely aware of the financial imperative of returning to the top flight at the first opportunity and have moved swiftly to make a change in the dugout following successive home defeats to Southampton and West Brom.

Parker, a club legend who won three successive Player of the Year awards during a four-year stint in east London, is seen as someone who can not only get supporters back onside but has experience getting teams promoted from the Championship.

The 46-year-old has earned promotion to the Premier League on three separate occasions across spells with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley, but his success has not come without criticism.

His time at Fulham, who offered him his first senior managerial role in May 2019, was dominated by tensions with the board, and Parker openly criticised the club’s long-term structure and recruitment.

West Ham agree new manager appointment after Nuno sacking

West Ham confirm Nuno Espirito Santo sack decision as statement issued

Nuno under pressure as West Ham sent tumbling down Championship table

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

Despite taking Fulham up from the Championship, Parker then struggled to build a competitive Premier League side and presided over a dispiriting relegation campaign, with his pragmatic style of play proving increasingly unpopular with supporters.

Parker left Fulham by mutual consent after their relegation in 2021 before swiftly taking charge at Bournemouth. While not direct rivals, the move left a bitter taste for some, with Bournemouth in direct competition with Fulham for promotion from the Championship.

Both teams went up automatically during the 2021/22 season. But while Fulham were able to stabilise under the guidance of Marco Silva, similar issues reared their head for Parker, and he was sacked four games into the season after questioning the direction and commitment of the club following a 9-0 defeat to Liverpool.

Parker’s comments, in which he said his team were "ill-equipped at this level", led Bournemouth’s then-owner Maxim Demin to hit back, stating that for the club to progress, everyone must “show belief in and respect for one another.”

Scott Parker is a manager with pedigree at this level but also plenty of baggage

West Ham will be aware of Parker’s history, including an ill-fated 67-day spell at Belgian side Club Brugge, and they will have made it clear during negotiations that he must secure promotion to secure his future.

After a toxic end to Nuno’s tenure, there will be a fair amount of goodwill for the former England international given his cult status at the club and his knowledge of the league.

The Championship is relentless, though, and results need to change quickly if West Ham are to keep pace with the top of the table and stop the chasing pack from gaining encouragement.

In Parker, West Ham believe they have a safe pair of hands who knows the club and knows how to get out of the Championship. Supporters are, however, bound to be more sceptical.

Parker’s vision for West Ham will almost certainly be built on defensive solidity, and with good reason. West Ham have conceded 18 goals in 13 league games this season, a rate of 1.4 goals per game.

Given the quality of the squad at his disposal, though, there will also be an expectation to entertain. West Ham, for all their struggles, have at times blown teams away this season, scoring in every game this term.

Parker is a manager with pedigree at this level but also plenty of baggage. West Ham can’t say they have not been warned.

#1835. William Saliba: Arsenal handed huge injury boost as defender returns to training

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

William Saliba handed Arsenal a huge boost by taking part in the final training session before the Champions League match against Slavia Prague.

The Frenchman has not played a single minute since he limped off after half an hour of France's World Cup semi-final against Spain.

Saliba was sent to see specialists on that back injury and while it was decided that surgery was not necessary, an extended period of rest has been required.

His recovery has gone well and Saliba has been back on the grass in recent weeks, going through individual training drills.

That has now been stepped up significantly, with Saliba understood to have to been back in first-team training on Monday.

The 25-year-old came through that without any issues and he was involved again on Tuesday morning, as the Arsenal squad trained in front of the media.

Mikel Arteta and his players will fly out to Prague later in the day ahead of facing Slavia Prague on Wednesday night.

It remains to be seen whether Saliba is included in that travelling squad, with Arsenal understandably cautious over his return to action.

The Gunners face Hull on Saturday before then having two weeks off for the November international break, allowing Saliba further time on the training pitch to build his fitness.

Saliba's return will leave Arteta with a serious selection headache heading into another hectic period.

Ezri Konsa, signed in the summer to cover for Saliba's absence, has been superb alongside Gabriel and probably Arsenal's best player so far this season.

The England international's strong form will allow Arsenal to ease Saliba back into action without taking significant risks with his fitness.

#1834. Big game players, big game performances: Player ratings for Milan-Inter from Italian papers

Last night’s win against Inter was proof of the quality within the AC Milan squad, so now it’s a case of continuing on the path upwards.

For Milan, a win in the derby wasn’t essential. Yes, it would always be a big help, but avoiding defeat was the priority, given a 10-point gap would’ve opened to the title leaders. Yet, the Rossoneri were brave and fought for three points, even if most would’ve taken one.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A defining performance of the Ruben Amorim era so far, everyone played their role stupendously – and that includes the Portuguese, who tactically outclassed his counterpart. As a result, the scores from us were rather high in our post-match ratings.

Looking at the ratings from elsewhere, Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) gave the performance an eight, also giving Amorim that score, too.

In terms of the players’ performances, Goncalo Ramos was the lowest, with a still passable score of a 6. However, Ardon Jashari and Davide Bartesaghi were also given these scores, understandable after coming off the bench.

With 6.5s, Koni De Winter, Yunus Musah and Alphadjo Cisse were all very solid, with the latter almost grabbing a fourth in the game. Mario Gila, Strahinja Pavlovic and Sankhoun Diawara were given 7s, as did Luka Modric and the first goalscorer Christian Pulisic.

The Diavolo’s French duo – Mike Maignan and Adrien Rabiot – were awarded a score of 7.5, whilst Diego Moreira was given an eight for his goal and two assists.

Moving to Corriere dello Sport, Amorim was given an eight again. Ramos scored the lowest again, at a six, whilst Musah, Diawara, Pavlovic and De Winter were given 6.5. Gila, Modric, Pulisic and Rabiot were given 7s. Then, Maignan was given a 7.5, Moreira, again, was given an 8/10.

Finally, Tuttosport’s ratings were largely the same. Ramos was given a downgrade to a 5/10, whilst Moreira was given another eight. The French goalkeeper kept his second-best position with a 7.5 – alongside Rabiot – thanks to his big saves, whilst Diawara was also given a bump up to a 7, thanks to an impressive derby debut.

Elsewhere, Gila, De Winter, Pavlovic, Musah and Pulisic were given 6.5s, Modric played a 7/10 game and Amorim was given a 7.5.

#1833. Chelsea's rivals eyeing unused Estevao - plus the reason Xabi Alonso is snubbing Brazilian, why other clubs believe Blues will win race for £90m Alex Scott and the Como wonderkid on radar: CHELSEA CONFIDENTIAL

Published: 08:00 EDT, 29 October 2026 | Updated: 18:06 EDT, 29 October 2026

Multiple Premier League and European rivals of Chelsea are watching the club's handling of Estevao Willian with intrigue after the Brazilian wonderkid again went unused under Xabi Alonso.

Despite Cole Palmer’s suspension and Joao Pedro’s injury, Estevao was overlooked during Wednesday’s Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool. The 19-year-old stayed sat on the bench at Anfield while four others were introduced during the 1-1 draw preceding the penalty shootout.

In Chelsea’s eight Premier League fixtures, he has been brought on as a late substitute six times and unused twice.

Estevao is tied down to a contract lasting into the 2030s with Chelsea, who consider him among their ‘untouchables’ and have looked at trying to arrange a new deal. But external sources have confided that his situation is piquing interest within Premier League and European circles.

It is understood Estevao's limited role under Alonso is not the result of a fall-out, and purely down to tactical and technical decisions. Chelsea’s manager has hinted that the physicality of the Premier League is a contributing factor while promising greater chances as the season progresses.

Alonso does not see Estevao as suited to a wing-back role, which involves a great deal of tracking back, but as a winger who can come inside, as Palmer does in the 3-4-2-1 system.

Estevao was an unused substitute during Chelsea's Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool and his lack of minutes is piquing the interest of rivals clubs in the Premier League and across Europe

In Chelsea’s eight Premier League fixtures, the Brazilian has been brought on as a late substitute six times and unused twice

Chelsea fans hope they will soon see more of Estevao in action – the away end at Anfield were singing his name on Wednesday while he went unused. But Palmer will be back available when Manchester United visit Stamford Bridge in the Premier League this Saturday lunchtime after serving his one-game ban.

Carlo Ancelotti has named him in his Brazil squad for their November friendlies against Japan and Singapore. Estevao has started as many matches for his country in their one international break as he has for Chelsea in all competitions this season.

Ancelotti said during the last break that he would overlook his lack of minutes with Chelsea because he considers it his duty to aid his development. The Sao Paulo native has six goals in 14 Brazil caps.

Chelsea are continuing to keep tabs on Jacobo Ramon, the 21-year-old defender of Como who is impressing under Cesc Fabregas, though they are joined by others across England and Europe.

Arsenal and Manchester United have also been linked with Ramon. His situation is likewise complicated by Real Madrid retaining a 50 per cent sell-on clause in any deal for the Spain Under 21s centre back, as well as an unspecified buy-back clause.

Ramon played under Alonso way back in 2018-19, when the now-Chelsea manager began his coaching career within Madrid’s youth system.

Chelsea’s interest predates Alonso’s arrival and goes back to last January, when they had Ramon on a shortlist along with Jeremy Jacquet – then of Rennes, now of Liverpool – and Marcos Senesi – then of Bournemouth, now of Tottenham.

Chelsea focused on trying to sign Jacquet, but he chose Liverpool, signing a pre-agreement to join them in the summer for £60million. He came on as a substitute in Wednesday’s Carabao Cup clash, replacing Virgil van Dijk.

Chelsea are continuing to keep tabs on 21-year-old Como defender Jacobo Ramon (left), but face competition from various rivals

Sources at rival clubs believe Chelsea will end up winning the race to Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, with it possible that an agreement could be reached before the January window.

The word is a fee of around £90m would be expected to be enough, despite Bournemouth saying they want £100m-plus.

In a way, the improving results of Marco Rose’s side are helping expedite Scott's exit, as they insist any winter sale would be blocked if their Premier League position were precarious. Scott is injured and Bournemouth have won five consecutive games in all competitions without him.

While Liverpool have looked at Scott, they are not said to have shown as much interest as Chelsea, and there are some suspicions that Bournemouth would like a bidding war for a 23-year-old midfielder who has indicated his interest in moving on.

Monaco’s Lamine Camara, who Chelsea came close to signing for half the price of Scott at £47m in the summer, also has his fans at Liverpool.

Chelsea's rivals believe the Blues will win the race to sign Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott

October 24, 2021: Manchester United lose 5-0 at home to Liverpool.

October 25-26: Ole Gunnar Solskjaer appears on the brink of losing his job.

October 27: Solskjaer surprisingly avoids the sack.

October 30: United head to London and win 3-0 away at Tottenham.

Chelsea are aiming to avoid history repeating itself when Michael Carrick's side visit Stamford Bridge this Saturday after a week in which United were beaten by Bournemouth but the boss avoided the axe.

Chelsea are expecting United captain Bruno Fernandes to return to their starting line-up after his clear-the-air talks with Carrick.

Romeo Lavia completed his first full 90 minutes in a competitive match for Chelsea against Liverpool, which can only be good for his confidence levels.

Alonso identified that as an issue in pre-season, when he allowed the 22-year-old midfielder to complete the match in a friendly win over AC Milan. Chelsea’s manager told those of us on the tour that he wanted to give Lavia that moment because he believed he had a ‘mental block’ about it after his injury history.

Romeo Lavia completed his first full 90 minutes in a competitive match for Chelsea against Liverpool on Wednesday night

This week, a group of Chelsea first-teamers and promising academy players got together in a meeting room at Cobham for a talk from a specialist brought in to discuss career-ending insurance.

While a dry topic, it is an important consideration for footballers in this unpredictable game.

Speaking of injuries, Chelsea have had an unfortunate run of muscle issues of late, with Maxence Lacroix struggling to walk off the pitch at Anfield after picking up a hamstring problem.

Chelsea are searching for a physical performance coach to join their first-team support staff. Within the job listing, they say they want someone who can ‘lead on GK specific physical development’.
